+/-! ### Average-case hardness definitions
+([Liu and Pass, Definitions 2.4 and 2.5, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]) -/
+
+/-- **[Liu and Pass, Definition 2.4, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]:
+Mildly hard on average (`MildlyHardOnAverage`).**
+A function $f : \{0, 1\}^* \to \mathbb{N}$ is mildly hard on average if there exists a positive
+polynomial $p$ such that for every uniform strict PPT heuristic
+$\mathcal{H} : \{0, 1\}^* \to \mathrm{ProbComp}\ \mathbb{N}$, for all sufficiently large
+$n \in \mathbb{N}$,
+$$\Pr_{x \leftarrow \{0, 1\}^n, v \leftarrow \mathcal{H}(x)}[v = f(x)] \le 1 - \frac{1}{p(n)}.$$ -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverage (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ProbComp ℕ, IsPPTOn encBits encNat H →
+      ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
+        (((BitString.uniformList n).bind fun x =>
+          (ProbComp.eval (H x)).map fun v => decide (v = f x)) true).toReal ≤
+          1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ)
+
+/-- **[Liu and Pass, Definition 2.5, §2.3, p. 8 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]:
+Mildly hard on average to $g$-approximate (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`).**
+A function $f : \{0, 1\}^* \to \mathbb{N}$ is mildly hard on average to $g$-approximate if there
+exists a positive polynomial $p$ such that for every uniform strict PPT heuristic
+$\mathcal{H} : \{0, 1\}^* \to \mathrm{ProbComp}\ \mathbb{N}$, for all sufficiently large
+$n \in \mathbb{N}$,
+$$\Pr_{x \leftarrow \{0, 1\}^n, v \leftarrow \mathcal{H}(x)}[|v - f(x)| \le g(n)]
+  \le 1 - \frac{1}{p(n)},$$
+where $|v - f(x)|$ is formalized on $\mathbb{N}$ by the symmetric distance `Nat.dist v (f x)`. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox (g : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ProbComp ℕ, IsPPTOn encBits encNat H →
+      ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
+        (((BitString.uniformList n).bind fun x =>
+          (ProbComp.eval (H x)).map fun v =>
+            decide (Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g n)) true).toReal ≤
+          1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ)
+
+/-- **Library helper (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox`):** one-sided underestimation
+approximation hardness against uniform strict PPT heuristics, requiring
+$$\Pr_{x \leftarrow \{0, 1\}^n, v \leftarrow \mathcal{H}(x)}[f(x) - g(n) \le v \le f(x)]
+  \le 1 - \frac{1}{p(n)}$$
+for all sufficiently large $n$. By
+`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`, one-sided
+$(2 g)$-approximation hardness implies symmetric $g$-approximation hardness
+(`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g f`) whenever `fun x => g x.length` is computable in polynomial time
+by shifting any heuristic output down by $g(|x|)$. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox (g : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ProbComp ℕ, IsPPTOn encBits encNat H →
+      ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
+        (((BitString.uniformList n).bind fun x =>
+          (ProbComp.eval (H x)).map fun v =>
+            decide (f x - g n ≤ v ∧ v ≤ f x)) true).toReal ≤
+          1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ)
+
+/-- **Library specialization (`MildlyHardOnAverageDet`):** deterministic polynomial-time heuristic
+specialization of `MildlyHardOnAverage`. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageDet (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ℕ, ComputableInPolyTime H encBits encNat →
+      ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
+        (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x => decide (H x = f x)) true).toReal ≤
+          1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ)
+
+/-- **Library specialization (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet`):** deterministic polynomial-time
+heuristic specialization of `MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet (g : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ℕ, ComputableInPolyTime H encBits encNat →
+      ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
+        (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x =>
+          decide (Nat.dist (H x) (f x) ≤ g n)) true).toReal ≤
+          1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ)
+
+/-- **Library specialization (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet`):** deterministic
+polynomial-time heuristic specialization of `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox`. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet (g : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ℕ, ComputableInPolyTime H encBits encNat →
+      ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
+        (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x =>
+          decide (f x - g n ≤ H x ∧ H x ≤ f x)) true).toReal ≤
+          1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ)
+
+/-- **Library companion (`MildlyHardOnAverageIO`):** infinitely-often (`∃ᶠ n in atTop`)
+deterministic-heuristic companion to `MildlyHardOnAverageDet`. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageIO (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ℕ, ComputableInPolyTime H encBits encNat →
+      ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
+        (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x => decide (H x = f x)) true).toReal ≤
+          1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ)
+
+/-- **Library companion (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO`):** infinitely-often (`∃ᶠ n in atTop`)
+deterministic-heuristic companion to `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet`. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO (g : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ℕ, ComputableInPolyTime H encBits encNat →
+      ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
+        (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x =>
+          decide (Nat.dist (H x) (f x) ≤ g n)) true).toReal ≤
+          1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ)
+
+/-- **Library companion (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO`):** infinitely-often
+(`∃ᶠ n in atTop`) deterministic-heuristic companion to `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet`. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO (g : ℕ → ℕ) (f : List Bool → ℕ) : Prop :=
+  ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+    ∀ H : List Bool → ℕ, ComputableInPolyTime H encBits encNat →
+      ∃ᶠ n in atTop,
+        (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x =>
+          decide (f x - g n ≤ H x ∧ H x ≤ f x)) true).toReal ≤
+          1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ)

+/-- **Library companion (`MildlyHardOnAverageENat`):** `ℕ∞`-valued companion to
+`MildlyHardOnAverage` for functions `f : List Bool → ℕ∞` such as `Kolmogorov.timeBounded t`. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageENat (f : List Bool → ℕ∞) : Prop :=

+        (((BitString.uniformList n).bind fun x =>
+          (ProbComp.eval (H x)).map fun v : ℕ => decide ((v : ℕ∞) = f x)) true).toReal ≤
+          1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ)

+/-- **Library companion (`MildlyHardOnAverageIOENat`):** `ℕ∞`-valued companion to
+`MildlyHardOnAverageIO` for functions `f : List Bool → ℕ∞` such as `Kolmogorov.timeBounded t`. -/
+def MildlyHardOnAverageIOENat (f : List Bool → ℕ∞) : Prop :=

+      ∃ᶠ n in atTop,

+/-! ### Monotonicity, shifting, and specialization bridges -/

+private theorem bind_map_decide_le_of_imp {n : ℕ} (q : List Bool → PMF ℕ)
+    (P Q : List Bool → ℕ → Prop) [∀ x v, Decidable (P x v)] [∀ x v, Decidable (Q x v)]
+    (himp : ∀ x ∈ (BitString.uniformList n).support, ∀ v, P x v → Q x v) :
+    (((BitString.uniformList n).bind fun x =>
+        (q x).map fun v => decide (P x v)) true).toReal ≤
+      (((BitString.uniformList n).bind fun x =>
+        (q x).map fun v => decide (Q x v)) true).toReal := by
+  apply ENNReal.toReal_mono (PMF.apply_ne_top _ _)
+  apply PMF.bind_apply_mono_on_support _ true
+  intro x hx
+  apply PMF.bind_apply_mono_on_support _ true
+  intro v _
+  simp only [Function.comp_apply, PMF.pure_apply]
+  by_cases hp : P x v
+  · have hq := himp x hx v hp
+    simp [hp, hq]
+  · simp [hp]
+
+private theorem map_decide_le_of_imp {n : ℕ} (P Q : List Bool → Prop)
+    [∀ x, Decidable (P x)] [∀ x, Decidable (Q x)]
+    (himp : ∀ x ∈ (BitString.uniformList n).support, P x → Q x) :
+    (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x => decide (P x)) true).toReal ≤
+      (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x => decide (Q x)) true).toReal := by
+  apply ENNReal.toReal_mono (PMF.apply_ne_top _ _)
+  apply PMF.bind_apply_mono_on_support _ true
+  intro x hx
+  simp only [Function.comp_apply, PMF.pure_apply]
+  by_cases hp : P x
+  · have hq := himp x hx hp
+    simp [hp, hq]
+  · simp [hp]
+
+/-- Monotonicity of `MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` in the error window: if $g_1(n) \le g_2(n)$ for
+all $n$, then hardness of $g_2$-approximation implies hardness of $g_1$-approximation. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox.mono {g₁ g₂ : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (hle : ∀ n, g₁ n ≤ g₂ n) (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g₂ f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g₁ f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hppt => ?_⟩
+  filter_upwards [hH H hppt] with n hn
+  refine (bind_map_decide_le_of_imp (fun x => ProbComp.eval (H x)) _ _ ?_).trans hn
+  intro x _ v hv
+  exact hv.trans (hle n)
+
+/-- Monotonicity of `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet` in the error window. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet.mono {g₁ g₂ : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (hle : ∀ n, g₁ n ≤ g₂ n) (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet g₂ f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet g₁ f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => ?_⟩
+  filter_upwards [hH H hpoly] with n hn
+  refine (map_decide_le_of_imp _ _ ?_).trans hn
+  intro x _ hx
+  exact hx.trans (hle n)
+
+/-- Monotonicity of `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox` in the error window. -/

+    (hle : ∀ n, g₁ n ≤ g₂ n) (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox g₂ f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox g₁ f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hppt => ?_⟩
+  filter_upwards [hH H hppt] with n hn

+/-- Monotonicity of `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet` in the error window. -/

+/-- Symmetric $g$-approximation hardness (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g f`) implies one-sided
+$g$-approximation hardness (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox g f`). -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox {g : ℕ → ℕ}
+    {f : List Bool → ℕ} (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox g f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hppt => ?_⟩
+  filter_upwards [hH H hppt] with n hn
+  refine (bind_map_decide_le_of_imp (fun x => ProbComp.eval (H x)) _ _ ?_).trans hn
+  intro x _ v ⟨h1, h2⟩
+  unfold Nat.dist
+  omega

+/--
+**Shift + gap-scaling bridge (`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`):**
+shifting a symmetric $g$-estimator $\mathcal{H}(x)$ down by $g(|x|)$ produces a one-sided
+$(2 g)$-estimator $\mathcal{H}'(x) = \mathcal{H}(x) - g(|x|)$, because $|v - f(x)| \le g(|x|)$
+implies $f(x) - 2 g(|x|) \le v - g(|x|) \le f(x)$. Consequently, when `fun x => g x.length` is
+computable in polynomial time, one-sided $(2 g)$-approximation hardness against PPT heuristics
+implies symmetric $g$-approximation hardness (`MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g f`). -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox {g : ℕ → ℕ}
+    {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (hg : ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => g x.length) encBits encNat)
+    (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox (fun n => 2 * g n) f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hppt => ?_⟩
+  have hsub : ComputableInPolyTime (fun pair : List Bool × ℕ => pair.2 - g pair.1.length)
+      (encPair encBits encNat) encNat :=
+    .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.binary_sub'
+      (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.snd encBits encNat)
+      (hg.tidy.comp (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst encBits encNat)))
+  have hppt' : IsPPTOn encBits encNat (fun x => (fun v => v - g x.length) <$> H x) :=
+    hppt.map_with hsub
+  filter_upwards [hH (fun x => (fun v => v - g x.length) <$> H x) hppt'] with n hn
+  refine (ENNReal.toReal_mono (PMF.apply_ne_top _ _) ?_).trans hn
+  apply PMF.bind_apply_mono_on_support _ true
+  intro x hx
+  have hlen : x.length = n := by
+    simp only [BitString.uniformList, PMF.mem_support_map_iff] at hx
+    rcases hx with ⟨y, -, rfl⟩
+    exact List.length_ofFn
+  rw [ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.map_comp]
+  apply PMF.bind_apply_mono_on_support _ true
+  intro v _
+  simp only [Function.comp_apply, PMF.pure_apply, hlen]
+  by_cases hdist : Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ g n
+  · have h_one_sided : f x - 2 * g n ≤ v - g n ∧ v - g n ≤ f x := by
+      unfold Nat.dist at hdist
+      omega
+    simp [hdist, h_one_sided]
+  · simp [hdist]
+
+/-- Deterministic counterpart of
+`MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet.mildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet {g : ℕ → ℕ}
+    {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (hg : ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => g x.length) encBits encNat)
+    (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet (fun n => 2 * g n) f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet g f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => ?_⟩
+  have hpoly' : ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : List Bool => H x - g x.length) encBits encNat :=
+    .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.binary_sub' hpoly.tidy hg.tidy)
+  filter_upwards [hH (fun x => H x - g x.length) hpoly'] with n hn
+  refine (map_decide_le_of_imp _ _ ?_).trans hn
+  intro x hx hdist
+  have hlen : x.length = n := by
+    simp only [BitString.uniformList, PMF.mem_support_map_iff] at hx
+    rcases hx with ⟨y, -, rfl⟩
+    exact List.length_ofFn
+  rw [hlen]
+  unfold Nat.dist at hdist
+  omega
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverageDet` implies `MildlyHardOnAverageIO`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageDet.mildlyHardOnAverageIO {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (h : MildlyHardOnAverageDet f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageIO f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => (hH H hpoly).frequently⟩
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet` implies `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet.mildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO {g : ℕ → ℕ}
+    {f : List Bool → ℕ} (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet g f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO g f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => (hH H hpoly).frequently⟩
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet` implies `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet.mildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO {g : ℕ → ℕ}
+    {f : List Bool → ℕ} (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet g f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO g f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  exact ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => (hH H hpoly).frequently⟩

+private theorem map_decide_eq_le_dist {f H : List Bool → ℕ} (g n : ℕ) :
+    (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x => decide (H x = f x)) true).toReal ≤
+      (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x =>
+        decide (Nat.dist (H x) (f x) ≤ g)) true).toReal :=
+  map_decide_le_of_imp _ _ fun x _ heq => by simp [heq]
+
+private theorem map_decide_eq_le_oneSided {f H : List Bool → ℕ} (g n : ℕ) :
+    (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x => decide (H x = f x)) true).toReal ≤
+      (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun x =>
+        decide (f x - g ≤ H x ∧ H x ≤ f x)) true).toReal :=
+  map_decide_le_of_imp _ _ fun x _ heq => by omega
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet g f` implies `MildlyHardOnAverageDet f`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet.mildlyHardOnAverageDet {g : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet g f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageDet f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => ?_⟩
+  filter_upwards [hH H hpoly] with n hn
+  exact (map_decide_eq_le_dist (g n) n).trans hn
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet g f` implies `MildlyHardOnAverageDet f`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet.mildlyHardOnAverageDet {g : ℕ → ℕ}
+    {f : List Bool → ℕ} (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet g f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageDet f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => ?_⟩
+  filter_upwards [hH H hpoly] with n hn
+  exact (map_decide_eq_le_oneSided (g n) n).trans hn
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO g f` implies `MildlyHardOnAverageIO f`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO.mildlyHardOnAverageIO {g : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO g f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageIO f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => ?_⟩
+  exact (hH H hpoly).mono fun n hn => (map_decide_eq_le_dist (g n) n).trans hn
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO g f` implies `MildlyHardOnAverageIO f`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO.mildlyHardOnAverageIO {g : ℕ → ℕ}
+    {f : List Bool → ℕ} (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxIO g f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageIO f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => ?_⟩
+  exact (hH H hpoly).mono fun n hn => (map_decide_eq_le_oneSided (g n) n).trans hn
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox` implies `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet` (since every
+deterministic polynomial-time heuristic is a strict PPT heuristic). -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet {g : ℕ → ℕ}
+    {f : List Bool → ℕ} (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet g f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => ?_⟩
+  have hppt : IsPPTOn encBits encNat (fun x => pure (H x)) := hpoly.isPPTOn
+  filter_upwards [hH (fun x => pure (H x)) hppt] with n hn
+  simp only [ProbComp.eval_pure, PMF.pure_map] at hn
+  exact hn
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox` implies `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet {g : ℕ → ℕ}
+    {f : List Bool → ℕ} (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox g f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApproxDet g f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => ?_⟩
+  have hppt : IsPPTOn encBits encNat (fun x => pure (H x)) := hpoly.isPPTOn
+  filter_upwards [hH (fun x => pure (H x)) hppt] with n hn
+  simp only [ProbComp.eval_pure, PMF.pure_map] at hn
+  exact hn
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverage` implies `MildlyHardOnAverageDet`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverage.mildlyHardOnAverageDet {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (h : MildlyHardOnAverage f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageDet f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hpoly => ?_⟩
+  have hppt : IsPPTOn encBits encNat (fun x => pure (H x)) := hpoly.isPPTOn
+  filter_upwards [hH (fun x => pure (H x)) hppt] with n hn
+  simp only [ProbComp.eval_pure, PMF.pure_map] at hn
+  exact hn
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverage` implies `MildlyHardOnAverageIO`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverage.mildlyHardOnAverageIO {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (h : MildlyHardOnAverage f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageIO f :=
+  h.mildlyHardOnAverageDet.mildlyHardOnAverageIO
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g f` implies `MildlyHardOnAverage f`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox.mildlyHardOnAverage {g : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverage f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hppt => ?_⟩
+  filter_upwards [hH H hppt] with n hn
+  refine (bind_map_decide_le_of_imp (fun x => ProbComp.eval (H x)) _ _ ?_).trans hn
+  intro x _ v heq
+  simp [heq]
+
+/-- `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox g f` implies `MildlyHardOnAverage f`. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox.mildlyHardOnAverage {g : ℕ → ℕ} {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox g f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverage f := by
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hppt => ?_⟩
+  filter_upwards [hH H hppt] with n hn
+  refine (bind_map_decide_le_of_imp (fun x => ProbComp.eval (H x)) _ _ ?_).trans hn
+  intro x _ v heq
+  omega
+
+/-! ### Rounded logarithm bounds and real-valued log window bridge -/
+
+/-- For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil \le \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$. -/
+theorem nat_clog_two_le_log_two_succ (n : ℕ) : Nat.clog 2 n ≤ Nat.log 2 n + 1 :=
+  Nat.clog_le_of_le_pow (Nat.le_of_lt (Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self Nat.one_lt_two n))
+
+/-- For every $n \ge 1$, the real binary logarithm satisfies
+$\log_2 n \le \lfloor \log_2 n \rfloor + 1$. -/
+theorem real_logb_two_le_nat_log_two_succ {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
+    Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ) ≤ (Nat.log 2 n + 1 : ℕ) := by
+  have hn_pos : (0 : ℝ) < (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
+  rw [Real.logb_le_iff_le_rpow (by norm_num : (1 : ℝ) < 2) hn_pos, Real.rpow_natCast]
+  have hlt := Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self Nat.one_lt_two n
+  exact_mod_cast hlt.le
+
+/-- Any real-valued symmetric approximation error $|(v : \mathbb{R}) - (w : \mathbb{R})| \le
+d \log_2 n$ (for $n \ge 1$) implies the upper-rounded integer distance bound
+`Nat.dist v w ≤ d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)`. -/
+theorem nat_dist_le_mul_log_two_succ_of_abs_sub_le_mul_logb {v w d n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n)
+    (h : |(v : ℝ) - (w : ℝ)| ≤ (d : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ)) :
+    Nat.dist v w ≤ d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1) := by
+  have hdist_real : ((Nat.dist v w : ℕ) : ℝ) = |(v : ℝ) - (w : ℝ)| := by
+    rcases le_total v w with hvw | hwv
+    · have h1 : Nat.dist v w = w - v := by
+        unfold Nat.dist
+        omega
+      have hvw_real : (v : ℝ) ≤ (w : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hvw
+      rw [h1, Nat.cast_sub hvw, abs_of_nonpos (by linarith)]
+      ring
+    · have h1 : Nat.dist v w = v - w := by
+        unfold Nat.dist
+        omega
+      have hwv_real : (w : ℝ) ≤ (v : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hwv
+      rw [h1, Nat.cast_sub hwv, abs_of_nonneg (by linarith)]
+  have hlog := real_logb_two_le_nat_log_two_succ hn
+  have hle : ((Nat.dist v w : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ((d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1) : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
+    rw [hdist_real, Nat.cast_mul]
+    exact h.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hlog (Nat.cast_nonneg d))
+  exact_mod_cast hle
+
+/-- **Real-valued $d \log_2 n$ approximation window bridge:** if `f` is mildly hard on average to
+approximate within the upper-rounded integer window `fun n => d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)`, then `f` is
+mildly hard on average to approximate within the real-valued window $d \log_2 n$ of
+[Liu and Pass, Definition 2.5 and Theorem 3.1 (c), pp. 8–9 of arXiv:2009.11514v1][LiuPass2020]. -/
+theorem MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox.eventually_real_abs_sub_le {d : ℕ} {f : List Bool → ℕ}
+    (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox (fun n => d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)) f) :
+    ∃ p : Polynomial ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < p.eval n) ∧
+      ∀ H : List Bool → ProbComp ℕ, IsPPTOn encBits encNat H →
+        ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
+          (((BitString.uniformList n).bind fun x =>
+            (ProbComp.eval (H x)).map fun v : ℕ =>
+              decide (|(v : ℝ) - (f x : ℝ)| ≤ (d : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ))) true).toReal ≤
+            1 - 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
+  classical
+  obtain ⟨p, hp, hH⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨p, hp, fun H hppt => ?_⟩
+  filter_upwards [hH H hppt, eventually_ge_atTop 1] with n hn hn1
+  refine (bind_map_decide_le_of_imp (fun x => ProbComp.eval (H x))
+    (fun x v => |(v : ℝ) - (f x : ℝ)| ≤ (d : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 (n : ℝ))
+    (fun x v => Nat.dist v (f x) ≤ d * (Nat.log 2 n + 1)) ?_).trans hn
+  intro x _ v hv
+  exact nat_dist_le_mul_log_two_succ_of_abs_sub_le_mul_logb hn1 hv
+
+/-! ### Negative-side nonvacuity lemmas for the constant zero function -/
+
+/-- The constant zero function `fun _ => 0` is **not** `MildlyHardOnAverageIO`, because the
+constant zero polynomial-time heuristic succeeds with probability $1$ on every input length. -/
+theorem not_mildlyHardOnAverageIO_zero : ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageIO (fun _ => 0) := by
+  rintro ⟨p, hp, hH⟩
+  have h0 : ComputableInPolyTime (fun _ : List Bool => (0 : ℕ)) encBits encNat := by fun_prop
+  have hfreq := hH (fun _ => 0) h0
+  refine hfreq (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun n => ?_)
+  rw [not_le]
+  have hp_pos : (0 : ℝ) < (p.eval n : ℕ) := by exact_mod_cast hp n
+  have hdiv_pos : 0 < 1 / ((p.eval n : ℕ) : ℝ) := one_div_pos.mpr hp_pos
+  have hval :
+      (((BitString.uniformList n).map fun _ => decide ((0 : ℕ) = 0)) true).toReal = 1 := by
+    simp
+  rw [hval]
+  linarith
+
+/-- The constant zero function `fun _ => 0` is not `MildlyHardOnAverageDet`. -/
+theorem not_mildlyHardOnAverageDet_zero : ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageDet (fun _ => 0) :=
+  fun h => not_mildlyHardOnAverageIO_zero h.mildlyHardOnAverageIO
+
+/-- The constant zero function `fun _ => 0` is not `MildlyHardOnAverage`. -/
+theorem not_mildlyHardOnAverage_zero : ¬ MildlyHardOnAverage (fun _ => 0) :=
+  fun h => not_mildlyHardOnAverageIO_zero h.mildlyHardOnAverageIO
+
+/-- The constant zero function `fun _ => 0` is not `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO g` for any error
+function `g`. -/
+theorem not_mildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO_zero (g : ℕ → ℕ) :
+    ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO g (fun _ => 0) :=
+  fun h => not_mildlyHardOnAverageIO_zero h.mildlyHardOnAverageIO
+
+/-- The constant zero function `fun _ => 0` is not `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet g` for any error
+function `g`. -/
+theorem not_mildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet_zero (g : ℕ → ℕ) :
+    ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet g (fun _ => 0) :=
+  fun h => not_mildlyHardOnAverageIO_zero h.mildlyHardOnAverageDet.mildlyHardOnAverageIO
+
+/-- The constant zero function `fun _ => 0` is not `MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g` for any error
+function `g`. -/
+theorem not_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_zero (g : ℕ → ℕ) :
+    ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g (fun _ => 0) :=
+  fun h => not_mildlyHardOnAverageIO_zero h.mildlyHardOnAverage.mildlyHardOnAverageIO
+
+/-- The constant zero function `fun _ => 0` is not `MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox g` for any
+error function `g`. -/
+theorem not_mildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox_zero (g : ℕ → ℕ) :
+    ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox g (fun _ => 0) :=
+  fun h => not_mildlyHardOnAverageIO_zero h.mildlyHardOnAverage.mildlyHardOnAverageIO
+
+end Cslib.Complexity

+/-- `fun _ => 0` is not `MildlyHardOnAverage`, `MildlyHardOnAverageDet`, `MildlyHardOnAverageIO`,
+`MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO g`, `MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet g`,

+    ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageDet (fun _ => 0) ∧
+    ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageIO (fun _ => 0) ∧
+    ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO g (fun _ => 0) ∧
+    ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageToApproxDet g (fun _ => 0) ∧
+    ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox g (fun _ => 0) ∧
+    ¬ MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox g (fun _ => 0) :=
+  ⟨not_mildlyHardOnAverage_zero,

+   not_mildlyHardOnAverageIO_zero,
+   not_mildlyHardOnAverageToApproxIO_zero g,

+   not_mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox_zero g,

+
+/-- Concrete instantiation of the rounded-logarithm comparison lemmas at $n = 6, d = 2$:
+$\lceil \log_2 6 \rceil = 3 \le \lfloor \log_2 6 \rfloor + 1 = 3$, and any $v, w \in \mathbb{N}$
+with $|(v : \mathbb{R}) - (w : \mathbb{R})| \le 2 \log_2 6$ satisfies `Nat.dist v w ≤ 6`. -/
+example (v w : ℕ) (h : |(v : ℝ) - (w : ℝ)| ≤ (2 : ℝ) * Real.logb 2 (6 : ℝ)) :
+    Nat.clog 2 6 ≤ Nat.log 2 6 + 1 ∧
+    Real.logb 2 (6 : ℝ) ≤ (Nat.log 2 6 + 1 : ℕ) ∧
+    Nat.dist v w ≤ 2 * (Nat.log 2 6 + 1) :=
+  ⟨nat_clog_two_le_log_two_succ 6,
+   real_logb_two_le_nat_log_two_succ (by omega : 1 ≤ 6),
+   nat_dist_le_mul_log_two_succ_of_abs_sub_le_mul_logb (by omega : 1 ≤ 6) h⟩
+

+for a constant gap $g(n) = c$: one-sided $(2c)$-approximation hardness implies symmetric
+$c$-approximation hardness, exact PPT hardness, deterministic hardness, and IO hardness. -/
+example (c : ℕ) (f : List Bool → ℕ)
+    (h : MildlyHardOnAverageToOneSidedApprox (fun _ => 2 * c) f) :
+    MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox (fun _ => c) f ∧
+    MildlyHardOnAverage f ∧
+    MildlyHardOnAverageDet f ∧
+    MildlyHardOnAverageIO f := by
+  have hsymm : MildlyHardOnAverageToApprox (fun _ => c) f :=
+    h.mildlyHardOnAverageToApprox (ComputableInPolyTime.const c)
+  have hexact := hsymm.mildlyHardOnAverage
+  exact ⟨hsymm, hexact, hexact.mildlyHardOnAverageDet, hexact.mildlyHardOnAverageIO⟩
+
+end Cslib.Complexity.AverageCaseTests

+/-

+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+import Complexity.Computability.Probabilistic.PPT.Capture
+import Complexity.Tactic.PPT
+
+/-!
+# Plain deterministic callbacks with captured probabilistic input
+
+The callback is certified on the entire framed pair of caller input and sampled value. It uses
+one uniform machine, with no separate premise about the sampled value's length or distribution.
+-/
+
+open Cslib Cslib.Probability Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+example {α β γ : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {sample : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {output : γ ↪ List Bool} {program : α → ProbComp β} {callback : α → β → γ}
+    (hp : IsPPTOn input sample program)
+    (hf : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p => callback p.1 p.2) (encPair input sample) output) :
+    IsPPTOn input output (fun a => callback a <$> program a) := by
+  fail_if_success (clear hf; ppt)
+  exact hp.map_with hf
+
+-- A raw construction certificate can still be explicitly forgotten inside an existing proof.
+example {α β γ : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {sample : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {output : γ ↪ List Bool} {program : α → ProbComp β} {callback : α → β → γ}
+    (hp : IsPPTOn input sample program)
+    (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p => callback p.1 p.2) (encPair input sample) output) :
+    IsPPTOn input output (fun a => callback a <$> program a) :=
+  hp.map_with (.of_tidy hf)
+
+-- The output retains an actual captured word as well as the sampled word.
+example {source : ℕ × List Bool → ProbComp (List Bool)}
+    (hs : IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary encBits) encBits source) :
+    IsPPTOn (encPair encUnary encBits) encBits
+      (fun a => (fun word => a.2 ++ word) <$> source a) := by
+  apply hs.map_with
+  fun_prop

+/-- Project a first component and convert its encoding. Certifying the pair-valued function first
+determines the source encoding before automation searches for the conversion certificate. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem fstWithEncoding {α β γ : Type} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {encC : γ ↪ List Bool} {output : α ↪ List Bool} {f : γ → α × β}
+    (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encC (encPair encA encB))
+    (h : ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => a) encA output) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun p => (f p).1) encC output :=
+  h.comp hf.fst'
+
+/-- Project a second component and convert its encoding. The pair certificate fixes the source
+encoding; the conversion certificate supplies the efficient change of representation. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem sndWithEncoding {α β γ : Type} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {encC : γ ↪ List Bool} {output : β ↪ List Bool} {f : γ → α × β}
+    (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f encC (encPair encA encB))
+    (h : ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => a) encB output) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun p => (f p).2) encC output :=
+  h.comp hf.snd'
+
 /-- A case distinction between functions computable in polynomial time on all inputs. -/
 @[fun_prop]
 theorem ite' {encC : Bool ↪ List Bool} {c : α → Bool} {f g : α → β}

@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Plain
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.BitString
+import Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime
+
+/-!
+# Encoding-aware plain projections
+
+The input context and both source encodings are fixed by the pair certificate before the
+conversion is sought. These clients also check a framed-word projection inside a bit operation.
+-/
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+example {α β γ : Type} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {input : γ ↪ List Bool} {output : α ↪ List Bool} {f : γ → α × β}
+    (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f input (encPair encA encB))
+    (h : ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => a) encA output) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (f x).1) input output := by
+  fail_if_success (clear h; fun_prop)
+  exact hf.fstWithEncoding h
+
+example {α β γ : Type} {encA : α ↪ List Bool} {encB : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {input : γ ↪ List Bool} {output : β ↪ List Bool} {f : γ → α × β}
+    (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f input (encPair encA encB))
+    (h : ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => a) encB output) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (f x).2) input output := by
+  fail_if_success (clear hf; fun_prop)
+  exact hf.sndWithEncoding h
+
+-- The conversion is an ordinary supplied certificate; no change of the input encoding is hidden.
+example : ComputableInPolyTime
+    (fun p : List Bool × ℕ => p.1.take (p.2 + 1))
+    (encPair (encList encBool) encUnary) encBits := by
+  have hconvert : ComputableInPolyTime (fun l => l) (encList encBool) encBits :=
+    .of_tidy ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.listToBits
+  fun_prop
+
+example : ComputableInPolyTime
+    (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => p.2.take (p.1 + 1))
+    (encPair encUnary (encList encBool)) encBits := by
+  have hconvert : ComputableInPolyTime (fun l => l) (encList encBool) encBits :=
+    .of_tidy ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.listToBits
+  fun_prop

@@ -462,6 +462,8 @@ end Turing.MultiTapeTM
 
 namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime
 
+variable {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+
 /-- Test whether any bit satisfies a captured predicate. -/
 @[fun_prop]
 theorem bitsAnyWithInput {α : Type}
@@ -507,4 +509,322 @@ theorem bitsZipWithInput (op : Bool → Bool → Bool) {α : Type} {input : α 
     ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (left a).zipWith op (right a)) input encBits :=
   .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsZipWithInput op hleft.tidy hright.tidy)
 
+/-- Convert framed Boolean lists to raw words without changing their contents. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem listToBits : ComputableInPolyTime (fun l => l) (encList encBool) encBits :=
+  .of_tidy ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.listToBits
+
+/-- Read a row of a computed word, charging padding and both computed unary indices. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsRowWithInput {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {width row : α → ℕ} {word : α → List Bool}
+    (hwidth : ComputableInPolyTime width input encUnary)
+    (hrow : ComputableInPolyTime row input encUnary)
+    (hword : ComputableInPolyTime word input encBits) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => Cslib.BitString.listRow (width a) (row a) (word a))
+      input encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsRowWithInput hwidth.tidy hrow.tidy hword.tidy)
+
+/-- Frame the existing input encoding, charging every delimiter. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsFrame {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => frame (enc a)) enc encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsFrame (α := α) (enc := enc))
+
+/-- Saturating binary decoding to unary is polynomial time on arbitrary input words. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsBoundedBinaryValue : ComputableInPolyTime
+    (fun p : ℕ × List Bool => Cslib.BitString.boundedBinaryValue p.1 p.2)
+    (encPair encUnary encBits) encUnary :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsBoundedBinaryValue)
+
+/-- Decode computed bits under a computed unary cap, fixing both intermediate encodings. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsBoundedBinaryValueWithInput {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {cap : α → ℕ} {word : α → List Bool}
+    (hcap : ComputableInPolyTime cap input encUnary)
+    (hword : ComputableInPolyTime word input encBits) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => Cslib.BitString.boundedBinaryValue (cap a) (word a))
+      input encUnary :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsBoundedBinaryValueWithInput (α := α)
+    (input := input)
+    (cap := cap)
+    (word := word)
+    (hcap := hcap.tidy)
+    (hword := hword.tidy))
+
+/-- Convert a binary value to unary under a computed unary bound. -/
+theorem binary_to_unary_bounded {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {value bound : α → ℕ}
+    (hvalue : ComputableInPolyTime value input encNat)
+    (hbound : ComputableInPolyTime bound input encUnary)
+    (hle : ∀ a, value a ≤ bound a) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime value input encUnary :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.binary_to_unary_bounded (α := α)
+    (input := input)
+    (value := value)
+    (bound := bound)
+    (hvalue := hvalue.tidy)
+    (hbound := hbound.tidy)
+    (hle := hle))
+
+/-- Convert a raw bit string to the framed list encoding. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsToList : ComputableInPolyTime (fun l => l) encBits (encList encBool) :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsToList)
+
+/-- Optional lookup in a raw bit string, fixing the representation of the returned bit. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsGetElem? {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {list : α → List Bool} {index : α → ℕ}
+    (hlist : ComputableInPolyTime list input encBits)
+    (hindex : ComputableInPolyTime index input encUnary) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (list x)[index x]?) input (encOption encBool) :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsGetElem? (α := α)
+    (input := input)
+    (list := list)
+    (index := index)
+    (hlist := hlist.tidy)
+    (hindex := hindex.tidy))
+
+/-- Concatenate computed raw words, fixing the intermediate list encoding before proof search. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsFlatten {words : α → List (List Bool)}
+    (hwords : ComputableInPolyTime words input (encList encBits)) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (words a).flatten) input encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsFlatten (words := words) (hwords := hwords.tidy))
+
+/-- Map a captured Boolean-valued function over a framed list, emitting a raw bit string. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem mapToBitsWithInput {β : Type} {enc : β ↪ List Bool} {list : α → List β}
+    {f : α → β → Bool}
+    (hlist : ComputableInPolyTime list input (encList enc))
+    (hf : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : α × β => f p.1 p.2)
+      (encPair input enc) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (list a).map (f a)) input encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.mapToBitsWithInput (β := β)
+    (enc := enc)
+    (list := list)
+    (f := f)
+    (hlist := hlist.tidy)
+    (hf := hf.tidy))
+
+/-- Concatenate captured raw bit strings over a framed list. The complete intermediate words
+and their framing are charged before concatenation. Apply this rule explicitly: registering both
+raw and framed `flatMap` outputs makes existing enumeration proof search exceed its limit. -/
+theorem flatMapToBitsWithInput {β : Type} {enc : β ↪ List Bool} {list : α → List β}
+    {f : α → β → List Bool}
+    (hlist : ComputableInPolyTime list input (encList enc))
+    (hf : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : α × β => f p.1 p.2)
+      (encPair input enc) encBits) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (list a).flatMap (f a)) input encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.flatMapToBitsWithInput (β := β)
+    (enc := enc)
+    (list := list)
+    (f := f)
+    (hlist := hlist.tidy)
+    (hf := hf.tidy))
+
+/-- Emit a computed unary number of low-order digits of a computed binary natural. The width
+charges every output bit, including leading zero digits. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsLow {width value : α → ℕ}
+    (hwidth : ComputableInPolyTime width input encUnary)
+    (hvalue : ComputableInPolyTime value input encNat) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => Cslib.BitString.lowBits (width a) (value a))
+      input encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsLow (width := width)
+    (value := value)
+    (hwidth := hwidth.tidy)
+    (hvalue := hvalue.tidy))
+
+/-- Map a captured Boolean operation over a raw bit string. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsMapWithInput {list : α → List Bool} {f : α → Bool → Bool}
+    (hlist : ComputableInPolyTime list input encBits)
+    (hf : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : α × Bool => f p.1 p.2)
+      (encPair input encBool) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (list a).map (f a)) input encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsMapWithInput (list := list)
+    (f := f)
+    (hlist := hlist.tidy)
+    (hf := hf.tidy))
+
+/-- Filter a raw bit string with a predicate that may capture its original input. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsFilterWithInput {list : α → List Bool} {test : α → Bool → Bool}
+    (hlist : ComputableInPolyTime list input encBits)
+    (htest : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : α × Bool => test p.1 p.2)
+      (encPair input encBool) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (list a).filter (test a)) input encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsFilterWithInput (list := list)
+    (test := test)
+    (hlist := hlist.tidy)
+    (htest := htest.tidy))
+
+/-- Count predicate matches in a raw bit string, including a captured input. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsCountPWithInput {list : α → List Bool} {test : α → Bool → Bool}
+    (hlist : ComputableInPolyTime list input encBits)
+    (htest : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : α × Bool => test p.1 p.2)
+      (encPair input encBool) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (list x).countP (test x)) input encUnary :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsCountPWithInput (list := list)
+    (test := test)
+    (hlist := hlist.tidy)
+    (htest := htest.tidy))
+
+/-- Count occurrences of a computed bit in a raw bit string. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsCountWithInput {list : α → List Bool} {value : α → Bool}
+    (hlist : ComputableInPolyTime list input encBits)
+    (hvalue : ComputableInPolyTime value input encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x => (list x).count (value x)) input encUnary :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsCountWithInput (list := list)
+    (value := value)
+    (hlist := hlist.tidy)
+    (hvalue := hvalue.tidy))
+
+/-- Test whether every bit satisfies a captured predicate. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsAllWithInput {list : α → List Bool} {test : α → Bool → Bool}
+    (hlist : ComputableInPolyTime list input encBits)
+    (htest : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : α × Bool => test p.1 p.2)
+      (encPair input encBool) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (list a).all (test a)) input encBool :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsAllWithInput (list := list)
+    (test := test)
+    (hlist := hlist.tidy)
+    (htest := htest.tidy))
+
+/-- A Boolean fold has constant-sized state, so no separate state bound is needed. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsFoldlWithInput (op : Bool → Bool → Bool) {list : α → List Bool} {init : α → Bool}
+    (hlist : ComputableInPolyTime list input encBits)
+    (hinit : ComputableInPolyTime init input encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (list a).foldl op (init a)) input encBool :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsFoldlWithInput (op := op)
+    (list := list)
+    (init := init)
+    (hlist := hlist.tidy)
+    (hinit := hinit.tidy))
+
+/-- Apply a fixed Boolean operation pointwise, stopping at the shorter word. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsZipWith (op : Bool → Bool → Bool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × List Bool => p.1.zipWith op p.2)
+      (encPair encBits encBits) encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsZipWith (op := op))
+
+/-- Strict majority uses filtering, length, unary multiplication and comparison. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsStrictMajority : ComputableInPolyTime Cslib.BitString.listStrictMajority
+    encBits encBool :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsStrictMajority)
+
+/-- Strict majority of computed votes fixes the intermediate raw-word encoding. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsStrictMajorityWithInput {votes : α → List Bool}
+    (hvotes : ComputableInPolyTime votes input encBits) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => Cslib.BitString.listStrictMajority (votes a))
+      input encBool :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsStrictMajorityWithInput (votes := votes)
+    (hvotes := hvotes.tidy))
+
+/-- The training test is polynomial time in the vote list and its supplied label. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsNonpositiveMarginWithInput
+    {votes : α → List Bool} {truth : α → Bool}
+    (hvotes : ComputableInPolyTime votes input encBits)
+    (htruth : ComputableInPolyTime truth input encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => Cslib.BitString.listNonpositiveMargin (votes a) (truth a))
+      input encBool :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsNonpositiveMarginWithInput (votes := votes)
+    (truth := truth)
+    (hvotes := hvotes.tidy)
+    (htruth := htruth.tidy))
+
+/-- Generate one coordinate mask from its unary width and index. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsSingle : ComputableInPolyTime
+    (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => Cslib.BitString.listSingle p.1 p.2)
+    (encPair encUnary encUnary) encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsSingle)
+
+/-- Generate all coordinate masks, charging for their quadratic total size. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsSingles : ComputableInPolyTime Cslib.BitString.listSingles
+    encUnary (encList encBits) :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsSingles)
+
+/-- Sum selected rows with a shrinking selector and an accumulator that never grows. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsXorSelected : ComputableInPolyTime
+    (fun p : ℕ × List Bool × List (List Bool) =>
+      Cslib.BitString.listXorSelected p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+    (encPair encUnary (encPair encBits (encList encBits))) encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsXorSelected)
+
+/-- Enumerate words only when their complete encoded size is polynomially bounded.
+This does not claim polynomial time in the number of enumerated bits. -/
+theorem bitsEnumList {count : α → ℕ}
+    (hcount : ComputableInPolyTime count input encUnary)
+    {size : ℕ → ℕ} (hsize : Cslib.PolynomiallyBounded size)
+    (hbudget : ∀ a, 2 ^ count a * (2 * count a + 1) ≤ size (input a).length) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => Cslib.BitString.enumList (count a))
+      input (encList encBits) :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsEnumList (count := count)
+    (hcount := hcount.tidy)
+    (size := size)
+    (hsize := hsize)
+    (hbudget := hbudget))
+
+/-- Extract rows from a word with polynomial-time unary dimensions. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsRowsWithInput {count width : α → ℕ} {word : α → List Bool}
+    (hcount : ComputableInPolyTime count input encUnary)
+    (hwidth : ComputableInPolyTime width input encUnary)
+    (hword : ComputableInPolyTime word input encBits) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => Cslib.BitString.listRows (count a) (width a) (word a))
+      input (encList encBits) :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsRowsWithInput (count := count)
+    (width := width)
+    (word := word)
+    (hcount := hcount.tidy)
+    (hwidth := hwidth.tidy)
+    (hword := hword.tidy))
+
+/-- Variable-width XOR uses runtime lookup and ordinary Boolean folds. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsXorWithInput {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {width : α → ℕ} {words : α → List (List Bool)}
+    (hwidth : ComputableInPolyTime width input encUnary)
+    (hwords : ComputableInPolyTime words input (encList encBits)) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => Cslib.BitString.listXor (width a) (words a))
+      input encBits :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsXorWithInput (α := α)
+    (input := input)
+    (width := width)
+    (words := words)
+    (hwidth := hwidth.tidy)
+    (hwords := hwords.tidy))
+
+/-- Lexicographic comparison of equal-length words is polynomial-time. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsWordLt {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {x y : α → List Bool}
+    (hx : ComputableInPolyTime x input encBits)
+    (hy : ComputableInPolyTime y input encBits) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun c => Cslib.BitString.wordLt (x c) (y c)) input encBool :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsWordLt (α := α)
+    (input := input)
+    (x := x)
+    (y := y)
+    (hx := hx.tidy)
+    (hy := hy.tidy))
+
+/-- Decode arbitrary most-significant-first bit words to binary naturals. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsBinaryValue :
+    ComputableInPolyTime Cslib.BitString.binaryValue encBits encNat :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsBinaryValue)
+
 end Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime

+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime
+
+/-- Division of two unary counters, including divisor zero. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem unary_div : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1 / p.2)
+    (encPair encUnary encUnary) encUnary :=
+  .of_tidy ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_div
+
+/-- Remainder of two unary counters, including divisor zero. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem unary_mod : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => p.1 % p.2)
+    (encPair encUnary encUnary) encUnary :=
+  .of_tidy ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_mod
+
+/-- Compute both quotient and remainder with a runtime unary divisor. Division by zero returns
+`(0, dividend)`, matching Lean's conventions. All intermediate counters have linear size. -/
+theorem unary_divMod : ComputableInPolyTime (fun p : ℕ × ℕ => (p.1 / p.2, p.1 % p.2))
+    (encPair encUnary encUnary) (encPair encUnary encUnary) :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_divMod)
+
+/-- Division by a fixed natural is a special case of runtime unary division. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem unary_div_const (divisor : ℕ) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun n : ℕ => n / divisor) encUnary encUnary :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_div_const (divisor := divisor))
+
+end Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime

+/-

+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.List
+public import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Nat
+public import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Plain
+public import Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime.Init
+
+/-!
+# Binary list length in polynomial time
+
+`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.length_list` computes the length of a framed list in
+unary (`encUnary`), the representation required by bounded loops and `List.range`. Verifiers and
+reductions that compare a list length against a binary parameter or add it to binary wire and
+vertex indices instead need the length in the binary natural encoding `encNat`. Composing
+`length_list` with `unary_to_binary` provides plain rules for `fun_prop` and `polytime`.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime.length_list_binary`: the length of a framed list in
+  the binary encoding `encNat`.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime.length_list_binary'`: the binary length of a computed
+  framed list, fixing the intermediate list encoding for proof search.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime
+
+/-- Length of a framed list in binary (`encNat`); the element encoding is inferred from the list
+encoding. -/
+@[fun_prop, aesop safe -30 apply (rule_sets := [PolyTime])]
+theorem length_list_binary {α : Type} (enc : α ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun l : List α => l.length) (encList enc) encNat :=
+  .of_tidy (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_to_binary.comp (.length_list enc))
+
+/-- Length of a computed framed list in binary (`encNat`), fixing the intermediate list encoding for
+proof search. -/
+@[fun_prop, aesop safe -30 apply (rule_sets := [PolyTime])]
+theorem length_list_binary' {α β : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {enc : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {list : α → List β} (hlist : ComputableInPolyTime list input (encList enc)) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => (list a).length) input encNat :=
+  (length_list_binary enc).comp hlist
+
+end Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime

title: fix(polytime): reject unsupported program certificate predicates (#766)
patch:
commit 51c80eff88c02c572eb27b63e6994c43eff12d86
Author:     Samuel Schlesinger <SamuelSchlesinger@users.noreply.github.com>

    fix(polytime): reject unsupported program certificate predicates (#766)

diff --git a/Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean b/Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean
index db5ba3ef..64bf3d8e 100644
--- a/Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean
+++ b/Complexity/Tactic/PolyTime/Init.lean
@@ -72,6 +72,14 @@ def efficiencyKey (statement : Expr) : MetaM (Name × Name × Bool) := do
   let statement := statement.consumeMData
   let some predicate := statement.getAppFn.constName?
     | throwError "expected an efficiency statement"
+  unless predicate == `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime ||
+      predicate == `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime ||
+      predicate == `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn || predicate == `Cslib.Probability.IsPPT ||
+      predicate == `Cslib.WordRAM.Refines ||
+      predicate == `Cslib.WordRAM.ComputableInPolyTime ||
+      predicate == `Cslib.WordRAM.UniformComputableInPolyTime do
+    throwError "unsupported efficiency predicate `{predicate}` for `program_certificate`; \
+      expected TM polynomial time, PPT, or a documented word-RAM certificate"
   let argument := if predicate == `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime ||
       predicate == `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime then
     statement.getAppArgs[2]! else statement.getAppArgs.back!
@@ -126,8 +134,11 @@ private def hasGlobalFunProp (decl : Name) : CoreM Bool := do
     (← hasGlobalEntry transitionTheoremsExt (·.thmName) decl)
 
 /-- `@[program_certificate]` registers an efficiency certificate for `polytime` and `ppt`. Its
-conclusion must be a `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`, `IsPPTOn` or `IsPPT` statement whose program
-body applies a constant, possibly under an output encoding.
+conclusion must be a `ComputableInPolyTime`, `ComputableTidilyInPolyTime`, `IsPPTOn` or `IsPPT`
+statement, or one of the word-RAM predicates `WordRAM.Refines`, `WordRAM.ComputableInPolyTime`,
+`WordRAM.UniformComputableInPolyTime` used by `Tactic.WordRAM`. The indexed argument must apply
+a constant, possibly under an output encoding. Other predicates are rejected rather than indexed
+by an unrelated final argument.
 Certificates are also registered with `fun_prop` for use in larger compositions, unless the same
 declaration already has a global registration.
 
diff --git a/ComplexityTests.lean b/ComplexityTests.lean
index af763fe2..fbb107e5 100644
--- a/ComplexityTests.lean
+++ b/ComplexityTests.lean
@@ -349,6 +349,7 @@ import ComplexityTests.ProbabilityNotation
 import ComplexityTests.ProbabilityToolkit
 import ComplexityTests.ProbabilityToolkit2
 import ComplexityTests.ProbabilityToolkit3
+import ComplexityTests.ProgramCertificateDiagnostics
 import ComplexityTests.Programs
 import ComplexityTests.ProofComplexity
 import ComplexityTests.ProofComplexity.Pigeonhole
diff --git a/ComplexityTests/ProgramCertificateDiagnostics.lean b/ComplexityTests/ProgramCertificateDiagnostics.lean
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..d4f8c4c7
--- /dev/null
+++ b/ComplexityTests/ProgramCertificateDiagnostics.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+import Complexity.Crypto.Computational.Signature
+import Complexity.Crypto.Computational.MAC
+import ComplexityTests.PolyTimePlainDriver
+
+/-! Actual imported verification projections must be indexed by their programs. Unsupported
+predicates must not silently register an inert certificate under their last argument. -/
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM Cslib.Crypto
+
+run_meta do
+  for (certificate, program) in
+      [(`Cslib.Crypto.SignatureScheme.verify_polyTime, `Cslib.Crypto.SignatureScheme.verify),
+       (`Cslib.Crypto.MACScheme.verify_polyTime, `Cslib.Crypto.MACScheme.verify)] do
+    let type := (← Lean.getConstInfo certificate).type
+    let key ← Lean.Meta.forallTelescope type fun _ conclusion =>
+      Cslib.Tactic.efficiencyKey conclusion
+    unless key == (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableInPolyTime, program, false) do
+      throwError "incorrect imported verification key: {key}"
+    let entries := (Cslib.Tactic.certificateExt.getState (← Lean.getEnv)).getD key #[]
+    unless entries.any (fun entry => entry.1 == certificate) do
+      throwError "actual verification certificate absent from its program key: {certificate}"
+
+example (S : SignatureScheme) : ComputableInPolyTime
+    (fun p : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool => S.verify p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+    (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits)) encBool := by polytime
+
+example (M : MACScheme) : ComputableInPolyTime
+    (fun p : List Bool × List Bool × List Bool => M.verify p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2)
+    (encPair encBits (encPair encBits encBits)) encBool := by polytime
+
+-- This existing irreducible routine and certificate come from another ordinary module import.
+-- The eager contract prevents fun_prop alone from hiding an inert named-certificate path.
+example (B : Cslib.WordRAM.Basis) (c : ℕ) : ComputableInPolyTime
+    (PlainDriverTests.checkedNamedConstant B c c) encUnary (encOption encNat) := by
+  fail_if_success fun_prop
+  polytime
+
+namespace ProgramCertificateDiagnostics
+
+def NotEfficiency (_ : List Bool → List Bool) : Prop := True
+
+theorem wrongPredicate : NotEfficiency List.reverse := True.intro
+
+/--
+error: unsupported efficiency predicate `ProgramCertificateDiagnostics.NotEfficiency` for
+`program_certificate`; expected TM polynomial time, PPT, or a documented word-RAM certificate
+-/
+#guard_msgs (whitespace := lax) in
+attribute [program_certificate] wrongPredicate
+
+theorem noProgram : True := True.intro
+
+/--
+error: unsupported efficiency predicate `True` for `program_certificate`; expected
+TM polynomial time, PPT, or a documented word-RAM certificate
+-/
+#guard_msgs (whitespace := lax) in
+attribute [program_certificate] noProgram
+
+end ProgramCertificateDiagnostics

title: feat(probability): approximately uniform residues modulo q in strict PPT (#726)
patch:
commit 9ec699cada947a48bf9dd20b5f9dba85484d1fca
Author:     Samuel Schlesinger <SamuelSchlesinger@users.noreply.github.com>
AuthorDate: Sat Oct 24 05:20:30 2026 +0000
Commit:     GitHub <noreply@github.com>
CommitDate: Sat Oct 24 05:20:30 2026 +0000

    feat(probability): approximately uniform residues modulo q in strict PPT (#726)
    
    A uniform value below `N`, read in `ZMod q`, is within statistical distance
    `(N mod q) / N ≤ q / N` of uniform (`dist_map_natCast_uniformOfFintype_le`).
    `sampleModNat width modulus` reduces `width` fair bits modulo `modulus`.
    Its law is `eval_sampleModNat`, and its distance from uniform on `ZMod q` is
    at most `q / 2 ^ width` (`dist_map_natCast_eval_sampleModNat_le`).
    `isPPTOn_sampleModNat` certifies it for computed widths and moduli, with
    plain hypotheses.
    
    Refs #581
    
    
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Dvi6MU29zU9t8zYfeU51sB
    
    Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+import Mathlib.Data.Int.CardIntervalMod
+import Mathlib.Data.ZMod.Basic

+/-!
+# Reducing a uniform value modulo `q`
+
+A uniform value below `N`, read in `ZMod q`, is close to uniform: each residue has `⌊N / q⌋` or
+`⌊N / q⌋ + 1` preimages, so the statistical distance to the uniform distribution on `ZMod q` is at
+most `(N mod q) / N`, and hence at most `q / N` (`dist_map_natCast_uniformOfFintype_le`). With
+`N = 2 ^ ℓ` fair bits this gives an efficient approximately uniform sampler for `ZMod q`, with
+distance at most `q / 2 ^ ℓ`; strict PPT machines cannot sample `ZMod q` exactly when `q` is not
+a power of two.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Probability.PMF.dist_map_natCast_uniformOfFintype_le`: distance at most `(N mod q) / N`.
+* `Cslib.Probability.PMF.dist_map_natCast_uniformOfFintype_le_div`: distance at most `q / N`.
+
+## References
+
+* [D. Boneh, V. Shoup, *A Graduate Course in Applied Cryptography*,
+  Version 0.6][BonehShoup2023], Section 3.11.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Probability.PMF
+
+/-- The mass of a residue: `⌊N / q⌋` preimages, plus one for the residues below `N mod q`. -/
+private theorem toReal_map_natCast_apply (N q : ℕ) [NeZero N] [NeZero q] (r : ZMod q) :
+    (((PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin N)).map fun x => (x.val : ZMod q)) r).toReal =
+      ((N / q + if r.val < N % q then 1 else 0 : ℕ) : ℝ) / N := by
+  classical
+  rw [PMF.map_apply, tsum_fintype, ENNReal.toReal_sum fun x _ => by
+    split <;> simp [PMF.uniformOfFintype_apply, NeZero.ne N]]
+  have hfilter : (Finset.range N).filter (fun k => ((k : ℕ) : ZMod q) = r) =
+      (Finset.range N).filter (fun k => k ≡ r.val [MOD q]) :=
+    Finset.filter_congr fun k _ => by
+      rw [show ((k : ℕ) : ZMod q) = r ↔ ((k : ℕ) : ZMod q) = ((r.val : ℕ) : ZMod q) by
+        rw [ZMod.natCast_zmod_val], ZMod.natCast_eq_natCast_iff']
+      rfl
+  have hfin : (∑ x : Fin N, if ((x : ℕ) : ZMod q) = r then (1 : ℝ) else 0) =
+      ((N / q + if r.val < N % q then 1 else 0 : ℕ) : ℝ) := by
+    have hcount := Nat.count_modEq_card (b := N) (NeZero.pos q) r.val
+    rw [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt (ZMod.val_lt r)] at hcount
+    rw [← hcount, Nat.count_eq_card_filter_range, ← hfilter,
+      Fin.sum_univ_eq_sum_range (fun k => if ((k : ℕ) : ZMod q) = r then (1 : ℝ) else 0) N,
+      Finset.sum_boole]
+  rw [← hfin, Finset.sum_div]
+  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
+  by_cases h : ((x : ℕ) : ZMod q) = r
+  · simp [h, PMF.uniformOfFintype_apply]
+  · simp [h, Ne.symm h]
+
+/-- **A uniform value reduced modulo `q`.** A uniform value below `N`, read in `ZMod q`, is within
+statistical distance `(N mod q) / N` of the uniform distribution on `ZMod q`. -/
+theorem dist_map_natCast_uniformOfFintype_le (N q : ℕ) [NeZero N] [NeZero q] :
+    dist ((PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin N)).map fun x => (x.val : ZMod q))
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod q)) ≤ (N % q : ℕ) / N := by
+  classical
+  have hN : (0 : ℝ) < N := by exact_mod_cast NeZero.pos N
+  have hq : (0 : ℝ) < q := by exact_mod_cast NeZero.pos q
+  have hdiv : (N : ℝ) = q * (N / q : ℕ) + (N % q : ℕ) := by
+    exact_mod_cast (Nat.div_add_mod N q).symm
+  have hterm (r : ZMod q) :
+      |(((PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin N)).map fun x => (x.val : ZMod q)) r).toReal -
+        (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod q) r).toReal| ≤
+        (if r.val < N % q then (1 : ℝ) else 0) / N + (N % q : ℕ) / (q * N) := by
+    rw [toReal_map_natCast_apply, PMF.uniformOfFintype_apply, ZMod.card, ENNReal.toReal_inv,
+      ENNReal.toReal_natCast]
+    have hsplit : ((N / q + if r.val < N % q then 1 else 0 : ℕ) : ℝ) / N - (q : ℝ)⁻¹ =
+        (if r.val < N % q then (1 : ℝ) else 0) / N - (N % q : ℕ) / (q * N) := by
+      split_ifs <;> push_cast <;> field_simp <;> linarith [hdiv]
+    rw [hsplit]
+    have h1 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (if r.val < N % q then (1 : ℝ) else 0) / N := by positivity
+    have h2 : (0 : ℝ) ≤ (N % q : ℕ) / (q * N) := by positivity
+    exact abs_sub_le_iff.mpr ⟨by linarith, by linarith⟩
+  have hcount : (∑ r : ZMod q, if r.val < N % q then (1 : ℝ) else 0) ≤ (N % q : ℕ) := by
+    rw [Finset.sum_boole]
+    exact_mod_cast (Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn ZMod.val (t := Finset.range (N % q))
+      (fun r hr => by simpa using hr) (ZMod.val_injective q).injOn).trans
+        (Finset.card_range _).le
+  rw [dist_eq]
+  calc (∑ r, |(((PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin N)).map fun x => (x.val : ZMod q)) r).toReal -
+        (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod q) r).toReal|) / 2
+      ≤ (∑ r : ZMod q, ((if r.val < N % q then (1 : ℝ) else 0) / N +
+          (N % q : ℕ) / (q * N))) / 2 := by

+        rw [Finset.sum_add_distrib, ← Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ,
+          ZMod.card, nsmul_eq_mul]
+    _ ≤ ((N % q : ℕ) / N + q * ((N % q : ℕ) / (q * N))) / 2 := by
+        gcongr
+    _ = (N % q : ℕ) / N := by
+        field_simp
+        ring

+uniform distribution on `ZMod q`. -/
+theorem dist_map_natCast_uniformOfFintype_le_div (N q : ℕ) [NeZero N] [NeZero q] :
+    dist ((PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin N)).map fun x => (x.val : ZMod q))
+      (PMF.uniformOfFintype (ZMod q)) ≤ q / N := by
+  refine (dist_map_natCast_uniformOfFintype_le N q).trans ?_
+  gcongr
+  exact_mod_cast (Nat.mod_lt N (NeZero.pos q)).le

title: perf(tests): evaluate materialized circuits and drop slow ppt searches (#648)

commit 6194624a987d09b1cae9d2c68d68395d9ef02ff1
Author:     Samuel Schlesinger <SamuelSchlesinger@users.noreply.github.com>
AuthorDate: Sat Oct 24 01:35:02 2026 +0000
Commit:     GitHub <noreply@github.com>
CommitDate: Sat Oct 24 01:35:02 2026 +0000

    perf(tests): evaluate materialized circuits and drop slow ppt searches (#648)
    
    The exhaustive `#eval` checks in BatchLookup, Routing, KeyedSort, DuplicateFlags and BatchOr
    spent 90-98% of their time resolving composed wire maps on every evaluation. The new test
    helper `ComplexityTests.CircuitMaterialize` stores each line's wires and the outputs in arrays
    once, and proves `materialize_eq : materialize c = c`. The checks keep every input set, edge
    case and expected message.
    
    In Crypto.ZeroKnowledge, three `ppt` calls each spent about 10 s on a goal that the local
    `hrun` certificate closes by `hrun.map (by fun_prop)`. The definitions, statements and axiom
    guards are unchanged.
    
    Refs #622
    
    
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Dvi6MU29zU9t8zYfeU51sB
    
    Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

+/-

+
+module
+
+public import Complexity.Computability.Circuit.Evaluation
+import Batteries.Data.Vector.Lemmas
+
+/-!
+# Materialized circuits for exhaustive compiled tests
+
+Composition maps every wire of the inner circuit through the outer wiring, so compiled code for
+a deeply composed circuit resolves a chain of wire maps each time it reads a wire. `materialize`
+stores each line's wires and the outputs in arrays once; `materialize_eq` proves the circuit is
+unchanged. Exhaustive `#eval` checks materialize once and then evaluate thousands of inputs.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace ComplexityTests.CircuitMaterialize
+
+open Cslib Cslib.Circuits
+
+universe v
+
+variable {σ : Signature.{v}} {n m : ℕ}
+
+private theorem get_ofFn {α : Type*} {k : ℕ} (f : Fin k → α) : (Vector.ofFn f).get = f :=
+  funext (Vector.get_ofFn f)
+
+/-- Rebuild a program, storing the argument wires of each line in an array. -/
+def materializeProgram : {g : ℕ} → Program σ n g → Program σ n g
+  | _, .empty => .empty
+  | _, .gate p line =>
+    let wires := Vector.ofFn line.wires
+    .gate (materializeProgram p) ⟨line.op, wires.get⟩
+
+@[simp] theorem materializeProgram_eq {g : ℕ} (p : Program σ n g) : materializeProgram p = p := by
+  induction p with
+  | empty => rfl
+  | gate p line ih =>
+    simp only [materializeProgram, ih, get_ofFn]
+
+/-- Rebuild a circuit, storing its line wires and outputs in arrays. -/
+def materialize (c : Circuit σ n m) : Circuit σ n m :=
+  let outputs := Vector.ofFn c.outputs
+  ⟨materializeProgram c.program, outputs.get⟩
+
+@[simp] theorem materialize_eq (c : Circuit σ n m) : materialize c = c := by
+  simp only [materialize, materializeProgram_eq, get_ofFn]
+
+end ComplexityTests.CircuitMaterialize

title: feat(polytime): certify negation and list membership for automation
patch:
commit f64d9638a1fc8c4844aad1aecda48d7c728511f2
Author:     Samuel Giuseppe Schlesinger <sgschlesinger@gmail.com>
AuthorDate: Fri Oct 23 19:17:40 2026 -0400
Commit:     Samuel Schlesinger <SamuelSchlesinger@users.noreply.github.com>
CommitDate: Sat Oct 24 00:11:32 2026 +0000

    feat(polytime): certify negation and list membership for automation
    
    `fun_prop` certified `decide` of conjunctions, disjunctions, equalities and disequalities, but not
    of negations or of membership in a computed list. A reduction map written as on paper, such as
    the graph complement keeping the pairs with `(u, v) ∉ G.2`, therefore defeated both `fun_prop`
    and `polytime`, and `Graph.computableTidilyInPolyTime_compl` needed a hand-proved rewrite into
    Boolean scans first.
    
    Add `decide_not` and `decide_mem` in a narrow module, `PolyTime/Membership`, imported by
    `Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime`. Membership is decided by an `anyWithInput` scan for an equal
    element. With them, the complement's certificate is `unfold compl encGraph; fun_prop`, and
    `Clique.mem_NP` proves its verifier's cost with `fun_prop` instead of `.of_tidy`. Checked
    examples cover membership, a filter by non-membership and the complement map, all plain and by
    `polytime`.
    
    Refs #585
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Dvi6MU29zU9t8zYfeU51sB

diff --git a/Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Membership.lean b/Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Membership.lean
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..dc8aca2f
--- /dev/null
+++ b/Complexity/Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Complexity/PolyTime/Membership.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.List
+
+/-!
+# Polynomial-time membership tests
+
+Reduction maps and verifiers test membership as they are written on paper, for example keeping
+the pairs `(u, v)` with `(u, v) ∉ G.2`. `fun_prop` already certifies `decide` of conjunctions,
+disjunctions, equalities and disequalities
+(`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.decide_and` and its neighbours). This file adds
+negation and membership of a computed value in a computed list, so such tests need no rewriting
+into Boolean operations before `fun_prop` or `polytime` runs. Membership is decided by scanning
+the list for an equal element (`Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.anyWithInput`).
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.decide_not`: negating a decided proposition.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.decide_mem`: membership in a computed list.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+
+variable {γ α : Type} {encIn : γ ↪ List Bool} {encA : α ↪ List Bool}
+
+/-- Negation of an efficiently decidable proposition uses the standard Boolean encoding. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem decide_not {p : γ → Prop} [∀ x, Decidable (p x)]
+    (h : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => decide (p x)) encIn encBool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => decide ¬p x) encIn encBool := by
+  simpa only [Function.comp_def, _root_.decide_not] using bool_not.comp h
+
+/-- Membership of a computed value in a computed list is decided by scanning the list for an equal
+element. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem decide_mem {list : γ → List α} {value : γ → α} [∀ x, Decidable (value x ∈ list x)]
+    (hlist : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime list encIn (encList encA))
+    (hvalue : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime value encIn encA) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => decide (value x ∈ list x)) encIn encBool := by
+  classical
+  have hscan (x : γ) : decide (value x ∈ list x) = (list x).any fun b => decide (b = value x) := by
+    rw [Bool.eq_iff_iff, decide_eq_true_eq, List.any_eq_true]
+    exact ⟨fun h => ⟨_, h, decide_eq_true rfl⟩, fun ⟨b, hb, e⟩ => of_decide_eq_true e ▸ hb⟩
+  simp only [hscan]
+  exact anyWithInput (test := fun x b => decide (b = value x)) hlist
+    (decide_eq' (snd _ _) (hvalue.comp (fst _ _)))
+
+end Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime

+    (encPair (encList encNat) (encList (encPair encNat encNat)))
+    (encList (encPair encNat encNat)) := by

+

+
+There is deliberately no `fun_prop` transition from plain to tidy: registering it together with
+the reverse transition would create a search cycle. In particular, a tidy goal such as
+`ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => [f a]) enc (encList encIntBin)` cannot use a plain certificate
+for `f` directly. This occurs when constructing singleton target lists in `WPP/Robustness.lean`
+and `WPP/TwoSided.lean`. Unbounded `fun_prop` can exhaust its heartbeat budget while looking for
+another certificate. Restate the needed hypothesis with `have hf := hf.tidy` before `fun_prop`,
+or use `polytime` from `Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime`, which prepares plain hypotheses for tidy
+search. When trying composition speculatively, use
+`fun_prop (config := { maxSteps := 32 })` to bound that attempt, then supply a certificate or
+switch tactics. This is a search budget, not a guarantee that every unsuccessful search is cheap.
+
+`selectVerifier`, `andVerifier` and `orVerifier` have plain `fun_prop` rules in
+`Classes/SharpP/Combinators.lean`, so plain verifier hypotheses need no manual `.tidy` conversion
+for a plain goal. Their tidy rules remain available for proofs using the tidy calculus.
+
+For a tidy certificate covering a whole composite whose intermediate encoding is difficult to
+infer, prefer `polytime`, or convert the hypotheses with `.tidy` and use
+`.of_tidy (by fun_prop)`. Two representative cases are the binary threshold
+`fun a => 3 * (k a * 2 ^ q.eval (enc a).length)` in `inter_mem_SBP_of_mem_BPP` (where `k` uses
+`encNat`, while the exponent uses `encUnary`), and the input-dependent `sharpTest` verifier in
+`Classes/Toda.lean`. `polytime` proves both directly from plain hypotheses. The mixed-encoding
+examples and the bounded singleton failure are checked in `ComplexityTests/PolyTimeMixes.lean`.
+
 Upstream `Turing.MultiTapeTM.DecidableInTimeAndSpace` decides a problem through its Boolean
 indicator. `Turing.MultiTapeTM.decidableInTimeAndSpace_iff` restates it for any Boolean function
 deciding membership, the form used by the classes in `Cslib.Complexity`.

+++ b/ComplexityTests.lean
@@ -307,6 +307,7 @@ import ComplexityTests.Parameterized

new file mode 100644
index 00000000..fd4cc3a8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/ComplexityTests/PolyTimeMixes.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+import Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime
+import Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Classes.SharpP.Combinators
+import Complexity.Computability.Complexity.Classes.Toda.Counting
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Int.Binary
+
+/-! Plain/tidy automation boundaries from #558: bounded failure, verifier rules, the SBP
+binary threshold and Toda's input-dependent counting verifier. -/
+
+namespace ComplexityTests.PolyTimeMixes
+
+open Cslib Cslib.Complexity Turing.MultiTapeTM
+variable {α : Type} {enc : α ↪ List Bool}
+
+set_option maxHeartbeats 2000 in
+-- Check that a bounded failed attempt and the explicit certificate fit a small heartbeat budget.
+/-- The WPP singleton target: bound a failed tidy search before explicitly preparing the plain
+hypothesis. The default search on this shape can run to its heartbeat limit. -/
+example {f : α → ℤ} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f enc encIntBin) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => [f a]) enc (encList encIntBin) := by
+  fail_if_success fun_prop (config := { maxSteps := 32 })
+  have hf := hf.tidy
+  fun_prop
+
+/-- `polytime` prepares the same plain hypothesis without a manual conversion. -/
+example {f : α → ℤ} (hf : ComputableInPolyTime f enc encIntBin) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => [f a]) enc (encList encIntBin) := by polytime
+
+/-- Before: prepare each verifier for the existing tidy rule, then convert its result. -/
+example {k : α → ℕ} {V W : α × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hk : ComputableInPolyTime k enc encUnary)
+    (hV : ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool)
+    (hW : ComputableInPolyTime W (encPair enc encBits) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (andVerifier k V W) (encPair enc encBits) encBool :=
+  .of_tidy (computableTidilyInPolyTime_andVerifier hk.tidy hV.tidy hW.tidy)
+
+/-- After: the plain rule lets `fun_prop` use the plain hypotheses directly. -/
+example {k : α → ℕ} {V W : α × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hk : ComputableInPolyTime k enc encUnary)
+    (hV : ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool)
+    (hW : ComputableInPolyTime W (encPair enc encBits) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (andVerifier k V W) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by fun_prop
+
+example {k : α → ℕ} {V W : α × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hk : ComputableInPolyTime k enc encUnary)
+    (hV : ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool)
+    (hW : ComputableInPolyTime W (encPair enc encBits) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (orVerifier k V W) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by fun_prop
+
+example {V W : α × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hV : ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool)
+    (hW : ComputableInPolyTime W (encPair enc encBits) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (selectVerifier V W) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by fun_prop
+
+/-- The plain rules still accept a mixture of plain and tidy verifier certificates. -/
+example {V W : α × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hV : ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair enc encBits) encBool)
+    (hW : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime W (encPair enc encBits) encBool) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (selectVerifier V W) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by fun_prop
+
+/-- Before: convert the binary input certificate, search tidily, and convert the result back. -/
+example {k : α → ℕ} (hk : ComputableInPolyTime k enc encNat) (q : Polynomial ℕ) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => 3 * (k a * 2 ^ q.eval (enc a).length)) enc encNat := by
+  have hk := hk.tidy
+  exact .of_tidy (by fun_prop)
+
+/-- The SBP threshold mixes binary `k`, unary exponents, multiplication and exponentiation. -/
+example {k : α → ℕ} (hk : ComputableInPolyTime k enc encNat) (q : Polynomial ℕ) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun a => 3 * (k a * 2 ^ q.eval (enc a).length)) enc encNat := by
+  polytime
+
+/-- Toda's `sharpTest` carries the original input through two witness arguments. -/
+example {V : (α × List Bool) × List Bool → Bool}
+    (hV : ComputableInPolyTime V (encPair (encPair enc encBits) encBits) encBool)
+    (R Z : Polynomial ℕ) :
+    ComputableInPolyTime (fun x : α × List Bool =>
+      Toda.sharpTest (fun r z => V ((x.1, r), z)) (R.eval (enc x.1).length)
+        (Z.eval (enc x.1).length) x.2) (encPair enc encBits) encBool := by
+  polytime
+
+end ComplexityTests.PolyTimeMixes

    Mathlib's linter.style.maxHeartbeats, enforced by lake test with --wfail,

    check_hygiene.py only looked at the preceding lines. A file could not satisfy
    both; #567 was ejected from the merge queue for following the linter.

+      encBool) :

+

commit b1832cfd0aaa562e8d3cf0c965ab4ae9fac4aab6
Author:     Samuel Schlesinger <SamuelSchlesinger@users.noreply.github.com>
AuthorDate: Thu Oct 22 01:56:09 2026 -0400
Commit:     GitHub <noreply@github.com>
CommitDate: Thu Oct 22 01:56:09 2026 -0400

    refactor(logics,classes): deduplicate FullTuple/Encoding, consolidate co-class helpers, and sync docs (#346)
    
    - Move FullTupleInterpretation.toDomainInterpretation, its rank/cardinality/admissibility lemmas, and encodedMap_toDomainInterpretation to FullTuple/Encoding.lean (re-exported by FullTuple/DomainInterpretation.lean) and derive wellFormed_encodedMap_iff and length_encStructure_encodedMap from DomainInterpretation.
    - Add generic complement-class helpers (ManyOneReducibleBy.mem_compl, PolyTimeReducible.mem_compl, compl_union_mem, compl_inter_mem, forall_mem_compl_iff, exists_forall_mem_compl_iff) in Reduction/ManyOne.lean and Reduction.lean, simplifying co* closure and characterization proofs across NP/Closure, NP/Witness, CeqP, ModP, ModP/GapP, UP, DP, and BooleanHierarchy.
    - Synchronize ROADMAP.md and UPSTREAM.md with the completed consolidation changes from #314-#317.
    
    Closes #338
    
    Co-authored-by: Gemini 2.5 Pro <noreply@google.com>
