+/-- If reductions preserve membership from `D` to `C`, they also preserve membership in the
+complement classes `{B | Bᶜ ∈ D}` and `{A | Aᶜ ∈ C}`. -/
+theorem mem_compl {C : Set (Set α)} {D : Set (Set β)}
+    (hCD : ∀ {A : Set α} {B : Set β}, ManyOneReducibleBy Good A B → B ∈ D → A ∈ C)
+    (h : ManyOneReducibleBy Good A B) (hB : Bᶜ ∈ D) : Aᶜ ∈ C :=
+  hCD h.compl hB
+
 /-- **Transfer along partial decodings.** Suppose representations `α'` and `β'` partially decode
 to `α` and `β`, and every admissible map `f` is simulated by an admissible map `F` of
 representations, in that `F` decodes to `f` on decodable inputs and to nothing elsewhere. Then a
@@ -126,6 +137,33 @@ theorem lift {α' : Type w} {β' : Type x} {Good' : (α' → β') → Prop}
 
 end ManyOneReducibleBy
 
+/-! ### Complement-class helpers -/
+
+/-- De Morgan dual: if `C` is closed under intersection, `{A | Aᶜ ∈ C}` is closed under union. -/
+theorem compl_union_mem {C : Set (Set α)} {A B : Set α}
+    (hinter : ∀ {A B : Set α}, A ∈ C → B ∈ C → A ∩ B ∈ C)
+    (hA : Aᶜ ∈ C) (hB : Bᶜ ∈ C) : (A ∪ B)ᶜ ∈ C :=
+  Set.compl_union A B ▸ hinter hA hB
+
+/-- De Morgan dual: if `C` is closed under union, `{A | Aᶜ ∈ C}` is closed under intersection. -/
+theorem compl_inter_mem {C : Set (Set α)} {A B : Set α}
+    (hunion : ∀ {A B : Set α}, A ∈ C → B ∈ C → A ∪ B ∈ C)
+    (hA : Aᶜ ∈ C) (hB : Bᶜ ∈ C) : (A ∩ B)ᶜ ∈ C :=
+  Set.compl_inter A B ▸ hunion hA hB
+
+/-- Negating the pointwise membership condition characterizes the complement `Aᶜ`. -/
+theorem forall_mem_compl_iff {P Q : α → Prop} (hPQ : ∀ a, ¬ P a ↔ Q a) :
+    (∀ a, a ∈ Aᶜ ↔ P a) ↔ ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ Q a :=
+  ⟨fun h a => by simpa [← hPQ a] using not_congr (h a),
+    fun h a => by simpa [← hPQ a] using not_congr (h a)⟩
+
+/-- Negating the pointwise membership condition in an existential class characterization gives
+the characterization of the complement class `{A | Aᶜ ∈ C}`. -/
+theorem exists_forall_mem_compl_iff {ι : Type w} {F : Set ι} {P Q : ι → α → Prop}
+    (hPQ : ∀ f a, ¬ P f a ↔ Q f a) :
+    (∃ f ∈ F, ∀ a, a ∈ Aᶜ ↔ P f a) ↔ ∃ f ∈ F, ∀ a, a ∈ A ↔ Q f a :=
+  exists_congr fun f => and_congr_right' (forall_mem_compl_iff (hPQ f))
+
 /-! ### Hardness and completeness -/
 
 section Hardness

 /-!
 # Encoding canonical full-tuple interpretations
 
-A valid source of size at least two is mapped to the full tuple universe, numbered by
-`lexRank`. Only the target input relations are serialized; canonical order, BIT and constants
-are computed from the target cardinality. Relation tables keep `tupleIndex` order across their
-arguments. Malformed sources and sizes zero and one map to a fixed malformed target.
+A full-tuple interpretation is the ordered interpretation whose domain formula is `true`
+(`FullTupleInterpretation.toDomainInterpretation`), with ranks given by lexicographic rank on all
+tuples. A valid source of size at least two is mapped to the full tuple universe, numbered by
+`lexRank`, agreeing with `DomainInterpretation.encodedMap`
+(`FullTupleInterpretation.encodedMap_toDomainInterpretation`). Only the target input relations are
+serialized; canonical order, BIT and constants are computed from the target cardinality. Relation
+tables keep `tupleIndex` order across their arguments. Malformed sources and sizes zero and one map
+to a fixed malformed target.
 
 ## Main definitions
 
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.Ordered.FullTupleInterpretation.toDomainInterpretation`: embedding as an
+  interpretation with domain formula `⊤`.
 * `Cslib.Logic.FO.Ordered.FullTupleInterpretation.encodedMap`: the total map on parsed instances.
 
 ## Main results
 
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.Ordered.FullTupleInterpretation.unrank_toDomainInterpretation`: ranks are
+  lexicographic ranks.
+* `Cslib.Logic.FO.Ordered.FullTupleInterpretation.encodedMap_toDomainInterpretation`: agreement
+  with `DomainInterpretation.encodedMap`.

Commit:     karnseth <karnseth@gmail.com>
CommitDate: Sun Oct 18 20:05:00 2026 -0400

    test(Circuit/Rational): rational hitting regression tests
    
    Concrete formulas and node counts, explicit Admissible/Nonzero witnesses on
    1 x 1 and 2 x 2 rational matrices (the commutator x0 x1 - x1 x0 is nonzero
    but vanishes on 1 x 1 matrices), non-admissible inverses via
    admissible_inv_iff_nonzero, two-sided inverse evaluation, evalMatrix?
    checks, the s = 0 and n = 0 boundary statements, kernel-computed list
    dimensions, nonvacuity of hittingList_hits (including that the list for the
    commutator has dimension at least 2), and axiom guards for the headline
    theorems.

@@ -0,0 +1,285 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+import Complexity.Computability.Circuit.Rational
+
+/-!
+# Rational hitting list regression tests
+
+Concrete formulas, their node counts, explicit admissibility and nonzeroness witnesses on `1 × 1`
+and `2 × 2` rational matrices, formulas outside the domain, exact matrix evaluation, the boundary
+cases `s = 0` and `n = 0`, and nonvacuity checks for the headline theorems. The hitting list itself
+is astronomically long and is never evaluated; only its dimension is computed, by the kernel.
+-/
+
+namespace ComplexityTests.RationalHitting
+
+open Cslib.Circuits.Rational
+
+/-! ### Concrete formulas -/
+
+/-- The commutator `x₀ x₁ - x₁ x₀`, written with the constant `-1`. -/
+def commutator : Formula 2 :=
+  .add (.mul (.var 0) (.var 1)) (.mul (.const (-1)) (.mul (.var 1) (.var 0)))
+
+/-- The formula `x₀ - x₀`, identically zero wherever defined. -/
+def cancel : Formula 1 := .add (.var 0) (.mul (.const (-1)) (.var 0))
+
+example : (Formula.var 0 : Formula 1).nodeCount = 1 := by simp
+example : (Formula.inv (.const 0) : Formula 1).nodeCount = 2 := by simp
+example : commutator.nodeCount = 9 := by simp [commutator]
+example : cancel.nodeCount = 5 := by simp [cancel]
+
+/-- info: [9, 5] -/
+#guard_msgs in
+#eval [commutator.nodeCount, cancel.nodeCount]
+
+-- The generic formula decidable equality distinguishes the order of the factors.
+example : (Formula.mul (.var 0) (.var 1) : Formula 2) ≠ .mul (.var 1) (.var 0) := by decide
+example : (Formula.var 0 : Formula 2) ≠ .var 1 := by decide
+example : (Formula.const 1 : Formula 2) ≠ .const 2 := by decide
+example : commutator = commutator := by decide
+
+/-! ### Evaluation with a genuine two-sided inverse -/
+
+-- In `ℚ`, the inverse of `2` is `1 / 2`, and the inverse of `0` is undefined, not `0`.
+example : (Formula.inv (.var 0) : Formula 1).Eval (RingHom.id ℚ) ![2] (1 / 2) :=
+  Formula.Eval.inv (a := 2) (Formula.Eval.var 0) (by norm_num) (by norm_num)
+
+example : ¬ ∃ v, (Formula.inv (.var 0) : Formula 1).Eval (RingHom.id ℚ) ![0] v := by
+  rintro ⟨v, a, ha, h, -⟩
+  simp only [Formula.eval_var_iff, Matrix.cons_val_zero] at ha
+  simp [ha] at h
+
+/-- An upper unitriangular `2 × 2` matrix. -/
+def unipotent : Mat 2 := !![1, 1; 0, 1]
+
+/-- The inverse of `unipotent`. -/
+def unipotentInv : Mat 2 := !![1, -1; 0, 1]
+
+theorem unipotent_mul : unipotent * unipotentInv = 1 := by
+  simp [unipotent, unipotentInv, Matrix.one_fin_two]
+
+theorem unipotentInv_mul : unipotentInv * unipotent = 1 := by
+  simp [unipotent, unipotentInv, Matrix.one_fin_two]
+
+theorem evaluates_inv_unipotent :
+    Evaluates (.inv (.var 0) : Formula 1) ![unipotent] unipotentInv :=
+  Formula.Eval.inv (Formula.Eval.var 0) unipotent_mul unipotentInv_mul
+
+-- The executable evaluator agrees, by the soundness and completeness theorem.
+example : (Formula.inv (.var 0) : Formula 1).evalMatrix? ![unipotent] = some unipotentInv :=
+  (Formula.evalMatrix?_eq_some_iff _ _ _).mpr evaluates_inv_unipotent
+
+-- Compiled evaluation on `1 × 1` and `2 × 2` matrices.
+/-- info: [true, true, true, true, true, true] -/
+#guard_msgs in
+#eval [
+  decide ((Formula.inv (.var 0) : Formula 1).evalMatrix? ![unipotent] = some unipotentInv),
+  decide ((Formula.inv (.var 0) : Formula 1).evalMatrix? ![!![2]] = some !![1 / 2]),
+  decide ((Formula.inv (.var 0) : Formula 1).evalMatrix? ![!![0]] = none),
+  decide ((Formula.inv (.const 0) : Formula 1).evalMatrix? ![unipotent] = none),
+  decide ((Formula.inv cancel).evalMatrix? ![unipotent] = none),
+  decide (cancel.evalMatrix? ![unipotent] = some 0)]
+
+-- The inverse of a singular constant is undefined, as a proof.
+example (X : Tuple 1 2) : (Formula.inv (.const 0) : Formula 1).evalMatrix? X = none := by
+  simp
+
+/-! ### Admissibility and nonzeroness witnesses -/
+
+theorem nonzero_var : Nonzero (.var 0 : Formula 1) :=
+  ⟨1, one_pos, fun _ => 1, 1, rfl, one_ne_zero⟩
+
+theorem admissible_var : Admissible (.var 0 : Formula 1) := nonzero_var.admissible
+
+/-- The `2 × 2` matrix unit `E₀₁`. -/
+def e01 : Mat 2 := !![0, 1; 0, 0]
+
+/-- The `2 × 2` matrix unit `E₁₀`. -/
+def e10 : Mat 2 := !![0, 0; 1, 0]
+
+theorem evaluates_commutator :
+    Evaluates commutator ![e01, e10] (e01 * e10 + algebraMap ℚ (Mat 2) (-1) * (e10 * e01)) :=
+  .add (.mul (.var 0) (.var 1)) (.mul (.const (-1)) (.mul (.var 1) (.var 0)))
+
+theorem nonzero_commutator : Nonzero commutator := by
+  refine ⟨2, two_pos, ![e01, e10], _, evaluates_commutator, fun h => ?_⟩
+  have h00 := congrFun (congrFun h 0) 0
+  simp [e01, e10, Matrix.algebraMap_eq_diagonal] at h00
+
+/-- On `1 × 1` matrices the commutator vanishes wherever it is defined. -/
+theorem commutator_eq_zero_of_dim_one {d : ℕ} (hd : d = 1) (X : Tuple 2 d) {v : Mat d}
+    (h : Evaluates commutator X v) : v = 0 := by
+  subst hd
+  obtain ⟨_, _, ⟨_, _, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩, ⟨_, _, rfl, ⟨_, _, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩, rfl⟩, rfl⟩ := h
+  ext i j
+  fin_cases i
+  fin_cases j
+  simp [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.algebraMap_eq_diagonal, mul_comm]
+
+-- The commutator is admissible, also on `1 × 1` matrices, but not nonzero there.
+theorem admissible_commutator : Admissible commutator := nonzero_commutator.admissible
+
+/-- The zero constant is admissible but not nonzero. -/
+theorem not_nonzero_const_zero : ¬ Nonzero (.const 0 : Formula 1) := by
+  rintro ⟨d, _, X, v, hv, hne⟩
+  exact hne (by simpa [Evaluates] using hv)
+
+theorem admissible_const_zero : Admissible (.const 0 : Formula 1) :=
+  ⟨1, one_pos, fun _ => 0, _, Formula.Eval.const 0⟩
+
+theorem not_nonzero_cancel : ¬ Nonzero cancel := by
+  rintro ⟨d, _, X, v, hv, hne⟩
+  obtain ⟨_, _, rfl, ⟨_, _, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩, rfl⟩ := hv
+  exact hne (by simp)
+
+-- The inverse of the zero constant and of an identically zero formula are not admissible.
+theorem not_admissible_inv_const_zero : ¬ Admissible (.inv (.const 0) : Formula 1) :=
+  fun h => not_nonzero_const_zero ((admissible_inv_iff_nonzero _).mp h)
+
+theorem not_admissible_inv_cancel : ¬ Admissible (.inv cancel) :=
+  fun h => not_nonzero_cancel ((admissible_inv_iff_nonzero _).mp h)
+
+theorem admissible_inv_var : Admissible (.inv (.var 0) : Formula 1) :=
+  (admissible_inv_iff_nonzero _).mpr nonzero_var
+
+-- The executable tests give the expected answers, by their correctness theorems.
+example : (Formula.var 0 : Formula 1).admissible? = true :=
+  (Formula.admissible?_eq_true_iff _).mpr admissible_var
+example : (Formula.const 0 : Formula 1).admissible? = true :=
+  (Formula.admissible?_eq_true_iff _).mpr admissible_const_zero
+example : (Formula.const 0 : Formula 1).nonzero? = false :=
+  Bool.eq_false_iff.mpr fun h => not_nonzero_const_zero ((Formula.nonzero?_eq_true_iff _).mp h)
+example : (Formula.inv cancel).admissible? = false :=
+  Bool.eq_false_iff.mpr fun h =>
+    not_admissible_inv_cancel ((Formula.admissible?_eq_true_iff _).mp h)
+example : commutator.nonzero? = true := (Formula.nonzero?_eq_true_iff _).mpr nonzero_commutator
+
+example : Decidable (Admissible commutator) := inferInstance
+example : Decidable (Nonzero (.inv cancel)) := inferInstance
+
+-- A small-dimension witness exists for every admissible formula.
+example : ∃ d, 0 < d ∧ d ≤ 256 * (2 + 9 + 3) ^ 10 ∧
+    ∃ (X : Tuple 2 d) (v : Mat d), Evaluates commutator X v := by
+  simpa [commutator] using admissible_commutator.exists_dimension_le
+
+/-! ### Boundary cases -/
+
+-- `s = 0`: every list hits, as every formula has a node.
+example (n : ℕ) (H : Output n) : Hits 0 H := hits_zero H
+example (n : ℕ) : Hits 0 (hittingList n 0) := hittingList_hits n 0
+
+-- `n = 0`: the zero-variable statements carry no hypothesis.
+example (s : ℕ) : Hits s (hittingList 0 s) := hittingList_hits 0 s
+example (s : ℕ) : (hittingList 0 s).dimension ≤ 256 * (s + 1) ^ 10 := by
+  simpa using hittingList_dimension_le 0 s
+example (s : ℕ) : (encodeOutput (hittingList 0 s)).length ≤
+    PolynomialBounds.outputConstant * (s + 1) ^ 104 := by
+  simpa using hittingList_encoding_length_le 0 s
+
+theorem nonzero_const_one : Nonzero (.const 1 : Formula 0) :=
+  ⟨1, one_pos, Fin.elim0, 1, by simp [Evaluates], one_ne_zero⟩
+
+-- The zero-variable list is nonempty: it hits the constant `1`.
+example : (hittingList 0 1).tuples ≠ [] := by
+  obtain ⟨X, hX, -⟩ :=
+    hittingList_hits 0 1 (.const 1) (by simp) nonzero_const_one.admissible nonzero_const_one
+  exact List.ne_nil_of_mem hX
+
+/-! ### The list's dimension, computed by the kernel -/
+
+example (n s : ℕ) : (hittingList n s).dimension =
+    2 ^ (Parameters.exponent n s + 1) * 2 ^ Parameters.exponent n s := rfl
+
+example : (hittingList 0 0).dimension = 8 := by decide
+example : (hittingList 1 1).dimension = 32768 := by decide
+
+/-! ### Nonvacuity of the headline theorems -/
+
+-- The hypotheses of the hitting property are satisfiable, and the list is nonempty.
+example : ∃ X ∈ (hittingList 1 1).tuples, ∃ v, Evaluates (.var 0) X v ∧ IsUnit v :=
+  hittingList_hits 1 1 (.var 0) (by simp) admissible_var nonzero_var
+
+-- Positive dimension is not enough: the list for the commutator must use dimension at least 2.
+example : 2 ≤ (hittingList 2 9).dimension := by
+  obtain ⟨X, -, v, hv, hu⟩ := hittingList_hits 2 9 commutator (by simp [commutator])
+    admissible_commutator nonzero_commutator
+  by_contra h
+  have hd : (hittingList 2 9).dimension = 1 := by
+    have := (hittingList 2 9).dimension_pos
+    omega
+  have hv0 := commutator_eq_zero_of_dim_one hd X hv
+  subst hv0
+  have : Nonempty (Fin (hittingList 2 9).dimension) := ⟨⟨0, by omega⟩⟩
+  exact not_isUnit_zero hu
+
+/-! ### Axioms of the headline theorems -/
+
+/--
+info: 'Cslib.Circuits.Rational.hits_zero' depends on axioms:
+[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+-/
+#guard_msgs (whitespace := lax) in
+#print axioms Cslib.Circuits.Rational.hits_zero
+
+/--
+info: 'Cslib.Circuits.Rational.hittingList_hits' depends on axioms:
+[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+-/
+#guard_msgs (whitespace := lax) in
+#print axioms Cslib.Circuits.Rational.hittingList_hits
+
+/--
+info: 'Cslib.Circuits.Rational.hittingList_dimension_le' depends on axioms:
+[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+-/
+#guard_msgs (whitespace := lax) in
+#print axioms Cslib.Circuits.Rational.hittingList_dimension_le
+
+/--
+info: 'Cslib.Circuits.Rational.hittingList_encoding_length_le' depends on axioms:
+[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+-/
+#guard_msgs (whitespace := lax) in
+#print axioms Cslib.Circuits.Rational.hittingList_encoding_length_le
+
+/--
+info: 'Cslib.Circuits.Rational.admissible_inv_iff_nonzero' depends on axioms:
+[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+-/
+#guard_msgs (whitespace := lax) in
+#print axioms Cslib.Circuits.Rational.admissible_inv_iff_nonzero
+
+/--
+info: 'Cslib.Circuits.Rational.Admissible.exists_dimension_le' depends on axioms:
+[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+-/
+#guard_msgs (whitespace := lax) in
+#print axioms Cslib.Circuits.Rational.Admissible.exists_dimension_le
+
+/--
+info: 'Cslib.Circuits.Rational.Formula.admissible?_eq_true_iff' depends on axioms:
+[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+-/
+#guard_msgs (whitespace := lax) in
+#print axioms Cslib.Circuits.Rational.Formula.admissible?_eq_true_iff
+
+/--
+info: 'Cslib.Circuits.Rational.Formula.nonzero?_eq_true_iff' depends on axioms:
+[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
+-/
+#guard_msgs (whitespace := lax) in

    Add hits_zero (every list hits the formulas with at most 0 nodes, as every
    formula has a node) and drop the hypothesis 1 <= s from hittingList_hits.
    Prove Parameters.polynomial_H for all n, bounding s + 2 by 2 * (n + s + 1);
    the grid constant becomes 49153 (was 24577, valid only for n >= 1), and
    logConstant, list_length_bound and outputConstant follow. The hypothesis
    1 <= n is dropped from list_length_bound, logarithmic_bound,
    list_output_bound, exact_output, algebraic_generator and
    hittingList_encoding_length_le.

+private abbrev TaggedRowsInput := (List (List Bool) × List Bool) × List (List Bool)
+private abbrev taggedRowsInputEncoding :=
+  encPair (encPair (encList encBits) encBits) (encList encBits)
+
+private def tagRows (p : TaggedRowsInput) : List (List Bool) :=
+  p.1.1.foldl (fun rows row => (row ++ p.1.2) :: rows) p.2
+
+-- Each copied row is bounded by the actual source list, including with an arbitrary initial state.
+-- No fixed additive bound would hold for all possible rows outside that list.
+private theorem tagRows_polytime :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime tagRows taggedRowsInputEncoding (encList encBits) := by
+  unfold tagRows taggedRowsInputEncoding
+  refine ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.foldlWith_of_bounded_growth (encA := encBits)
+    (par := fun p : TaggedRowsInput => p.1.2)
+    (step := fun tag rows row => (row ++ tag) :: rows)
+    (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
+    (growth := fun p => 2 * ((encList encBits p.1.1).length + p.1.2.length) + 1)
+    (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.polyBounded (by fun_prop)) ?_
+  intro p state row hrow
+  have hsize := SizedListEncoding.length_elem_le
+    (encA := encBits) (encL := encList encBits) p.1.1 row hrow
+  simp only [encList_cons, List.length_append, length_frame, encBits_apply] at hsize ⊢
+  lia
+
+-- A downstream traversal consumes the accumulated rows through the ordinary list API.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p => (tagRows p).map List.reverse)
+    taggedRowsInputEncoding (encList encBits) := by
+  have h := tagRows_polytime
+  polytime
+
+example : tagRows (([], [true]), [[false]]) = [[false]] := rfl
+example : tagRows (([[false], [false]], [true]), [[true]]) =
+    [[false, true], [false, true], [true]] := by decide
+
+private def skipCopies (p : (Bool × ℕ) × List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  (List.replicate p.1.2 p.1.1).foldl
+    (fun state bit => if bit = p.1.1 then state else state ++ state) p.2
+
+-- Prefix membership, rather than a global growth claim, rules out the doubling branch.
+private theorem skipCopies_spec :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime skipCopies (encPair (encPair encBool encUnary) encBits) encBits ∧
+      ∀ p, skipCopies p = p.2 := by
+  unfold skipCopies
+  refine ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.foldlWith_spec (encA := encBool) (encL := encList encBool)
+    (par := fun p : (Bool × ℕ) × List Bool => p.1.1)
+    (step := fun tag state bit => if bit = tag then state else state ++ state)
+    (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
+    (fun p _ state => state = p.2) (by simp) ?_
+    (size := fun p => p.2.length) (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.polyBounded (by fun_prop)) ?_
+  · intro p consumed state bit hprefix hstate
+    have hbit : bit = p.1.1 := List.eq_of_mem_replicate (hprefix.subset (by simp))
+    simp [hbit, hstate]
+  · intro p consumed state _ hstate
+    simp [hstate]
+
+example : skipCopies ((true, 3), [true, false]) = [true, false] := skipCopies_spec.2 _
+
 -- A standard outer operation leaves the fold's meaningful step and growth contracts usable.
 example (step : List Bool → Bool → List Bool) (growth : ℕ)
     (hstep : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : List Bool × Bool => step pair.1 pair.2)

@@ -0,0 +1,156 @@
+/-

+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+import Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime
+
+/-!
+# Encoding inference and input-dependent loop contracts
+
+Fixed scans need no encoding of their indices. Runtime scans retain joint certificates, while
+loop bounds charge the full framed state on every reachable iteration.
+-/
+
+namespace ComplexityTests.PolyTimeContracts
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+-- Fixed lists may contain higher-universe objects for which no bit encoding is supplied.
+example {ι : Type 1} (indices : List ι) (test : List Bool → ι → Bool)
+    (htest : ∀ i ∈ indices,
+      ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun word => test word i) encBits encBool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun word => indices.all (test word)) encBits encBool := by
+  fun_prop
+
+example {ι : Type 1} (indices : List ι) (test : List Bool → ι → Bool)
+    (htest : ∀ i ∈ indices,
+      ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun word => test word i) encBits encBool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun word => indices.any fun i => test word i)
+      encBits encBool := by
+  polytime
+
+-- No callback certificate is needed when there are no indices.
+example (test : List Bool → Fin 0 → Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun word => ([] : List (Fin 0)).all (test word))
+      encBits encBool := by
+  exact ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.allConst [] (by simp)
+
+-- The same runtime scan supports unrelated element representations.
+example {α β : Type} (input : α ↪ List Bool) (element : β ↪ List Bool)
+    (values : α → List β) (test : α × β → Bool)
+    (hvalues : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime values input (encList element))
+    (htest : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime test (encPair input element) encBool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun x => let entries := values x; entries.all fun value => test (x, value))
+      input encBool := by
+  fail_if_success (clear hvalues; polytime)
+  fail_if_success (clear htest; polytime)
+  polytime
+
+example {α β : Type} (input : α ↪ List Bool) (element : β ↪ List Bool)
+    (values : α → List β) (test : α × β → Bool)
+    (hvalues : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime values input (encList element))
+    (htest : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime test (encPair input element) encBool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => (values x).any fun value => test (x, value))
+      input encBool := by
+  polytime
+
+-- Raw and framed Boolean words use their existing list interfaces.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun p : List Bool × Bool => p.1.all fun bit => bit == p.2)
+    (encPair encBits encBool) encBool := by polytime
+
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun p : List Bool × Bool => p.1.all (fun bit => bit == p.2))
+    (encPair (encList encBool) encBool) encBool := by polytime
+
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun p : List ℕ × ℕ => p.1.any fun n => n == p.2)
+    (encPair (encList encNat) encNat) encBool := by polytime
+
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun p : List ℕ × ℕ => p.1.any fun n => n == p.2)
+    (encPair (encList encUnary) encUnary) encBool := by polytime
+
+-- Separate certificates at each fixed index give no uniform runtime-index certificate.
+example (test : List Bool → ℕ → Bool)
+    (_hfixed : ∀ n, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun word => test word n) encBits encBool) :
+    True := by
+  fail_if_success
+    have : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+        (fun word => (List.range word.length).all (test word)) encBits encBool := by polytime
+  trivial
+
+-- An arbitrary mathematical bound need not have a computation certificate.
+example {α β : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {stateEncoding : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {initial : α → β} {step : β → β} {count bound : α → ℕ}
+    (hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime count input encUnary)
+    (hinitial : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime initial input stateEncoding)
+    (hstep : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime step stateEncoding stateEncoding)
+    (invariant : α → ℕ → β → Prop)
+    (hbase : ∀ x, invariant x 0 (initial x))
+    (hpreserve : ∀ x i state, i < count x → invariant x i state →
+      invariant x (i + 1) (step state))
+    (hsize : PolyBounded (fun x => (input x).length) bound)
+    (hbound : ∀ x i state, i ≤ count x → invariant x i state →
+      (stateEncoding state).length ≤ bound x) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => step^[count x] (initial x)) input stateEncoding := by
+  exact (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.iterate_spec hcount hinitial hstep invariant
+    hbase hpreserve hsize hbound).1
+
+-- Accumulating rows charges each copied row and every outer list frame.
+private def repeatRows (p : List Bool × ℕ) : List (List Bool) :=
+  (fun rows => p.1 :: rows)^[p.2] []
+
+private theorem repeatRows_spec :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime repeatRows (encPair encBits encUnary) (encList encBits) ∧
+      ∀ p, (repeatRows p).length = p.2 ∧ ∀ row ∈ repeatRows p, row = p.1 := by
+  unfold repeatRows
+  refine ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.iterateWith_spec (par := Prod.fst)
+    (count := Prod.snd) (init := fun _ => []) (step := List.cons)
+    (by polytime) (by polytime) (by polytime) (by polytime)
+    (invariant := fun p i rows => rows.length = i ∧ ∀ row ∈ rows, row = p.1)
+    (by simp) ?_ (size := fun p => p.2 * (2 * p.1.length + 1)) ?_ ?_
+  · intro p i rows _ h
+    simpa only [List.length_cons, h.1, List.mem_cons, forall_eq_or_imp, true_and]
+      using h.2
+  · exact ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.polyBounded (by polytime)
+  · intro p i rows hi h
+    calc
+      (encList encBits rows).length ≤ rows.length * (2 * p.1.length + 1) :=
+        length_encList_le encBits rows fun row hrow => by simp [h.2 row hrow]
+      _ ≤ _ := by simpa only [h.1] using Nat.mul_le_mul_right (2 * p.1.length + 1) hi
+
+-- A nested loop composes the row certificate; no intermediate representation is supplied here.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : List Bool × ℕ =>
+    (List.range p.2).flatMap fun n => repeatRows (p.1, n))
+    (encPair encBits encUnary) (encList encBits) := by
+  have h := repeatRows_spec.1
+  polytime
+
+example : repeatRows ([true, false], 0) = [] := rfl
+example : (encList encBits (repeatRows ([true, false], 3))).length = 15 := by decide
+
+-- Growth outside the reachable invariant does not matter; the step still has a uniform certificate.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun n : ℕ => (fun word : List Bool => if word.isEmpty then [] else word ++ word)^[n] [])
+    encUnary encBits := by
+  refine (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.iterate_spec (by polytime) (by polytime) (by polytime)
+    (fun _ _ word => word = []) (by simp) ?_ (.const 0) ?_).1
+  · intros
+    simp_all
+  · intros
+    simp_all
+
+-- A small final projection supplies no bound on a loop's intermediate storage.
+example : True := by
+  fail_if_success
+    have : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun n : ℕ =>
+        ((fun p : ℕ × List Bool =>
+          if p.1 = 0 then (0, []) else (p.1 - 1, p.2 ++ p.2))^[n + 1] (n, [true])).2)
+        encUnary encBits := by polytime
+  trivial
+
+end ComplexityTests.PolyTimeContracts

@@ -9,20 +9,32 @@ module
 
 public import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Nat
 public import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Log
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Iteration
 import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.List
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Nat.Div
+import Complexity.Foundations.Data.Nat.Log
 import Mathlib.Data.Nat.Size
 
 /-!
-# Polynomial-time binary logarithms
+# Polynomial-time logarithms and bounded powers
 
 The base-two logarithm is the binary representation's length minus one, with truncated
 subtraction handling zero. Unary input first uses the certified unary-to-binary conversion.
+Other fixed bases use repeated division with a linear bound on the encoded state. Ceiling
+logarithms follow from floor logarithms; raising a fixed factor to a ceiling logarithm uses the
+existing polynomial bound on logarithmically many multiplications. These latter certificates
+charge unary counter lengths; the bounded-power rule also accepts any caller's encoding with
+a certified unary size function.
 
 ## Main results
 
 * `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.binary_log_two`: compute the logarithm of a
   binary natural, returning its unary value.
 * `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_log_two`: the unary-input version.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_log_const`, `.unary_clog_const`:
+  floor and ceiling logarithms in any fixed base on unary counters.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_pow_clog_const`: a fixed factor raised to
+  a fixed-base ceiling logarithm, with unary output and complete intermediate-size bounds.
 
 ## References
 
@@ -53,4 +65,94 @@ theorem binary_log_two : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (Nat.log 2) encNat encUnary
 theorem unary_log_two : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (Nat.log 2) encUnary encUnary :=
   binary_log_two.comp unary_to_binary
 
+/-- Fixed-base logarithms are polynomial-time on unary counters, including bases zero and one.
+The division loop maintains the logarithm identity and a linear bound on its complete state. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem unary_log_const (base : ℕ) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (Nat.log base) encUnary encUnary := by
+  rcases le_or_gt base 1 with hb | hb
+  · convert (const (encIn := encUnary) (encMid := encUnary) 0) using 1
+    exact funext (Nat.log_of_left_le_one hb)
+  let step (state : ℕ × ℕ) :=
+    if base ≤ state.1 then (state.1 / base, state.2 + 1) else state
+  have hstep : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime step (encPair encUnary encUnary)
+      (encPair encUnary encUnary) := by unfold step; fun_prop
+  obtain ⟨hefficient, hspec⟩ := iterate_spec (count := id) (init := fun n => (n, 0))
+    (encIn := encUnary) id' (by fun_prop) hstep
+    (fun n i state => state.1 ≤ n ∧ state.2 ≤ i ∧
+      (state.1 < base ∨ state.1 + i ≤ n) ∧
+      Nat.log base state.1 + state.2 = Nat.log base n)
+    (fun _ => by simp) (fun n i state _ h => by
+      dsimp only [step]
+      split
+      · rename_i htest
+        have hdrop := Nat.div_lt_self (lt_of_lt_of_le (by lia : 0 < base) htest) hb
+        have hprogress : state.1 + i ≤ n := h.2.2.1.resolve_left (by lia)
+        have hlog := Nat.log_of_one_lt_of_le hb htest
+        exact ⟨(Nat.div_le_self _ _).trans h.1, by lia, Or.inr (by lia), by lia⟩
+      · rename_i htest
+        exact ⟨h.1, by lia, Or.inl (by lia), h.2.2.2⟩)
+    (size := fun n => 3 * n + 1) (by fun_prop) (fun _ _ _ hi h => by
+      simp only [length_encPair, encUnary_apply, List.length_replicate]
+      simp only [id_eq] at hi
+      lia)
+  have hresult (n : ℕ) : (step^[n] (n, 0)).2 = Nat.log base n := by
+    have h := hspec n
+    have hsmall : (step^[n] (n, 0)).1 < base := by
+      rcases h.2.2.1 with hsmall | hsmall <;> simp only [id_eq] at * <;> lia
+    simpa only [id_eq, Nat.log_of_lt hsmall, zero_add] using h.2.2.2
+  simpa only [Function.comp_def, id_eq, hresult] using hefficient.snd'
+
+/-- Ceiling logarithms in any fixed base are polynomial-time on unary counters. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem unary_clog_const (base : ℕ) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (Nat.clog base) encUnary encUnary := by
+  rcases le_or_gt base 1 with hb | hb
+  · convert (const (encIn := encUnary) (encMid := encUnary) 0) using 1
+    exact funext (Nat.clog_of_left_le_one hb)
+  have heq (n : ℕ) : Nat.clog base n =
+      if n ≤ 1 then 0 else Nat.log base (n - 1) + 1 := by
+    split
+    · rename_i hn
+      exact Nat.clog_of_right_le_one hn base
+    · rename_i hn
+      apply le_antisymm
+      · rw [Nat.clog_le_iff_le_pow hb]
+        have h := Nat.lt_pow_succ_log_self hb (n - 1)
+        lia
+      · apply Nat.succ_le_of_lt
+        rw [Nat.lt_clog_iff_pow_lt hb]
+        exact (Nat.pow_log_le_self base (by lia : n - 1 ≠ 0)).trans_lt (by lia)
+  convert (show ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun n : ℕ => if n ≤ 1 then 0 else Nat.log base (n - 1) + 1) encUnary encUnary
+      from by fun_prop) using 1
+  exact funext heq
+
+/-- Given an efficient unary size function, a fixed factor raised to its fixed-base ceiling
+logarithm has a polynomial-time unary output in the caller's original encoding. The bound charges
+every intermediate power, including the initial one when the factor is zero. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem unary_pow_clog_const {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {size : α → ℕ}
+    (hsize : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime size input encUnary) (factor base : ℕ) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => factor ^ Nat.clog base (size x)) input encUnary := by
+  suffices ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun n : ℕ => factor ^ Nat.clog base n)
+      encUnary encUnary from this.comp hsize
+  rcases le_or_gt base 1 with hb | hb
+  · simpa only [Nat.clog_of_left_le_one hb, pow_zero] using
+      (const (encIn := encUnary) (encMid := encUnary) 1)
+  obtain ⟨hefficient, hspec⟩ := iterate_spec (count := Nat.clog base) (init := fun _ => 1)
+    (step := fun state => state * factor) (encIn := encUnary) (encState := encUnary)
+    (unary_clog_const base) (by fun_prop) (by fun_prop)
+    (fun _ i state => state = factor ^ i) (fun _ => rfl)
+    (fun _ _ _ _ h => by rw [h, pow_succ])
+    (size := fun n => base ^ Nat.clog base (max factor 1) *
+      (n + 1) ^ Nat.clog base (max factor 1)) (by fun_prop) (fun n i state hi h => by
+      simp only [encUnary_apply, List.length_replicate, h]
+      calc factor ^ i ≤ max factor 1 ^ i := Nat.pow_le_pow_left (Nat.le_max_left _ _) _
+        _ ≤ max factor 1 ^ Nat.clog base (n + 1) :=
+          Nat.pow_le_pow_right (Nat.le_max_right _ _)
+            (hi.trans (Nat.clog_mono_right base (Nat.le_succ n)))
+        _ ≤ _ := Nat.pow_clog_le_pow_clog_mul_pow_clog hb _ (Nat.succ_ne_zero n))
+  simpa only [hspec] using hefficient
+
 end Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime

+/-!
+# Logarithmic construction schedules
+
+The actual tower depth and selected size automate for an unbounded vertex count. The certificates
+charge unary counters and outputs; a binary input cannot silently provide the same output budget.
+An arbitrary fixed growth factor also supports the size schedules of amplification rounds.
+-/
+
+namespace ComplexityTests.Logarithms
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+example (base : ℕ) : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun n : ℕ => (Nat.clog base n - 1, base ^ Nat.clog base n))

+
+example (base : ℕ) : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun n : ℕ => let rounds := Nat.clog base n; (rounds - 1, base ^ rounds))

+
+-- Explicit let reduction also lets `fun_prop` retain the relation between size and exponent.
+example (base : ℕ) : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun n : ℕ => let rounds := Nat.clog base n; (rounds - 1, base ^ rounds))
+    encUnary (encPair encUnary encUnary) := by dsimp only; fun_prop
+
+-- A caller may use any encoding with a certified unary size function.
+example {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {size : α → ℕ}
+    (hsize : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime size input encUnary) (base factor : ℕ) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun x => (Nat.clog base (size x), factor ^ Nat.clog base (size x)))
+      input (encPair encUnary encUnary) := by fun_prop
+
+-- Raw and framed words provide different input encodings of the same size-based program.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun w : List Bool => 3 ^ Nat.clog 2 w.length) encBits encUnary := by fun_prop
+
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun w : List Bool => 3 ^ Nat.clog 2 w.length) (encList encBool) encUnary := by fun_prop
+

+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun n : ℕ => Nat.clog (257 ^ 8) n - 1)
+    encUnary encUnary := by fun_prop
+

+/-

+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Basic
+import Complexity.Foundations.Data.List.Basic
+import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Basic
+
+/-!
+# Polynomial-time finite case analysis
+
+An efficiently computed finite tag selects a branch retaining the original input. Both the tag
+encoding and output encoding are arbitrary. The finite type and all branch machines are fixed
+independently of runtime input; this does not enumerate a family whose size grows with the input.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.finite_cases`: finite dispatch with captured input.
+
+## References
+
+Adapts `Computability/Probabilistic/Finite.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the existing tidy calculus.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+
+/-- A fixed finite tag selects a certified branch, charging the tag and captured input.
+Neither the tag nor the result type requires a default inhabitant. -/
+theorem finite_cases
+    {α β Tag : Type} [Finite Tag] {input : α ↪ List Bool} {output : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {tagEncoding : Tag ↪ List Bool} {tag : α → Tag} {branch : Tag → α → β}
+    (htag : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime tag input tagEncoding)
+    (hbranch : ∀ choice, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (branch choice) input output) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => branch (tag a) a) input output := by
+  classical
+  let _ := Fintype.ofFinite Tag
+  cases isEmpty_or_nonempty Tag with
+  | inl hempty =>
+    let : IsEmpty α := ⟨fun a => isEmptyElim (tag a)⟩
+    exact of_finite _
+  | inr hnonempty =>
+    let fallback := Classical.choice hnonempty
+    have hselect (tags : List Tag) : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a =>
+        tags.foldr (fun choice rest => if tag a = choice then branch choice a else rest)
+          (branch fallback a)) input output := by
+      induction tags with
+      | nil => exact hbranch fallback
+      | cons choice tags ih => exact (htag.decide_eq' (const choice)).ite_decide (hbranch choice) ih
+    simpa only [List.foldr_ite_eq_of_mem, Finset.mem_toList, Finset.mem_univ] using
+      hselect (Finset.univ.toList : List Tag)
+
+end Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime

+/-- Read a computed index of a fixed finite table, charging the index and all stored entries. -/
+theorem pi_apply' [Fintype Index] {indexEncoding : Index ↪ List Bool}
+    {values : α → Index → Value} {index : α → Index}
+    (hvalues : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime values input (encPi enc))
+    (hindex : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime index input indexEncoding) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => values a (index a)) input enc :=
+  hindex.finite_cases (fun i => (pi_apply enc i).comp hvalues)
+
+/-- Evaluate a stored table at a stored index. The product view is registered with `fun_prop`;
+for separately computed tables and indices, apply `pi_apply'` to their certificates. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem pi_eval [Fintype Index] (indexEncoding : Index ↪ List Bool) (enc : Value ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : (Index → Value) × Index => pair.1 pair.2)
+      (encPair (encPi enc) indexEncoding) enc := pi_apply' (fst _ _) (snd _ _)
+
+/-- Update a computed index while retaining and charging every other entry. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem pi_update' [Fintype Index] [DecidableEq Index] {indexEncoding : Index ↪ List Bool}
+    {values : α → Index → Value} {index : α → Index} {value : α → Value}
+    (hvalues : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime values input (encPi enc))
+    (hindex : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime index input indexEncoding)
+    (hvalue : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime value input enc) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => Function.update (values a) (index a) (value a))
+      input (encPi enc) := hindex.finite_cases (fun i => pi_update hvalues hvalue i)
+
 end Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime

+
+/-!
+# Efficient finite case analysis for probabilistic programs
+
+A computed finite tag selects among certified programs retaining the original input. The finite
+control type and its branch machines are fixed independently of runtime input. Each branch may
+return values of unbounded encoded length, which its certificate charges.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.finite_cases`: finite probabilistic dispatch with captured input.
+
+## References
+
+Adapts `Computability/Probabilistic/Finite.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the existing tidy calculus and closed PPT rules.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Probability
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+/-- A fixed finite tag selects a certified probabilistic branch with captured input.
+The result has the chosen branch's exact distribution, including state returned with its output. -/
+theorem IsPPTOn.finite_cases
+    {α β Tag : Type} [Finite Tag] {input : α ↪ List Bool} {output : β ↪ List Bool}
+    {tagEncoding : Tag ↪ List Bool} {tag : α → Tag} {branch : Tag → α → ProbComp β}
+    (htag : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime tag input tagEncoding)
+    (hbranch : ∀ choice, IsPPTOn input output (branch choice)) :
+    IsPPTOn input output (fun a => branch (tag a) a) := by
+  classical
+  let _ := Fintype.ofFinite Tag
+  cases isEmpty_or_nonempty Tag with
+  | inl hempty =>
+    let : IsEmpty α := ⟨fun a => isEmptyElim (tag a)⟩
+    apply (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.of_finite (encA := input) (encB := output)
+      (fun a : α => isEmptyElim a)).isPPTOn.congr
+    intro a
+    exact isEmptyElim a
+  | inr hnonempty =>
+    let fallback := Classical.choice hnonempty
+    have hselect (tags : List Tag) : IsPPTOn input output (fun a =>
+        tags.foldr (fun choice rest => if tag a = choice then branch choice a else rest)
+          (branch fallback a)) := by
+      induction tags with
+      | nil => exact hbranch fallback
+      | cons choice tags ih =>
+        exact IsPPTOn.ite (htag.decide_eq' (.const choice)) (hbranch choice) ih
+    simpa only [List.foldr_ite_eq_of_mem, Finset.mem_toList, Finset.mem_univ] using
+      hselect (Finset.univ.toList : List Tag)
+
+end Cslib.Probability

+/-- A chain of equality tests selects a contained tag, regardless of duplicates or fallback. -/
+theorem List.foldr_ite_eq_of_mem {Tag Value : Type*} [DecidableEq Tag]
+    (tags : List Tag) (tag : Tag) (branch : Tag → Value) (fallback : Value) (h : tag ∈ tags) :
+    tags.foldr (fun candidate rest => if tag = candidate then branch candidate else rest)
+      fallback = branch tag := by
+  induction tags with
+  | nil => simp at h
+  | cons candidate tags ih =>
+    by_cases heq : tag = candidate
+    · simp [heq]
+    · simp only [List.foldr_cons, heq, ↓reduceIte]
+      exact ih (List.mem_cons.mp h |>.resolve_left heq)

+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Finite

+/-! Finite dispatch retains captured data and charges every table entry and selected result. -/
+
+namespace ComplexityTests.FiniteControl
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM Cslib Cslib.Probability
+
+-- Stored table/index pairs use ordinary function application.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun pair : (Bool → List Bool) × Bool => pair.1 pair.2)
+    (encPair (encPi encBits) encBool) encBits := by fun_prop
+
+-- The explicit closure rule handles separately computed higher-order values without a default.
+example {α Index Value : Type} [Fintype Index] {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+    {enc : Value ↪ List Bool} {indexEnc : Index ↪ List Bool}
+    (values : α → Index → Value) (index : α → Index)
+    (hv : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime values input (encPi enc))
+    (hi : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime index input indexEnc) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => values a (index a)) input enc := hv.pi_apply' hi
+
+-- A different encoding of the same index type uses the same lookup rule.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun pair : (Bool → List Bool) × Bool => pair.1 pair.2)
+    (encPair (encPi encBits) (encFinite Bool)) encBits := by polytime
+
+-- Computed update and lookup preserve unbounded words in all unselected entries.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun pair : (Bool → List Bool) × Bool =>
+      Function.update pair.1 pair.2 (pair.1 pair.2).reverse)
+    (encPair (encPi encBits) encBool) (encPi encBits) := by fun_prop
+
+-- Naming the shared tuple gives the same program certificate.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun pair : (Bool → List Bool) × Bool =>
+      let data := pair
+      Function.update data.1 data.2 (data.1 data.2).reverse)
+    (encPair (encPi encBits) encBool) (encPi encBits) := by polytime
+
+-- A computed index uses the general closure rule when plain higher-order inference is insufficient.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun pair : (Bool → List Bool) × Bool =>
+      let data := (pair.1, !pair.2)
+      Function.update data.1 data.2 (data.1 data.2).reverse)
+    (encPair (encPi encBits) encBool) (encPi encBits) := by
+  have hv := ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst (encPi (Index := Bool) encBits) encBool
+  have hi := ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bool_not.comp
+    (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.snd (encPi (Index := Bool) encBits) encBool)
+  exact hv.pi_update' hi (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsReverse.comp (hv.pi_apply' hi))
+
+-- Finite dispatch retains the original unbounded input in every branch.
+example {α β Tag : Type} [Finite Tag] (input : α ↪ List Bool) (output : β ↪ List Bool)
+    (tagEncoding : Tag ↪ List Bool) (tag : α → Tag) (branch : Tag → α → β)
+    (htag : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime tag input tagEncoding)
+    (hbranch : ∀ choice, ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (branch choice) input output) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => branch (tag a) a) input output :=
+  htag.finite_cases hbranch
+
+-- Probabilistic branches may return both output and private state.
+example {α β State Tag : Type} [Finite Tag] (input : α ↪ List Bool)
+    (output : β ↪ List Bool) (stateEncoding : State ↪ List Bool)
+    (tagEncoding : Tag ↪ List Bool) (tag : α → Tag)
+    (branch : Tag → α → ProbComp (β × State))
+    (htag : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime tag input tagEncoding)
+    (hbranch : ∀ choice, IsPPTOn input (encPair output stateEncoding) (branch choice)) :
+    IsPPTOn input (encPair output stateEncoding) (fun a => branch (tag a) a) :=
+  IsPPTOn.finite_cases htag hbranch
+
+private def encEmpty : Empty ↪ List Bool := ⟨Empty.elim, fun value => value.elim⟩
+
+-- Empty finite control requires no fallback program or inhabited result type.
+example : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+    (fun a : Empty => (a.elim : Empty → Empty) a) encEmpty encEmpty :=
+  ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.finite_cases
+    (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.id' (encIn := encEmpty)) (fun tag => tag.elim)
+
+example : IsPPTOn encEmpty encEmpty
+    (fun a : Empty => (a.elim : Empty → ProbComp Empty) a) :=
+  IsPPTOn.finite_cases (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.id' (encIn := encEmpty)) (fun tag => tag.elim)
+
+-- A concrete branch selector combines finite control, unbounded state and independent sampling.
+private noncomputable def choose (tag : Bool) (word : List Bool) :
+    ProbComp (List Bool × List Bool) :=
+  if tag then do
+    let bit ← ProbComp.uniform Bool
+    return (bit :: word, word)
+  else pure (word.reverse, word)
+
+example : IsPPTOn encBits (encPair encBits encBits) (fun word => choose word.isEmpty word) := by
+  apply IsPPTOn.finite_cases (tagEncoding := encBool)
+  · fun_prop
+  · intro tag
+    unfold choose
+    ppt
+
+end ComplexityTests.FiniteControl

+/-!
+# Polynomial-time operations on finite tape storage
+
+The operations of cslib's existing tapes are certified by composition of list, option and pair
+operations. They charge the complete stored tapes and accept any symbol encoding, including
+infinite or empty alphabets. Finite-control interpreters can use these rules without building
+new tape machines.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.stackTape_cons`: prepend a computed cell,
+  retaining the stack's omission of trailing blanks.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.biTape_moveLeft`, `.biTape_moveRight`,
+  `.biTape_write`, `.biTape_step`: native tape operations with `fun_prop` certificates.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.biTape_mk₁`: load a computed list.
+
+## References
+
+Adapts `Computability/Probabilistic/Tape.lean` from the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8` to the tidy calculus, using arbitrary symbol encodings
+instead of fixed finite tags.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+
+open Cslib.Turing
+
+variable {Symbol α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool}
+
+/-- Reading the stored list is a change of view of the same encoded bits. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem stackTape_toList (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime StackTape.toList (encStackTape enc) (encList (encOption enc)) :=
+  of_eq fun _ => rfl
+
+/-- Reading a stack head decodes the first cell, with a blank default. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem stackTape_head (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime StackTape.head (encStackTape enc) (encOption enc) := by
+  apply ((headD (encA := encOption enc) none).comp (stackTape_toList enc)).of_enc_eq
+  intro tape
+  cases tape with | mk values h => cases values <;> rfl
+
+/-- Removing a stack head is the certified list-tail operation. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem stackTape_tail (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime StackTape.tail (encStackTape enc) (encStackTape enc) :=
+  ((tail (encA := encOption enc)).comp (stackTape_toList enc)).of_enc_eq (fun tape => by
+    simp only [Function.comp_def, encStackTape_apply, StackTape.tail_toList])
+
+/-- Prepend a cell without requiring a default symbol or case analysis over the alphabet. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem stackTape_cons {symbol : α → Option Symbol} {tape : α → StackTape Symbol}
+    (hsymbol : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime symbol input (encOption enc))
+    (htape : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime tape input (encStackTape enc)) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => StackTape.cons (symbol a) (tape a)) input
+      (encStackTape enc) := by
+  have hdata := (stackTape_toList enc).comp htape
+  have hempty := (listIsEmpty (encA := encOption enc)).comp hdata
+  have hlist : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun a => if (symbol a).isSome || !(tape a).toList.isEmpty
+        then symbol a :: (tape a).toList else []) input (encList (encOption enc)) := by fun_prop
+  exact hlist.of_enc_eq (fun a => by rw [encStackTape_apply, StackTape.cons_toList])
+
+/-- Map symbols to occupied cells with the certified list map. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem stackTape_mapSome (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime StackTape.mapSome (encList enc) (encStackTape enc) :=
+  (map (optionSome enc)).of_enc_eq (fun _ => rfl)
+
+private theorem biTape_parts (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun tape : BiTape Symbol => (tape.head, tape.left, tape.right))
+      (encBiTape enc) (encPair (encOption enc) (encPair (encStackTape enc) (encStackTape enc))) :=
+  of_eq fun _ => rfl
+
+/-- Assemble a tape from its computed head and two sides. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem biTape_mk {head : α → Option Symbol} {left right : α → StackTape Symbol}
+    (hhead : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime head input (encOption enc))
+    (hleft : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime left input (encStackTape enc))
+    (hright : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime right input (encStackTape enc)) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => BiTape.mk (head a) (left a) (right a)) input
+      (encBiTape enc) :=
+  (hhead.prod (hleft.prod hright)).of_enc_eq (fun _ => rfl)
+
+/-- Read the current cell of a computed tape. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem biTape_head (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime BiTape.head (encBiTape enc) (encOption enc) :=
+  (biTape_parts enc).fst'
+
+/-- Extract the stored left side. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem biTape_left (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime BiTape.left (encBiTape enc) (encStackTape enc) :=
+  (biTape_parts enc).snd'.fst'
+
+/-- Extract the stored right side. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem biTape_right (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime BiTape.right (encBiTape enc) (encStackTape enc) :=
+  (biTape_parts enc).snd'.snd'
+
+/-- Move left by the existing stack operations. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem biTape_moveLeft (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime BiTape.moveLeft (encBiTape enc) (encBiTape enc) := by
+  unfold BiTape.moveLeft
+  fun_prop
+
+/-- Move right by the existing stack operations. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem biTape_moveRight (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime BiTape.moveRight (encBiTape enc) (encBiTape enc) := by
+  unfold BiTape.moveRight
+  fun_prop
+
+/-- Write a computed optional symbol, including blank erasure. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem biTape_write {tape : α → BiTape Symbol} {symbol : α → Option Symbol}
+    (htape : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime tape input (encBiTape enc))
+    (hsymbol : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime symbol input (encOption enc)) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => (tape a).write (symbol a)) input (encBiTape enc) := by
+  unfold BiTape.write
+  fun_prop
+
+/-- Execute a fixed native action, charging the full encoded tape. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem biTape_step (action : Option (Option Symbol) × SignType)
+    {tape : α → BiTape Symbol}
+    (htape : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime tape input (encBiTape enc)) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => (tape a).step action) input (encBiTape enc) := by
+  rcases action with ⟨write, move⟩
+  cases write <;> cases move <;>
+    simp only [BiTape.step, Option.elim_none, Option.elim_some] <;> fun_prop
+
+/-- Loading a list constructs a head and two stacks with no default symbol. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem biTape_mk₁ (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime BiTape.mk₁ (encList enc) (encBiTape enc) := by
+  have hparts : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+      (fun values : List Symbol => BiTape.mk (values.head?) StackTape.nil
+        (StackTape.mapSome values.tail)) (encList enc) (encBiTape enc) := by fun_prop
+  apply hparts.of_enc_eq
+  intro values
+  cases values <;> rfl
+
+end Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime

+/-!
+# Encodings of finite tape storage
+
+The existing stack and bidirectional tapes use the standard list, option and pair encodings.
+The symbol encoding is a parameter: the operations do not require a finite or inhabited alphabet.
+If symbol encodings have a uniform length bound, the complete tape encoding is linear in its
+stored extent, including blank gaps.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.encStackTape`: encode a stack's stored list of optional cells.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.encBiTape`: encode the head and both sides of a bidirectional tape.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.length_encStackTape_le`, `Turing.MultiTapeTM.length_encBiTape_le`:
+  explicit bounds from a fixed symbol-length bound.
+
+## References
+
+Adapts the encodings in `Computability/Probabilistic/Tape.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using Christian Reitwiessner's standard encodings
+and Bolton Bailey's tape representations.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+open Cslib.Turing
+
+variable {Symbol : Type}
+
+/-- Encode the finite stored list, retaining interior blank cells. -/
+def encStackTape (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) : StackTape Symbol ↪ List Bool where
+  toFun tape := encList (encOption enc) tape.toList
+  inj' := fun _ _ h => StackTape.ext ((encList _).injective h)
+
+@[simp] theorem encStackTape_apply (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) (tape : StackTape Symbol) :
+    encStackTape enc tape = encList (encOption enc) tape.toList := rfl
+
+/-- Encode the current cell, left side and right side with their standard framing. -/
+def encBiTape (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) : BiTape Symbol ↪ List Bool where
+  toFun tape := encPair (encOption enc) (encPair (encStackTape enc) (encStackTape enc))
+    (tape.head, tape.left, tape.right)
+  inj' := fun _ _ h =>
+    let heq := (encPair _ _).injective h
+    BiTape.ext (congrArg Prod.fst heq) (congrArg (Prod.fst ∘ Prod.snd) heq)
+      (congrArg (Prod.snd ∘ Prod.snd) heq)
+
+@[simp] theorem encBiTape_apply (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) (tape : BiTape Symbol) :
+    encBiTape enc tape = encPair (encOption enc) (encPair (encStackTape enc) (encStackTape enc))
+      (tape.head, tape.left, tape.right) := rfl
+
+/-- Bounded symbol encodings give a linear bound for the stored stack. -/
+theorem length_encStackTape_le (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) (tape : StackTape Symbol)
+    {bound : ℕ} (hbound : ∀ symbol, (enc symbol).length ≤ bound) :
+    (encStackTape enc tape).length ≤ tape.length * (2 * bound + 3) := by
+  have hoption (symbol : Option Symbol) : (encOption enc symbol).length ≤ bound + 1 := by
+    cases symbol with
+    | none => simp
+    | some symbol =>
+      simpa only [encOption_some, List.length_cons] using Nat.add_le_add_right (hbound symbol) 1
+  exact length_encList_le (encOption enc) tape.toList (fun symbol _ => hoption symbol)
+
+/-- The encoding charges all stored cells, including blanks between nonblank cells. -/
+theorem length_encBiTape_le (enc : Symbol ↪ List Bool) (tape : BiTape Symbol)
+    {bound : ℕ} (hbound : ∀ symbol, (enc symbol).length ≤ bound) :
+    (encBiTape enc tape).length ≤ 4 * (bound + 2) * tape.spaceUsed := by
+  have hhead : (encOption enc tape.head).length ≤ bound + 1 := by
+    cases tape.head with
+    | none => simp
+    | some symbol =>
+      simpa only [encOption_some, List.length_cons] using Nat.add_le_add_right (hbound symbol) 1
+  have hleft := length_encStackTape_le enc tape.left hbound
+  have hright := length_encStackTape_le enc tape.right hbound
+  simp only [encBiTape_apply, length_encPair, BiTape.spaceUsed]
+  nlinarith
+
+end Turing.MultiTapeTM

 @[expose] public section
@@ -86,10 +88,44 @@ theorem bool_not : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime Bool.not encBool encBool := of_fin
 theorem bool_and : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : Bool × Bool => p.1 && p.2)

+/-- Conjoin computed guards, fixing both intermediate Boolean encodings. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bool_and' {left right : α → Bool}
+    (hleft : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime left encA encBool)
+    (hright : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime right encA encBool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => left a && right a) encA encBool :=
+  bool_and.comp (hleft.prod hright)
+
 @[fun_prop]
 theorem bool_or : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : Bool × Bool => p.1 || p.2)
     (encPair encBool encBool) encBool := of_finite _
 
+/-- Conjunction of efficiently decidable propositions uses the standard Boolean encoding. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem decide_and {left right : α → Prop} [∀ a, Decidable (left a)] [∀ a, Decidable (right a)]
+    (hleft : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => decide (left a)) encA encBool)
+    (hright : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => decide (right a)) encA encBool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => decide (left a ∧ right a)) encA encBool := by
+  simpa only [Bool.decide_and, Function.comp_def] using bool_and.comp (hleft.prod hright)
+
+/-- A Boolean conditional fixes the guard encoding before automation synthesizes its proof. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem cond {condition : α → Bool} {yes no : α → β}
+    (hcondition : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime condition encA encBool)
+    (hyes : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime yes encA encB)
+    (hno : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime no encA encB) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => if condition a then yes a else no a) encA encB :=
+  hcondition.ite' hyes hno
+
+/-- A proposition-valued conditional computes its decision in the standard Boolean encoding. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem ite_decide {condition : α → Prop} [∀ a, Decidable (condition a)] {yes no : α → β}
+    (hcondition : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => decide (condition a)) encA encBool)
+    (hyes : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime yes encA encB)
+    (hno : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime no encA encB) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => if condition a then yes a else no a) encA encB := by
+  simpa only [decide_eq_true_eq] using hcondition.cond hyes hno
+
 /-- Comparing two Boolean values is a finite-domain computation. -/
 @[fun_prop]
 theorem bool_beq : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun p : Bool × Bool => p.1 == p.2)

+module

+/-!
+# Polynomial-time fixed-width bit lists
+
+Replicating a fixed bit and reading fixed-width rows use the existing list and iteration
+calculus. Runtime row counts and widths are computed in unary, charging the complete output.
+The operations are total on empty and short lists.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsReplicate`: repeat a fixed bit.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsRowWithInput`: read one fixed-width row.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsRowsWithInput`: read a runtime number of rows.
+
+## References
+
+The row interface is adapted from `Computability/Probabilistic/BitString.lean` on the cslib
+`crypto` branch at `5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime
+
+/-- Repeat a fixed bit a unary number of times. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsReplicate (bit : Bool) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun n => List.replicate n bit) encUnary encBits := by
+  have h (n : ℕ) : (List.cons bit)^[n] [] = List.replicate n bit := by
+    induction n with
+    | zero => rfl
+    | succ n ih => simp only [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, List.replicate_succ]
+  simpa only [h, id_eq] using iterate_of_bounded_growth (count := id) (init := fun _ : ℕ => [])
+    (step := List.cons bit) id' (const []) (by fun_prop) (growth := 1) (fun _ => by simp)
+
+variable {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool}
+
+/-- Read a row of a computed word, including the cost of padding a short word. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsRowWithInput {width row : α → ℕ} {word : α → List Bool}
+    (hwidth : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime width input encUnary)
+    (hrow : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime row input encUnary)
+    (hword : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime word input encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => Cslib.BitString.listRow (width a) (row a) (word a))
+      input encBits := by
+  unfold Cslib.BitString.listRow
+  fun_prop
+
+/-- Extract rows from a word with polynomial-time unary dimensions. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem bitsRowsWithInput {count width : α → ℕ} {word : α → List Bool}
+    (hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime count input encUnary)
+    (hwidth : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime width input encUnary)
+    (hword : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime word input encBits) :
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => Cslib.BitString.listRows (count a) (width a) (word a))
+      input (encList encBits) := by
+  unfold Cslib.BitString.listRows
+  fun_prop
+
+end Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime

diff --git a/Complexity/Computability/Probabilistic/Adaptive.lean b/Complexity/Computability/Probabilistic/Adaptive.lean
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..9164e0e6
--- /dev/null
+++ b/Complexity/Computability/Probabilistic/Adaptive.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,210 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.Iteration
+public import Complexity.Computability.Probabilistic.PPT
+public import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Basic
+import Complexity.Computability.Probabilistic.CoinTape
+import Complexity.Computability.Probabilistic.PPT.Capture
+import Complexity.Computability.Probabilistic.Sampling
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.BitString
+import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Complexity.PolyTime.Nat
+import Complexity.Probability.BitString.List
+
+/-!
+# Strict PPT adaptive iteration
+
+A bounded probabilistic loop is strict PPT when its step is strict PPT and one invariant bounds
+the encoded size of every reachable state. The same rule proves the final invariant. The step
+may capture the original input. Constant-growth and length-nonincreasing variants supply the
+size invariant automatically.
+
+Internally, a polynomial-length random tape is split into independent blocks. The total typed
+saved-coin evaluator gives a deterministic fold, certified by the existing tidy TM calculus.
+Clients supply ordinary programs and invariants, without machines, replay code or decoders.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.iterate_spec`: certify efficiency and the final supported invariant.
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.iterateWith_spec`: allow the step to capture the original input.
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.iterate_of_bounded_growth`, `.iterate_of_length_le`: automatic
+  intermediate-size bounds.
+
+## References
+
+Adapted from `Computability/Probabilistic/Adaptive.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, reusing the tidy fold calculus.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Probability
+
+open Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+variable {α State : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {stateEncoding : State ↪ List Bool}
+
+/-- One invariant proves both a polynomial resource bound and the final supported postcondition.
+The resource invariant must hold on every possible execution, not just with high probability. -/
+theorem IsPPTOn.iterate_spec {initial : α → State} {count : α → ℕ}
+    {step : State → ProbComp State}
+    (hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime count input encUnary)
+    (hinitial : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime initial input stateEncoding)
+    (hstep : IsPPTOn stateEncoding stateEncoding step)
+    (invariant : α → ℕ → State → Prop) (hbase : ∀ a, invariant a 0 (initial a))
+    (hpreserve : ∀ a i state, i < count a → invariant a i state →
+      ∀ next ∈ (ProbComp.eval (step state)).support, invariant a (i + 1) next)
+    {size : ℕ → ℕ} (hsize : PolynomiallyBounded size)
+    (hbound : ∀ a i state, i ≤ count a → invariant a i state →
+      (stateEncoding state).length ≤ size (input a).length) :
+    IsPPTOn input stateEncoding (fun a => OracleComp.iterate (count a) step (initial a)) ∧
+      ∀ a state, state ∈ (ProbComp.eval (OracleComp.iterate (count a) step (initial a))).support →
+        invariant a (count a) state := by
+  obtain ⟨c, d, evaluate, hevaluate, hsupport, hlaw⟩ := hstep.exists_total_seeded_evaluator
+  obtain ⟨cs, ds, hs⟩ := polynomiallyBounded_iff_le.mp hsize
+  let bound (a : α) := cs * ((input a).length + 1) ^ ds
+  let budget (a : α) := c * (bound a + 1) ^ d
+  have hbudgetEff : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime budget input encUnary := by
+    dsimp only [budget, bound]
+    fun_prop
+  have hbudget (a : α) (i : ℕ) (state : State) (hi : i ≤ count a)
+      (hinvariant : invariant a i state) :
+      c * ((stateEncoding state).length + 1) ^ d ≤ budget a :=
+    Nat.mul_le_mul_left c (Nat.pow_le_pow_left
+      (Nat.add_le_add_right ((hbound a i state hi hinvariant).trans (hs _)) 1) d)
+  have hfold : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : α × List Bool =>
+      (BitString.listRows (count pair.1) (budget pair.1) pair.2).foldl evaluate (initial pair.1))
+      (encPair input encBits) stateEncoding := by
+    have hrows : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair : α × List Bool =>
+        BitString.listRows (count pair.1) (budget pair.1) pair.2)
+        (encPair input encBits) (encList encBits) := by
+      have hfirst := ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst input encBits
+      exact ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.bitsRowsWithInput (hcount.comp hfirst)
+        (hbudgetEff.comp hfirst) (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.snd input encBits)
+    have hstart := hinitial.comp (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst input encBits)
+    refine (hrows.foldl_spec hstart hevaluate
+      (fun pair consumed state => invariant pair.1 consumed.length state)
+      (fun pair => hbase pair.1) ?_
+      (size := fun n => cs * (n + 1) ^ ds) (by fun_prop) ?_).1
+    · intro pair consumed state coins hprefix hinvariant
+      have hlength := hprefix.length_le
+      simp only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton, BitString.length_listRows] at hlength
+      simpa only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton] using
+        hpreserve pair.1 consumed.length state (by lia) hinvariant _ (hsupport state coins)
+    · intro pair consumed state hprefix hinvariant
+      have hlength := hprefix.length_le
+      simp only [BitString.length_listRows] at hlength
+      have hstate := (hbound pair.1 consumed.length state hlength hinvariant).trans (hs _)
+      exact hstate.trans (Nat.mul_le_mul_left cs (Nat.pow_le_pow_left
+        (by simp only [length_encPair]; lia) ds))
+  let replayed (a : α) : ProbComp State := do
+    let coins ← BitString.sampleList (count a * budget a)
+    return (BitString.listRows (count a) (budget a) coins).foldl evaluate (initial a)
+  have hbits : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => count a * budget a) input encUnary :=
+    ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.unary_mul.comp (hcount.prod hbudgetEff)
+  have hefficient : IsPPTOn input stateEncoding replayed :=
+    hbits.sampleList.bind_with hfold.isPPTOn
+  refine ⟨hefficient.congr ?_, fun a => ProbComp.iterate_invariant (count a) step (initial a)
+    (invariant a) (hbase a) (fun i hi state hinvariant => hpreserve a i state hi hinvariant)⟩
+  intro a
+  have hjoint := ProbComp.eval_iterate_of_uniform (Seed := BitString (budget a))
+    (count a) step (initial a) (fun state bits => evaluate state (List.ofFn bits))
+    (invariant a) (hbase a) (fun i hi state hinvariant => hpreserve a i state hi hinvariant)
+    (fun i hi state hinvariant => by
+      simpa only [BitString.uniformList, PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def] using
+        hlaw state (budget a) (hbudget a i state hi.le hinvariant))
+  rw [hjoint]
+  have hrows := congrArg (PMF.map (fun rows : List (List Bool) => rows.foldl evaluate (initial a)))
+    (BitString.uniformList_listRows (count a) (budget a))
+  simpa only [replayed, ProbComp.eval_bind, BitString.eval_sampleList, ProbComp.eval_pure,
+    PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def, ← List.foldl_map, List.map_ofFn, PMF.map,
+    PMF.bind_bind, PMF.pure_bind] using hrows
+
+/-- The loop body may capture the original input. The joint step certificate charges for both
+that input and the changing state; the client invariant describes only the changing state. -/
+theorem IsPPTOn.iterateWith_spec {initial : α → State} {count : α → ℕ}
+    {step : α → State → ProbComp State}
+    (hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime count input encUnary)
+    (hinitial : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime initial input stateEncoding)
+    (hstep : IsPPTOn (encPair input stateEncoding) stateEncoding (fun pair => step pair.1 pair.2))
+    (invariant : α → ℕ → State → Prop) (hbase : ∀ a, invariant a 0 (initial a))
+    (hpreserve : ∀ a i state, i < count a → invariant a i state →
+      ∀ next ∈ (ProbComp.eval (step a state)).support, invariant a (i + 1) next)
+    {size : ℕ → ℕ} (hsize : PolynomiallyBounded size)
+    (hbound : ∀ a i state, i ≤ count a → invariant a i state →
+      (stateEncoding state).length ≤ size (input a).length) :
+    IsPPTOn input stateEncoding (fun a => OracleComp.iterate (count a) (step a) (initial a)) ∧
+      ∀ a state,
+        state ∈ (ProbComp.eval (OracleComp.iterate (count a) (step a) (initial a))).support →
+        invariant a (count a) state := by
+  let packedStep (pair : α × State) : ProbComp (α × State) :=
+    (fun next => (pair.1, next)) <$> step pair.1 pair.2
+  have hpackedStep : IsPPTOn (encPair input stateEncoding)
+      (encPair input stateEncoding) packedStep :=
+    hstep.pair (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.fst input stateEncoding)
+  have hstart := ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.id'.prod hinitial
+  have hpacked := (IsPPTOn.iterate_spec hcount hstart hpackedStep
+    (fun a i pair => pair.1 = a ∧ invariant a i pair.2)
+    (fun a => ⟨rfl, hbase a⟩)
+    (by
+      rintro a i ⟨captured, state⟩ hi ⟨rfl, hstate⟩ next hnext
+      simp only [packedStep, ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.mem_support_map_iff] at hnext
+      obtain ⟨value, hvalue, rfl⟩ := hnext
+      exact ⟨rfl, hpreserve captured i state hi hstate value hvalue⟩)
+    (size := fun n => 2 * n + size n + 1) (by fun_prop)
+    (by
+      rintro a i ⟨captured, state⟩ hi ⟨rfl, hstate⟩
+      simp only [length_encPair]
+      have := hbound captured i state hi hstate
+      lia)).1
+  refine ⟨(hpacked.map (ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.snd input stateEncoding)).congr ?_, fun a =>
+    ProbComp.iterate_invariant (count a) (step a) (initial a)
+      (invariant a) (hbase a) (fun i hi state hinvariant => hpreserve a i state hi hinvariant)⟩
+  intro a
+  rw [OracleComp.iterate_map (count a) (step a) packedStep (fun state => (a, state))
+    (fun _ => rfl) (initial a)]
+  simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def]
+  exact PMF.map_id _
+
+/-- A strict PPT step with constant growth can be repeated a polynomial number of times. -/
+theorem IsPPTOn.iterate_of_bounded_growth {initial : α → State} {count : α → ℕ}
+    {step : State → ProbComp State}
+    (hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime count input encUnary)
+    (hinitial : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime initial input stateEncoding)
+    (hstep : IsPPTOn stateEncoding stateEncoding step)
+    {growth : ℕ} (hgrowth : ∀ state next, next ∈ (ProbComp.eval (step state)).support →
+      (stateEncoding next).length ≤ (stateEncoding state).length + growth) :
+    IsPPTOn input stateEncoding (fun a => OracleComp.iterate (count a) step (initial a)) := by
+  obtain ⟨ci, di, hi⟩ := hinitial.polyBounded_length
+  obtain ⟨cc, dc, hc⟩ := hcount.polyBounded_length
+  simp only [encUnary_apply, List.length_replicate] at hc
+  exact (IsPPTOn.iterate_spec hcount hinitial hstep
+    (fun a i state => (stateEncoding state).length ≤
+      (stateEncoding (initial a)).length + i * growth)
+    (by simp)
+    (by
+      intro a i state _ hinvariant next hnext
+      have := hgrowth state next hnext
+      nlinarith)
+    (size := fun n => ci * (n + 1) ^ di + cc * (n + 1) ^ dc * growth) (by fun_prop)
+    (fun a i state hiCount hinvariant => hinvariant.trans
+      (Nat.add_le_add (hi a) (Nat.mul_le_mul_right growth (hiCount.trans (hc a)))))).1
+
+/-- Iteration of a step that never increases its encoded state needs no extra size invariant. -/
+theorem IsPPTOn.iterate_of_length_le {initial : α → State} {count : α → ℕ}
+    {step : State → ProbComp State}
+    (hcount : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime count input encUnary)
+    (hinitial : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime initial input stateEncoding)
+    (hstep : IsPPTOn stateEncoding stateEncoding step)
+    (hshrink : ∀ state next, next ∈ (ProbComp.eval (step state)).support →
+      (stateEncoding next).length ≤ (stateEncoding state).length) :
+    IsPPTOn input stateEncoding (fun a => OracleComp.iterate (count a) step (initial a)) :=
+  IsPPTOn.iterate_of_bounded_growth hcount hinitial hstep (growth := 0) (by simpa using hshrink)
+
+end Cslib.Probability

+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Foundations.Data.BitString.Block
+public import Mathlib.Data.List.OfFn
+
+/-!
+# Bit strings represented by lists
+
+Fixed-width views of ordinary lists pad missing bits with `false`. A flat list can also be read
+as a specified number of fixed-width rows. The representation uses the existing `blocksEquiv`;
+row extraction is ordinary dropping, padding and taking, including on short or empty lists.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.BitString.ofList`: a fixed-width view of a list.
+* `Cslib.BitString.listRow`, `Cslib.BitString.listRows`: fixed-width rows of a flat list.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.BitString.ofList_ofFn`, `Cslib.BitString.ofFn_ofList`: representation round trips.
+* `Cslib.BitString.listRows_eq_ofFn`: agreement with the finite block representation.
+
+## References
+
+Adapted from `Probability/WordBits.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, reusing the shared bit-string block equivalence.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.BitString
+
+/-- View a list as `n` bits, padding missing bits with `false`. -/
+def ofList (n : ℕ) (word : List Bool) : BitString n := fun i => word.getD i.val false
+
+@[simp] theorem ofList_ofFn {n : ℕ} (bits : BitString n) :
+    ofList n (List.ofFn bits) = bits := by
+  funext i
+  simp [ofList]
+
+/-- A list of the declared width loses no data through the finite representation. -/
+theorem ofFn_ofList {n : ℕ} {word : List Bool} (hlen : word.length = n) :
+    List.ofFn (ofList n word) = word := by
+  subst n
+  apply List.ext_getElem (by simp)
+  intro i hi hi'
+  simp [ofList, List.getD, List.getElem?_eq_getElem hi']
+
+/-- Read one fixed-width row, using `false` beyond the end of the supplied list. -/
+def listRow (width row : ℕ) (word : List Bool) : List Bool :=
+  (word.drop (row * width) ++ List.replicate width false).take width
+
+@[simp] theorem length_listRow (width row : ℕ) (word : List Bool) :
+    (listRow width row word).length = width := by
+  simp [listRow]
+
+/-- List slicing agrees with the finite block representation, even on short input lists. -/
+theorem listRow_eq_ofFn {count : ℕ} (width : ℕ) (row : Fin count) (word : List Bool) :
+    listRow width row.val word = List.ofFn (block (ofList (count * width) word) row) := by
+  apply List.ext_getElem (by simp)
+  intro column hleft hright
+  simp only [length_listRow] at hleft
+  by_cases h : column + width * row.val < word.length <;>
+    simp [listRow, ofList, block, List.getElem_take, List.getElem_append,
+      List.getElem_drop, List.getD, Nat.lt_sub_iff_add_lt,
+      Nat.add_comm, Nat.mul_comm, h]
+
+/-- Read a specified number of rows, retaining empty rows when the width is zero. -/
+def listRows (count width : ℕ) (word : List Bool) : List (List Bool) :=
+  (List.range count).map (fun row => listRow width row word)
+
+@[simp] theorem length_listRows (count width : ℕ) (word : List Bool) :
+    (listRows count width word).length = count := by
+  simp [listRows]
+
+/-- Every extracted row has the declared width. -/
+theorem length_of_mem_listRows {count width : ℕ} {word row : List Bool}
+    (hrow : row ∈ listRows count width word) : row.length = width := by
+  obtain ⟨index, _, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hrow
+  simp
+
+/-- Extracting rows gives the list representation of the existing finite block view. -/
+theorem listRows_eq_ofFn (count width : ℕ) (word : List Bool) :
+    listRows count width word =
+      List.ofFn (fun row => List.ofFn (block (ofList (count * width) word) row)) := by
+  apply List.ext_getElem (by simp)
+  intro row hleft hright
+  simpa only [listRows, List.getElem_map, List.getElem_range, List.getElem_ofFn] using
+    listRow_eq_ofFn width ⟨row, by simpa using hright⟩ word
+
+end Cslib.BitString

+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.Basic
+public import Mathlib.Data.List.OfFn
