@@ -0,0 +1,152 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Probabilistic.Closed
+public import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.BitString
+
+/-!
+# A uniform word sampler
+
+One fixed machine with one control state and no work tapes scans its input, emitting a fresh fair
+bit per symbol and halting at the right boundary. On an input of length `n` it writes a uniform
+word of length `n` in exactly `n + 1` transitions. The last transition samples and discards a coin,
+as the common interpreter does on every live instruction; the results below concern closed
+distributions, not equality of programs with different numbers of coin queries.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.uniformListMachine`: the finite uniform scanner.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.eval_uniformListMachine`: uniform output at the linear clock.
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.uniformListMachine_halted`: every run has halted at that clock.
+
+## References
+
+Adapted from `Cslib/Computability/Probabilistic/Sampling.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the common machine and input length.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapePTM
+
+open Cslib MultiTapeMachine
+
+/-- Emit one fair bit per input symbol, then halt without using work tapes. -/
+def uniformListMachine : MultiTapePTM 0 Bool Unit where
+  initial := ()
+  tr _ symbol _ _ bit := .step
+    { inputTape := if symbol.isSome then 1 else 0
+      workTapes := Fin.elim0
+      output := if symbol.isSome then some bit else none
+      state := if symbol.isSome then some () else none }
+    Empty.elim Empty.elim
+
+namespace UniformListMachine
+
+/-- The scanner at an input position, with the output written so far. -/
+def config (input : List Bool) (state : Option Unit) (index : ℕ) (output : List Bool)
+    (h : index ≤ input.length) : Config 0 Bool Unit Empty input where
+  tapes :=
+    { state := state
+      inputPos := ⟨index + 1, by lia⟩
+      workTapes := Fin.elim0
+      workTapePos := Fin.elim0
+      output := output }
+
+/-- Reading any remaining symbol writes the sampled bit and advances once. -/
+theorem step {input output : List Bool} {index : ℕ} (h : index < input.length) (bit : Bool) :
+    (config input (some ()) index output (by lia)).step
+      { inputTape := 1, workTapes := Fin.elim0, output := some bit, state := some () }
+      Empty.elim Empty.elim =
+      config input (some ()) (index + 1) (output ++ [bit]) h := by
+  refine Config.ext ?_ (funext fun oracle => oracle.elim)
+  refine Cfg.ext_zero_tapes rfl ?_ rfl
+  apply Fin.ext
+  change (moveInputPos _ .pos).val = index + 1 + 1
+  rw [moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right _ (by simp only [config]; lia)]
+  rfl
+
+/-- The complete configuration distribution after scanning the remaining suffix and halting. -/
+theorem eval_run_config (input : List Bool) (remaining : ℕ) :
+    ∀ (index : ℕ) (output : List Bool) (h : index + remaining = input.length),
+      ProbComp.eval (uniformListMachine.runClosedConfigFrom (remaining + 1)
+        (config input (some ()) index output (by lia))) =
+        (BitString.uniformList remaining).map
+          (fun tail => config input none input.length (output ++ tail) le_rfl) := by
+  induction remaining with
+  | zero =>
+    intro index output h
+    have hi : index = input.length := by lia
+    subst index
+    have hsym := inputSymbol_eq_none_of_boundary (cfg :=
+      (config input (some ()) input.length output le_rfl).tapes)
+      (Or.inr (by simp [config]))
+    rw [runClosedConfigFrom, runConfigFrom, MultiTapeMachine.runConfigFrom]
+    simp only [
+      show (config input (some ()) input.length output le_rfl).tapes.state = some () from rfl,
+      uniformListMachine, hsym, Option.isSome_none, Bool.false_eq_true, ↓reduceIte, bind_map_left]
+    simp only [MultiTapeMachine.runConfigFrom, ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_pure,
+      PMF.bind_const, BitString.uniformList_zero, PMF.pure_map, List.append_nil]
+    congr 1
+    refine Config.ext ?_ (funext fun oracle => oracle.elim)
+    exact Cfg.ext_zero_tapes rfl (by simp [Config.step, config, Turing.Action.apply])
+      (by simp [Config.step, config, Turing.Action.apply])
+  | succ remaining ih =>
+    intro index output h
+    have hi : index < input.length := by lia
+    have hsym := inputSymbolInner (cfg :=
+      (config input (some ()) index output (by lia)).tapes) index (by simp [config]; lia) hi
+    rw [runClosedConfigFrom, runConfigFrom, MultiTapeMachine.runConfigFrom]
+    simp only [
+      show (config input (some ()) index output (by lia)).tapes.state = some () from rfl,
+      hsym, uniformListMachine, Option.isSome_some, ↓reduceIte, bind_map_left, step hi]
+    change (ProbComp.eval (ProbComp.uniform Bool >>= fun bit =>
+      uniformListMachine.runClosedConfigFrom (remaining + 1)
+        (config input (some ()) (index + 1) (output ++ [bit]) hi))) = _
+    simp only [ProbComp.eval_bind, ProbComp.eval_uniform, ih (index + 1) _ (by lia),
+      BitString.uniformList_succ, PMF.map_bind, PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def,
+      List.append_assoc, List.singleton_append]
+
+end UniformListMachine
+
+/-- The final configuration retains the generated word and has halted at the right boundary. -/
+theorem eval_runClosedConfig_uniformListMachine (input : List Bool) :
+    ProbComp.eval (uniformListMachine.runClosedConfigFrom (input.length + 1)
+      (uniformListMachine.initialConfig input)) =
+      (BitString.uniformList input.length).map
+        (fun output => UniformListMachine.config input none input.length output le_rfl) := by
+  have hcfg : uniformListMachine.initialConfig input =
+      UniformListMachine.config input (some ()) 0 [] (Nat.zero_le _) := by
+    refine Config.ext ?_ rfl
+    exact Cfg.ext_zero_tapes rfl rfl rfl
+  rw [hcfg]
+  simpa only [List.nil_append] using
+    UniformListMachine.eval_run_config input input.length 0 [] (by lia)
+
+/-- The scanner outputs a uniform word of the input length in a linear number of transitions. -/
+theorem eval_uniformListMachine (input : List Bool) :
+    ProbComp.eval (uniformListMachine.runClosed (input.length + 1) input) =
+      BitString.uniformList input.length := by
+  rw [runClosed_eq_map, ProbComp.eval_map, eval_runClosedConfig_uniformListMachine,
+    PMF.map_comp]
+  exact PMF.map_id _
+
+/-- Every supported configuration has actually halted by the linear clock. -/
+theorem uniformListMachine_halted (input : List Bool) :
+    ∀ final ∈ (ProbComp.eval (uniformListMachine.runClosedConfigFrom (input.length + 1)
+      (uniformListMachine.initialConfig input))).support, final.tapes.state = none := by
+  intro final hfinal
+  rw [eval_runClosedConfig_uniformListMachine] at hfinal
+  obtain ⟨output, _, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp hfinal
+  rfl
+
+end Turing.MultiTapePTM

+/-

+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Languages.Probabilistic.Basic
+public import Complexity.Probability.BitString
+
+/-!
+# Sampling bit strings one fair bit at a time
+
+`BitString.sampleList n` is an ordinary recursive program drawing `n` independent Boolean values.
+Its distribution is the uniform law on lists of exactly that length. Computational efficiency is
+certified separately in `Computability.Probabilistic.Sampling`.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.BitString.sampleList`: sample a word using only fair Boolean choices.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.BitString.eval_sampleList`: agreement with the finite uniform distribution.
+
+## References
+
+Adapted from `Cslib/Languages/Probabilistic/BitString.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the typed `PFunctor.FreeM` program interface.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.BitString
+
+/-- Sample `n` independent fair bits, returned in sampling order. -/
+noncomputable def sampleList : ℕ → ProbComp (List Bool)
+  | 0 => pure []
+  | n + 1 => do
+    let bit ← ProbComp.uniform Bool
+    return bit :: (← sampleList n)
+
+/-- The operational fair-bit sampler has the finite uniform word distribution. -/
+@[simp] theorem eval_sampleList (n : ℕ) : ProbComp.eval (sampleList n) = uniformList n := by
+  induction n with
+  | zero => simp [sampleList]
+  | succ n ih => simp [sampleList, uniformList_succ, ih]
+
+end Cslib.BitString
diff --git a/Complexity/Probability/BitString.lean b/Complexity/Probability/BitString.lean
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..3cd629a2
--- /dev/null
+++ b/Complexity/Probability/BitString.lean
@@ -0,0 +1,139 @@
+/-
+Copyright (c) 2026 Samuel Schlesinger. All rights reserved.
+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Probability.PMF
+public import Mathlib.Data.Fintype.Pi
+public import Mathlib.Data.List.OfFn
+public import Mathlib.Data.Vector.Basic
+
+/-!
+# Uniform binary strings
+
+Uniform sampling from `Fin n → Bool`, represented as a list. The recursive equations connect
+this finite uniform distribution to a program drawing one independent fair bit at a time.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Cslib.BitString.uniformList`: uniform fixed-length words represented as lists.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.BitString.uniformList_succ`, `Cslib.BitString.uniformList_add`: independent decomposition.
+* `Cslib.BitString.mem_support_uniformList_iff`: support is exactly the requested length.
+* `Cslib.BitString.uniformList_map_of_bijective`: length-preserving permutations preserve
+  uniformity.
+
+## References
+
+Adapted from `Cslib/Probability/BitString.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, placed in the shared bit-string namespace.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Cslib.BitString
+
+open Probability
+
+/-- The uniform distribution on binary words of exactly `n` bits. -/
+noncomputable def uniformList (n : ℕ) : PMF (List Bool) :=
+  (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin n → Bool)).map List.ofFn
+
+@[simp] theorem uniformList_zero : uniformList 0 = PMF.pure [] := by
+  simp [uniformList, PMF.map, Function.comp_def]
+
+/-- A uniform nonempty string consists of a fair first bit and an independent uniform tail. -/
+theorem uniformList_succ (n : ℕ) :
+    uniformList (n + 1) = (PMF.uniformOfFintype Bool).bind
+      (fun bit => (uniformList n).map (List.cons bit)) := by
+  unfold uniformList
+  rw [← PMF.uniformOfFintype_map_equiv (Fin.consEquiv (fun _ : Fin (n + 1) => Bool)),
+    PMF.map_comp, ← PMF.uniformOfFintype_prod]
+  simp [PMF.map_bind, PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def, Fin.consEquiv]
+
+/-- Concatenating independent uniform words gives a uniform word of the combined length. -/
+theorem uniformList_add (m n : ℕ) :
+    uniformList (m + n) = (uniformList m).bind
+      (fun left => (uniformList n).map (left ++ ·)) := by
+  induction m with
+  | zero => simp [PMF.map, Function.comp_def]
+  | succ m ih =>
+    rw [Nat.succ_add, uniformList_succ, ih, uniformList_succ]
+    simp [PMF.map_bind, PMF.bind_map, PMF.map_comp, PMF.bind_bind, Function.comp_def]
+
+/-- Appending one independent fair bit gives a uniform word one bit longer. -/
+theorem uniformList_snoc (n : ℕ) :
+    uniformList (n + 1) = (uniformList n).bind
+      (fun word => (PMF.uniformOfFintype Bool).map (fun bit => word ++ [bit])) := by
+  rw [uniformList_add n 1, uniformList_succ 0]
+  simp [PMF.map, Function.comp_def]
+
+/-- Every sampled word has exactly the requested length. -/
+theorem length_of_mem_support_uniformList {n : ℕ} {word : List Bool}
+    (h : word ∈ (uniformList n).support) : word.length = n := by
+  obtain ⟨bits, _, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp h
+  simp
+
+/-- Every word of the requested length has positive uniform probability, and no other word does. -/
+theorem mem_support_uniformList_iff {n : ℕ} {word : List Bool} :
+    word ∈ (uniformList n).support ↔ word.length = n := by
+  refine ⟨length_of_mem_support_uniformList, fun h => ?_⟩
+  subst n
+  exact (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mpr
+    ⟨word.get, by simp, List.ofFn_get _⟩
+
+/-- Splitting a uniform tape gives two independent tapes, also when either length is zero. -/
+theorem uniformList_bind_split {α : Type*} (first second : ℕ)
+    (next : List Bool → List Bool → PMF α) :
+    (uniformList (first + second)).bind (fun tape => next (tape.take first) (tape.drop first)) =
+      (uniformList first).bind (fun front => (uniformList second).bind (next front)) := by
+  rw [uniformList_add, PMF.bind_bind]
+  apply PMF.bind_congr_on_support
+  intro front hfront
+  rw [PMF.bind_map]

+    change List.ofFn (List.Vector.get (e (List.Vector.ofFn word))) = _
+    rw [← List.Vector.toList_ofFn, List.Vector.ofFn_get]
+    change f (List.Vector.ofFn word).toList = _
+    rw [List.Vector.toList_ofFn]
+  calc
+    (uniformList n).map f = ((PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin n → Bool)).map bits).map List.ofFn := by
+      simp only [uniformList, PMF.map_comp]
+      congr 1
+      funext word
+      exact (hbits word).symm
+    _ = uniformList n := by rw [PMF.uniformOfFintype_map_equiv]; rfl

+/-

+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Tactic.PolyTime
+public import Complexity.Computability.Probabilistic.PPT.Capture
+public import Complexity.Computability.Probabilistic.Sampling
+
+/-!
+# Certifying functional probabilistic programs
+
+`ppt` combines the proved closed PPT rules with deterministic `polytime` automation. Programs
+use ordinary `do` notation, captured inputs and conditionals. Named and local certificates are
+tried before generic composition, and tuple arguments are prepared with the shared routine-call
+matcher. Every proof supplies the uniform strict fair-coin machine contract of `IsPPTOn`.
+
+Unknown algorithms need certificates. Fair-bit sampling is the only primitive here. Sampling
+uniform bitstrings of runtime length, probabilistic loops and oracle PPT need further rules.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `ppt`: prove a closed encoded PPT certificate using the `PPT` and `PolyTime` Aesop rule sets.
+
+## References
+
+Adapted from `Cslib/Tactic/PPT.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the common machine realization and tidy calculus.
+-/
+
+public section
+
+namespace Cslib.Tactic.PPT
+
+open Lean Meta Elab Tactic Probability
+
+/-- Prepare local probabilistic routine calls through the same matcher as deterministic calls. -/
+@[aesop safe -40 tactic (rule_sets := [PPT])]
+private meta def pptKnownCall : TacticM Unit :=
+  Cslib.Tactic.applyKnownCall ``IsPPTOn 4 ``IsPPTOn.preprocess `prepare `hprogram `hprepare
+
+/-- Use a named certificate before unfolding its program. -/
+@[aesop safe -30 tactic (rule_sets := [PPT])]
+private meta def pptCertificate : TacticM Unit :=
+  Cslib.Tactic.applyCertificate ``IsPPTOn
+
+/-- Let compositional rules finish a goal before exposing individual monadic binds. -/
+@[aesop safe -20 tactic (rule_sets := [PPT])]
+private meta def pptFunProp : TacticM Unit :=
+  withMainContext <| Term.withoutErrToSorry <| withoutRecover do
+    unless (← getMainTarget).isAppOf ``IsPPTOn do
+      throwError "expected an encoded-input PPT goal"
+    evalTactic (← `(tactic| solve | fun_prop (config := { maxSteps := 128 })))
+
+attribute [program_certificate]
+  Turing.MultiTapeTM.ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.isPPTOn
+  isPPTOn_uniform_bool
+
+/-- Let either the sampler or continuation determine the intermediate encoding. Commit only
+after both premises are proved, so an unsuitable choice cannot hide the other order. -/
+@[aesop safe 10 tactic (rule_sets := [PPT])]
+private meta def pptCaptured : TacticM Unit :=
+  withMainContext <| focus <| Term.withoutErrToSorry <| withoutRecover do
+    let target := (← Core.betaReduce (← instantiateMVars (← getMainTarget))).consumeMData
+    unless target.isAppOf ``IsPPTOn do throwError "expected an encoded-input PPT goal"
+    let isBind ← lambdaTelescope target.getAppArgs.back! fun _ body => do
+      if body.isAppOf ``Bind.bind then return true
+      if body.isAppOf ``Functor.map then return false
+      throwError "expected probabilistic sequencing"
+    let (rule, sampler, continuation) := if isBind then
+      (``IsPPTOn.bind_with, `hfirst, `hsecond) else (``IsPPTOn.map_with, `hprogram, `hf)
+    for samplerFirst in [true, false] do
+      let saved ← saveState
+      try
+        liftMetaTactic fun goal => goal.applyConst rule
+        Cslib.Tactic.solveTagged (if samplerFirst then sampler else continuation)
+        Cslib.Tactic.solveTagged (if samplerFirst then continuation else sampler)
+        return
+      catch _ => saved.restore
+    throwError "no compatible encoding for the sampler and continuation"
+
+/-- Certify a probabilistic program using proved sampling, composition and deterministic rules. -/
+macro "ppt" : tactic => `(tactic| solve | aesop (rule_sets := [PPT, PolyTime]))
+
+end Cslib.Tactic.PPT

+    let program := target.getAppArgs[programIndex]!
+    if program.hasExprMVar then throwError "the called program is not determined"
+    let head ← lambdaTelescope (← Core.betaReduce (← etaExpand program)) fun _ body =>
+      pure body.getAppFn
+    for decl in ← getLCtx do
+      if decl.isImplementationDetail || !decl.type.isAppOf predicate then continue
+      let certified := decl.type.getAppArgs[programIndex]!
+      let called ← lambdaTelescope (← Core.betaReduce (← etaExpand certified)) fun _ body =>
+        pure body.getAppFn
+      unless called == head do continue
+      let saved ← saveState
+      try
+        let argument ← prepareArgument target.getAppArgs[0]! decl.type.getAppArgs[0]!
+        let composed ← withLocalDeclD `input target.getAppArgs[0]! fun input =>
+          mkLambdaFVars #[input] (mkApp certified (mkApp argument input))
+        unless ← isDefEq (← withReducible (reduce composed)) program do
+          throwError "the certificate does not match this call"
+        applyWithArguments rule #[(argumentName, argument), (certificateName, decl.toExpr)]
+        if ← (← getGoals).anyM (fun goal => do isDefEq (← goal.getType) target) then
+          throwError "composition made no progress"
+        solveTagged argumentGoal
+        return
+      catch _ => saved.restore
+    throwError "no applicable local routine certificate"
+
 end Cslib.Tactic

+/-

+Authors: Samuel Schlesinger
+-/
+
+module
+-- upstream: candidate
+
+public import Complexity.Computability.Machines.Turing.MultiTape.Machine.Simulation
+
+/-!
+# Retaining an existing output prefix
+
+A machine cannot read its output. Prepending a word to that output therefore preserves its
+entire execution program, including stateful choices and oracle interactions. This is a
+configuration invariance law; writing the prefix remains separate, charged machine work.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeMachine.Config.prependOutput`: prepend a word to the ordinary output.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeMachine.runConfigFrom_prependOutput`: retain the prefix throughout execution.
+
+## References
+
+Adapted from `Computability/Machines/Turing/MultiTape/Oracle/OutputPrefix.lean` on the cslib
+`crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using upstream's configuration operation and the
+common one-step program simulation rule.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeMachine
+
+open Cslib
+
+universe u v
+
+variable {k : ℕ} {Symbol State Oracle : Type} {Query : Type u}
+  {Choose : Type → Type v} {spec : OracleSpec.{u, 0} Query} {input : List Symbol}
+
+/-- Change only the unreadable output, retaining all communication channels. -/
+def Config.prependOutput (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) (pre : List Symbol) :
+    Config k Symbol State Oracle input :=
+  { cfg with tapes := cfg.tapes.prependOutput pre }
+
+@[simp] theorem Config.prependOutput_state (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input)
+    (pre : List Symbol) : (cfg.prependOutput pre).tapes.state = cfg.tapes.state := rfl
+
+@[simp] theorem Config.prependOutput_inputSymbol (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input)
+    (pre : List Symbol) : (cfg.prependOutput pre).tapes.inputSymbol = cfg.tapes.inputSymbol := rfl
+
+@[simp] theorem Config.prependOutput_workTapeSymbols (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input)
+    (pre : List Symbol) :
+    (cfg.prependOutput pre).tapes.workTapeSymbols = cfg.tapes.workTapeSymbols := rfl
+
+@[simp] theorem Config.prependOutput_channels (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input)
+    (pre : List Symbol) : (cfg.prependOutput pre).channels = cfg.channels := rfl
+
+@[simp] theorem Config.prependOutput_answerSymbols (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input)
+    (pre : List Symbol) : (cfg.prependOutput pre).answerSymbols = cfg.answerSymbols := rfl
+
+@[simp] theorem Config.prependOutput_output (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input)
+    (pre : List Symbol) : (cfg.prependOutput pre).tapes.output = pre ++ cfg.tapes.output := rfl
+
+theorem Config.step_prependOutput (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) (pre : List Symbol)
+    (action : Turing.Action k Symbol State) (symbol : Oracle → Option Symbol)
+    (move : Oracle → SignType) :
+    (cfg.prependOutput pre).step action symbol move =

+/-!
+# Writing a prefix before a probabilistic computation
+
+A deterministic preparation restores the input head and blank work tapes after writing a prefix.
+Shared-tape sequencing then runs the probabilistic source on its original input. Both phases
+actually halt within the sum of their bounds; every instruction of preparation is charged.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.eval_runClosedConfigFrom_seq_prependOutput`: retain a prepared prefix.
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.seq_prependOutput_halted`: add the two actual halting bounds.
+

+branch at `5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the shared sequencing compiler.

+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapePTM
+
+open Cslib MultiTapeMachine
+
+variable {k : ℕ} {Symbol State State₀ State₁ : Type} {input : List Symbol}
+
+/-- An unreadable output prefix preserves the entire closed execution program. -/
+theorem runClosedConfigFrom_prependOutput (machine : MultiTapePTM k Symbol State)
+    (fuel : ℕ) (cfg : Config k Symbol State Empty input) (pre : List Symbol) :
+    machine.runClosedConfigFrom fuel (cfg.prependOutput pre) =
+      (fun final => final.prependOutput pre) <$> machine.runClosedConfigFrom fuel cfg :=
+  MultiTapeMachine.runConfigFrom_prependOutput machine _ _ fuel cfg pre
+
+variable (prepare : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State₀) (source : MultiTapePTM k Symbol State₁)
+  (input pre : List Symbol) (prepareTime runTime : ℕ)
+  (hprepare : prepare.runFrom (prepare.initCfg input) prepareTime =
+    wordsCfg input none (fun _ => []) pre)
+  (hsource : ∀ final ∈ (ProbComp.eval
+    (source.runClosedConfigFrom runTime (source.initialConfig input))).support,
+    final.tapes.state = none)
+
+include hprepare hsource
+
+/-- A workspace-restoring preparation retains the prefix and the source distribution. -/
+theorem eval_runClosedConfigFrom_seq_prependOutput :
+    ProbComp.eval (((ofDeterministic prepare).seq source).runClosedConfigFrom
+      (prepareTime + runTime) (((ofDeterministic prepare).seq source).initialConfig input)) =
+      (ProbComp.eval (source.runClosedConfigFrom runTime (source.initialConfig input))).map
+        (fun final => Sequential.right (final.prependOutput pre)) := by
+  let cfg : Config k Symbol State₀ Empty input := (ofDeterministic prepare).initialConfig input
+  let ready : Config k Symbol State₀ Empty input :=
+    { tapes := wordsCfg input none (fun _ => []) pre }
+  have hfirst : ProbComp.eval ((ofDeterministic prepare).runClosedConfigFrom prepareTime cfg) =
+      PMF.pure ready := by
+    rw [eval_runClosedConfigFrom_ofDeterministic]
+    change PMF.pure ({ tapes := prepare.runFrom (prepare.initCfg input) prepareTime } :
+      Config k Symbol State₀ Empty input) = _
+    rw [hprepare]
+  have hstart : Sequential.start source ready = (source.initialConfig input).prependOutput pre := by
+    simp [Sequential.start, ready, initialConfig, Config.prependOutput,
+      Cfg.prependOutput, wordsCfg, Cfg.withState]
+  have hsecond : ∀ final ∈ (ProbComp.eval
+      (source.runClosedConfigFrom runTime (Sequential.start source ready))).support,
+      final.tapes.state = none := by
+    intro final hfinal
+    rw [hstart, runClosedConfigFrom_prependOutput, ProbComp.eval_map] at hfinal
+    obtain ⟨original, horiginal, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp hfinal
+    exact hsource original horiginal
+  change ProbComp.eval (((ofDeterministic prepare).seq source).runClosedConfigFrom
+    _ (Sequential.left source cfg)) = _
+  rw [eval_runClosedConfigFrom_seq _ _ _ prepareTime runTime
+    (by simp [hfirst, ready]) (by simpa [hfirst] using hsecond),
+    hfirst, PMF.pure_bind, hstart, runClosedConfigFrom_prependOutput, ProbComp.eval_map,
+    PMF.map_comp]
+  rfl
+
+/-- The prepared-prefix computation actually halts within the sum of the phase bounds. -/
+theorem seq_prependOutput_halted :
+    ∀ final ∈ (ProbComp.eval (((ofDeterministic prepare).seq source).runClosedConfigFrom
+      (prepareTime + runTime)
+      (((ofDeterministic prepare).seq source).initialConfig input))).support,
+      final.tapes.state = none := by
+  intro final hfinal
+  rw [eval_runClosedConfigFrom_seq_prependOutput prepare source input pre prepareTime runTime
+    hprepare hsource] at hfinal
+  obtain ⟨original, horiginal, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp hfinal
+  change original.tapes.state.map Sum.inr = none
+  rw [hsource original horiginal]
+  rfl
+
+/-- The final output consists of the prepared prefix followed by the sampled source output. -/
+theorem eval_seq_prependOutput :
+    ProbComp.eval (((ofDeterministic prepare).seq source).runClosed
+      (prepareTime + runTime) input) =
+      (ProbComp.eval (source.runClosed runTime input)).map (pre ++ ·) := by
+  simp only [runClosed_eq_map, ProbComp.eval_map,
+    eval_runClosedConfigFrom_seq_prependOutput prepare source input pre prepareTime runTime
+      hprepare hsource, PMF.map_comp]
+  rfl
+
+end Turing.MultiTapePTM

+/-!
+# Captured inputs in efficient probabilistic programs
+
+Ordinary monadic continuations and callbacks may use both the caller's input and a sampled
+result. A tidy deterministic routine writes the retained data before the sampler runs; the
+existing pair encoding makes this a typed value for the next computation. The machine proof
+charges all copying, framing and preparation, without exposing those details to clients.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.pair`: retain efficiently computed data alongside a sampled result.
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.bind_with`: a monadic continuation may capture the original input.
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.map_with`: a deterministic callback may capture the original input.
+* `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.cond`, `Cslib.Probability.IsPPTOn.ite`: efficient branch selection.
+
+## References

+Adapted from `Computability/Probabilistic/{Realization/Composition,Composition}.lean` on the cslib
+`crypto` branch at `5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the existing tidy calculus
+and framed pair encoding.

+@[expose] public section

+namespace Cslib.Probability

+open Turing Turing.MultiTapeTM Turing.MultiTapePTM Turing.MultiTapeMachine

+/-- Write efficiently computed input data before a probabilistic output, charging preparation. -/
+theorem IsPPTOn.prefix {α : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {pre : α → List Bool}
+    {program : α → ProbComp (List Bool)} (hprogram : IsPPTOn input encBits program)
+    (hprefix : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime pre input encBits) :
+    IsPPTOn input encBits (fun a => (pre a ++ ·) <$> program a) := by
+  obtain ⟨t, s, ⟨ci, di, ht⟩, _, ki, InitState, hfinite, initializer, hi⟩ := hprefix
+  obtain ⟨ks, State, hfinite', source, cs, ds, hsource, hhalt⟩ := hprogram.exists_halting_machine
+  let prep := initializer.extendTapes (Fin.castAddEmb ks)
+  let runner := source.extendTapes (Fin.natAddEmb ki)
+  let compiled := (ofDeterministic prep).seq runner
+  let prepareTime := fun length => ci * (length + 1) ^ di
+  let runTime := fun length => cs * (length + 1) ^ ds
+  have hpoly : PolynomiallyBounded (fun length => prepareTime length + runTime length) := by
+    fun_prop
+  obtain ⟨coefficient, degree, htime⟩ := polynomiallyBounded_iff_le.mp hpoly
+  have hprep (a : α) : prep.runFrom (prep.initCfg (input a)) (prepareTime (input a).length) =
+      wordsCfg (input a) none (fun _ => []) (pre a) :=
+    (((hi a).mono (ht a) le_rfl).extendTapes (Fin.castAddEmb ks)).runFrom_initCfg_eq
+  have hrunner (a : α) : ∀ final ∈ (ProbComp.eval
+      (runner.runClosedConfigFrom (runTime (input a).length)
+        (runner.initialConfig (input a)))).support,
+      final.tapes.state = none := by
+    intro final hfinal
+    simp only [runner, runClosedConfigFrom, initialConfig_extendTapes,
+      MultiTapePTM.runConfigFrom_embed, ProbComp.eval_map] at hfinal
+    obtain ⟨original, horiginal, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp hfinal
+    exact hhalt (input a) original horiginal
+  refine ⟨ki + ks, InitState ⊕ State, inferInstance, compiled, coefficient, degree, fun a => ?_⟩
+  rw [eval_runClosed_eq_of_halted compiled _ (htime (input a).length)
+    (seq_prependOutput_halted prep runner (input a) (pre a) _ _ (hprep a) (hrunner a)),
+    eval_seq_prependOutput prep runner (input a) (pre a) _ _ (hprep a) (hrunner a),
+    runClosed_extendTapes, ← hsource a]
+  simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, encBits, Function.Embedding.coe_refl, PMF.map_id]
+
+variable {α β γ : Type} {input : α ↪ List Bool} {left : β ↪ List Bool}
+  {right : γ ↪ List Bool}
+
+/-- Retain efficiently computed input data beside a sampled result, using the existing encoding. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem IsPPTOn.pair {program : α → ProbComp γ} {f : α → β}
+    (hprogram : IsPPTOn input right program) (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime f input left) :
+    IsPPTOn input (encPair left right) (fun a => (fun b => (f a, b)) <$> program a) := by
+  apply isPPTOn_iff_encoded.mpr
+  have hframe : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun b => frame (left b)) left encBits :=
+    .of_linear (.of_frame fun _ => rfl)
+  refine ((isPPTOn_iff_encoded.mp hprogram).prefix (hframe.comp hf)).congr ?_
+  intro a
+  simp only [ProbComp.eval_map, PMF.map_comp]
+  rfl
+
+/-- Keep the original argument available to a later computation, charging its encoded copy. -/
+theorem IsPPTOn.keep_input {program : α → ProbComp β}
+    (hprogram : IsPPTOn input left program) :
+    IsPPTOn input (encPair input left) (fun a => (fun b => (a, b)) <$> program a) :=
+  hprogram.pair ComputableTidilyInPolyTime.id'
+
+/-- A monadic continuation may use both the caller's input and the sampled result. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem IsPPTOn.bind_with {first : α → ProbComp β} {second : α → β → ProbComp γ}
+    (hfirst : IsPPTOn input left first)
+    (hsecond : IsPPTOn (encPair input left) right (fun pair => second pair.1 pair.2)) :
+    IsPPTOn input right (fun a => do
+      let b ← first a
+      second a b) := by
+  simpa only [bind_map_left] using hfirst.keep_input.bind hsecond
+
+/-- A deterministic callback may capture the original argument. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem IsPPTOn.map_with {program : α → ProbComp β} {f : α → β → γ}
+    (hprogram : IsPPTOn input left program)
+    (hf : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun pair => f pair.1 pair.2) (encPair input left) right) :
+    IsPPTOn input right (fun a => f a <$> program a) := by
+  simpa only [bind_pure_comp] using
+    hprogram.bind_with (right := right) (second := fun a b => pure (f a b)) hf.isPPTOn
+
+/-- Select a closed probabilistic branch with an efficient Boolean condition. A witness may
+run both total branches and discard one result; the sum of their clocks is still polynomial. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem IsPPTOn.cond {condition : α → Bool} {yes no : α → ProbComp β}
+    (hcondition : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime condition input encBool)
+    (hyes : IsPPTOn input left yes) (hno : IsPPTOn input left no) :
+    IsPPTOn input left (fun a => if condition a then yes a else no a) := by
+  have hcombined : IsPPTOn input left (fun a => do
+      let b ← yes a
+      let c ← no a
+      pure (if condition a then b else c)) := by
+    fun_prop
+  apply hcombined.congr
+  intro a
+  cases condition a <;> simp [ProbComp.eval_bind, PMF.map, Function.comp_def]
+
+/-- Select a closed probabilistic branch with an efficiently decidable condition. -/
+@[fun_prop]
+theorem IsPPTOn.ite {condition : α → Prop} [∀ a, Decidable (condition a)]
+    {yes no : α → ProbComp β}
+    (hcondition : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime (fun a => decide (condition a)) input encBool)
+    (hyes : IsPPTOn input left yes) (hno : IsPPTOn input left no) :
+    IsPPTOn input left (fun a => if condition a then yes a else no a) := by
+  simpa only [decide_eq_true_eq] using hyes.cond hcondition hno
+
+end Cslib.Probability

+    (hgenerator : ComputableTidilyInPolyTime generator encBits encBits) :
+    IsPPTOn encBits encBits (fun path => do
+      let seed ← sample path
+      pure (Crypto.GGM.eval generator seed path)) := by
+  fun_prop
+
+-- Branch selection depends on the unbounded input, and both branches are probabilistic.
+example {yes no : List Bool → ProbComp Bool}
+    (hyes : IsPPTOn encBits encBool yes) (hno : IsPPTOn encBits encBool no) :
+    IsPPTOn encBits encBool (fun word => if word = [] then yes word else no word.reverse) := by
+  fun_prop
+
 end ComplexityTests.PPTComposition

+/-!
+# Reading an effectful machine's input from work tapes
+
+Two fresh work tapes hold the virtual input and its left-boundary marker. The compiler reuses
+upstream's clamped-input simulation, retaining all typed choices and oracle interactions. The
+real input head stays at its original position, and the real input is never inspected.
+
+The simulation starts from a prepared virtual input. Preparing these tapes is a separate
+computation whose cost must be included when composing machines.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeMachine.inputFromTape`: read a virtual input without adding instructions.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeMachine.InputFromTape.config`: embed the input and retain all oracle channels.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeMachine.runConfigFrom_inputFromTape`: preserve the complete clocked program.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeMachine.toTM_inputFromTape`: agree with upstream's deterministic compiler.
+
+## References
+
+Adapted from `MultiTape/Oracle/InputFromTape.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the common machine and upstream input redirection
+by Christian Reitwiessner and Samuel Schlesinger.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeMachine
+
+open Cslib
+
+universe u v
+
+variable {k : ℕ} {Symbol State Oracle : Type} {Query : Type u}
+  {Choose : Type → Type v} {spec : OracleSpec.{u, 0} Query} {input : List Symbol}
+
+namespace InputFromTape
+
+/-- Move the virtual input and boundary heads together, clamping at either end. -/
+def action (a : Turing.Action k Symbol State) (symbol flag : Option Symbol) :
+    Turing.Action (k + 2) Symbol State :=
+  { a with
+    inputTape := 0
+    workTapes := Fin.append a.workTapes
+      (fun _ => (none, MultiTapeTM.clampMove symbol flag a.inputTape)) }
+
+/-- Redirect input movement while retaining communication instructions. -/
+def instruction (symbol flag : Option Symbol) :
+    Action k Symbol State Oracle → Action (k + 2) Symbol State Oracle
+  | .step a querySymbol answerMove => .step (action a symbol flag) querySymbol answerMove
+  | .query oracle next => .query oracle next
+
+/-- Embed the source input on work tapes while retaining every communication channel. -/
+def config (mark : Symbol) (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) (outerInput : List Symbol)
+    (outerPosition : Fin (outerInput.length + 2)) : Config (k + 2) Symbol State Oracle outerInput :=
+  { cfg with
+    tapes := { MultiTapeTM.inCfg mark cfg.tapes outerInput with inputPos := outerPosition } }
+
+variable (mark : Symbol) (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) (outerInput : List Symbol)
+  (outerPosition : Fin (outerInput.length + 2))
+
+@[simp] theorem config_state :
+    (config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition).tapes.state = cfg.tapes.state := rfl
+
+@[simp] theorem config_workTapeSymbols (i : Fin k) :
+    (config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition).tapes.workTapeSymbols (i.castAdd 2) =
+      cfg.tapes.workTapeSymbols i :=
+  MultiTapeTM.inCfg_workTapeSymbols_castAdd (outerInput := outerInput) cfg.tapes i
+
+@[simp] theorem config_inputSymbol :
+    (config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition).tapes.workTapeSymbols (Fin.natAdd k 0) =
+      cfg.tapes.inputSymbol :=
+  MultiTapeTM.inCfg_workTapeSymbols_vip (outerInput := outerInput) cfg.tapes
+
+@[simp] theorem config_flagSymbol :
+    (config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition).tapes.workTapeSymbols (Fin.natAdd k 1) =
+      if cfg.tapes.inputPos.val = 0 then some mark else none :=
+  MultiTapeTM.inCfg_workTapeSymbols_flag (outerInput := outerInput) cfg.tapes
+
+@[simp] theorem config_channels :
+    (config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition).channels = cfg.channels := rfl
+
+@[simp] theorem config_answerSymbols :
+    (config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition).answerSymbols = cfg.answerSymbols := rfl
+
+@[simp] theorem config_output :
+    (config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition).tapes.output = cfg.tapes.output := rfl
+
+/-- Upstream's clamped move preserves the virtual input geometry after every instruction. -/
+theorem step_config (a : Turing.Action k Symbol State) (symbol : Oracle → Option Symbol)
+    (move : Oracle → SignType) :
+    (config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition).step
+        (action a cfg.tapes.inputSymbol (if cfg.tapes.inputPos.val = 0 then some mark else none))
+        symbol move = config mark (cfg.step a symbol move) outerInput outerPosition := by
+  refine Config.ext ?_ rfl
+  refine Cfg.ext rfl (by simp [config, Config.step, action, Turing.Action.apply])
+    ?_ ?_ rfl <;> funext i <;> induction i using Fin.addCases <;>
+    simp [config, Config.step, action, Turing.Action.apply, MultiTapeTM.inCfg,
+      MultiTapeTM.val_moveInputPos_sub_one_eq_clampMove mark]
+
+theorem receive_config [DecidableEq Oracle] (oracle : Oracle) (next : State)
+    (answer : List Symbol) :
+    (config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition).receive oracle next answer =
+      config mark (cfg.receive oracle next answer) outerInput outerPosition := rfl
+
+end InputFromTape
+
+/-- Read the input from two fresh work tapes: a word and its boundary marker. -/
+@[simps! initial] def inputFromTape [Functor Choose]
+    (machine : MultiTapeMachine k Symbol State Oracle Choose) :
+    MultiTapeMachine (k + 2) Symbol State Oracle Choose where
+  initial := machine.initial
+  tr state _ work answer :=
+    InputFromTape.instruction (work (Fin.natAdd k 0)) (work (Fin.natAdd k 1)) <$>
+      machine.tr state (work (Fin.natAdd k 0)) (fun i => work (i.castAdd 2)) answer
+
+/-- Unfold a single virtual-input transition without unfolding its machine in continuations. -/
+theorem inputFromTape_tr [Functor Choose] (machine : MultiTapeMachine k Symbol State Oracle Choose)
+    (state : State) (symbol : Option Symbol) (work : Fin (k + 2) → Option Symbol)
+    (answer : Oracle → Option Symbol) :
+    machine.inputFromTape.tr state symbol work answer =
+      InputFromTape.instruction (work (Fin.natAdd k 0)) (work (Fin.natAdd k 1)) <$>
+        machine.tr state (work (Fin.natAdd k 0)) (fun i => work (i.castAdd 2)) answer := rfl
+
+variable [Functor Choose] [DecidableEq Oracle]
+  (machine : MultiTapeMachine k Symbol State Oracle Choose)
+  (choose : {α : Type} → Choose α → OracleComp spec α)
+  (hchoose : ∀ {α β : Type} (f : α → β) (choices : Choose α),
+    choose (f <$> choices) = f <$> choose choices)
+  (query : Oracle → List Symbol → OracleComp spec (List Symbol))
+
+include hchoose
+
+/-- Virtual input preserves the complete program, including communication and private state. -/
+theorem runConfigFrom_inputFromTape (mark : Symbol) (fuel : ℕ)
+    (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) (outerInput : List Symbol)
+    (outerPosition : Fin (outerInput.length + 2)) :
+    machine.inputFromTape.runConfigFrom choose query fuel
+        (InputFromTape.config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition) =
+      (fun final => InputFromTape.config mark final outerInput outerPosition) <$>
+        machine.runConfigFrom choose query fuel cfg := by
+  apply runConfigFrom_map machine machine.inputFromTape choose choose query query
+    (fun cfg => InputFromTape.config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition)
+  intro cfg
+  cases hs : cfg.tapes.state with
+  | none => simp [runConfigFrom, hs]
+  | some state =>
+    simp only [runConfigFrom, InputFromTape.config_state, hs,
+      InputFromTape.config_workTapeSymbols, InputFromTape.config_inputSymbol,
+      InputFromTape.config_flagSymbol, InputFromTape.config_answerSymbols, inputFromTape_tr,
+      hchoose, bind_map_left, map_bind]
+    congr 1
+    funext a
+    cases a <;> simp only [InputFromTape.instruction, InputFromTape.step_config,
+      InputFromTape.receive_config, InputFromTape.config_channels, map_pure, map_bind]
+
+/-- The virtual-input compiler emits exactly the source output program. -/
+theorem runFrom_inputFromTape (mark : Symbol) (fuel : ℕ)
+    (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) (outerInput : List Symbol)
+    (outerPosition : Fin (outerInput.length + 2)) :
+    machine.inputFromTape.runFrom choose query fuel
+        (InputFromTape.config mark cfg outerInput outerPosition) =
+      machine.runFrom choose query fuel cfg := by
+  simp [runFrom, runConfigFrom_inputFromTape machine choose hchoose query]
+
+omit hchoose in
+/-- Effect-free deterministic input redirection is exactly upstream's compiler. -/
+theorem toTM_inputFromTape (machine : MultiTapeMachine k Symbol State Empty Id) :
+    machine.inputFromTape.toTM = machine.toTM.inputFromTape := by
+  simp only [toTM, MultiTapeTM.inputFromTape, MultiTapeTM.tr_ofTr, inputFromTape]
+  congr 1
+  funext state symbol work
+  cases machine.tr state (work (Fin.natAdd k 0)) (fun i => work (i.castAdd 2)) Empty.elim with
+  | step a symbol move => rfl
+  | query oracle next => exact oracle.elim
+
+end Turing.MultiTapeMachine

+/-!
+# Buffering an effectful machine's output
+
+The output is redirected to a fresh last work tape, whose head remains at the write frontier.
+The real output stays empty. All choices and oracle interactions are preserved as a typed
+program, so this construction also retains state shared by coin and query interpreters.
+
+The configuration map reuses upstream's `outCfg`. No budget or already computed output is
+supplied to the machine: an initially blank buffer is filled one source instruction at a time.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeMachine.outputToTape`: buffer the source output without adding instructions.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeMachine.OutputToTape.config`: retain source data and communication channels.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeMachine.runConfigFrom_outputToTape`: preserve the whole clocked program.
+* `Turing.MultiTapeMachine.toTM_outputToTape`: agree exactly with upstream's deterministic compiler.
+
+## References
+
+Adapted from `MultiTape/Oracle/OutputToTape.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, using the common machine and upstream output redirection
+by Christian Reitwiessner and Samuel Schlesinger.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeMachine
+
+open Cslib
+
+universe u v
+
+variable {k : ℕ} {Symbol State Oracle : Type} {Query : Type u}
+  {Choose : Type → Type v} {spec : OracleSpec.{u, 0} Query} {input : List Symbol}
+
+namespace OutputToTape
+
+/-- Redirect an emitted symbol to the fresh work tape and advance its write frontier. -/
+def action (a : Turing.Action k Symbol State) : Turing.Action (k + 1) Symbol State where
+  inputTape := a.inputTape
+  workTapes := Fin.lastCases
+    (match a.output with
+      | none => (none, 0)
+      | some symbol => (some (some symbol), 1)) a.workTapes
+  output := none
+  state := a.state
+
+/-- Redirect ordinary output writes while retaining communication instructions. -/
+def instruction : Action k Symbol State Oracle → Action (k + 1) Symbol State Oracle
+  | .step a symbol move => .step (action a) symbol move
+  | .query oracle next => .query oracle next
+
+/-- Upstream's output-buffered configuration, with every communication channel retained. -/
+def config (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) : Config (k + 1) Symbol State Oracle input :=
+  { cfg with tapes := MultiTapeTM.outCfg cfg.tapes }
+
+@[simp] theorem config_state (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) :
+    (config cfg).tapes.state = cfg.tapes.state := rfl
+
+@[simp] theorem config_inputSymbol (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) :
+    (config cfg).tapes.inputSymbol = cfg.tapes.inputSymbol := rfl
+
+@[simp] theorem config_workTapeSymbols (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) (i : Fin k) :
+    (config cfg).tapes.workTapeSymbols i.castSucc = cfg.tapes.workTapeSymbols i :=
+  MultiTapeTM.outCfg_workTapeSymbols_castSucc cfg.tapes i
+
+@[simp] theorem config_channels (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) :
+    (config cfg).channels = cfg.channels := rfl
+
+@[simp] theorem config_answerSymbols (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) :
+    (config cfg).answerSymbols = cfg.answerSymbols := rfl
+
+/-- A source output write appends exactly one cell at the buffer's write frontier. -/
+theorem step_config (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) (a : Turing.Action k Symbol State)
+    (symbol : Oracle → Option Symbol) (move : Oracle → SignType) :
+    (config cfg).step (action a) symbol move = config (cfg.step a symbol move) := by
+  refine Config.ext ?_ rfl
+  refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ ?_ rfl <;> funext i <;> induction i using Fin.lastCases with
+  | cast i => simp [config, action, Config.step, Turing.Action.apply, MultiTapeTM.outCfg]
+  | last =>
+    cases h : a.output <;>
+      simp [config, action, Config.step, Turing.Action.apply, MultiTapeTM.outCfg, h,
+        tapeOfList_append_single, SignType.cast]
+
+theorem receive_config [DecidableEq Oracle] (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input)
+    (oracle : Oracle) (next : State) (answer : List Symbol) :
+    (config cfg).receive oracle next answer = config (cfg.receive oracle next answer) := rfl
+
+end OutputToTape
+
+/-- Buffer output on a fresh work tape, retaining the source's oracle interactions. -/
+@[simps! initial] def outputToTape [Functor Choose]
+    (machine : MultiTapeMachine k Symbol State Oracle Choose) :
+    MultiTapeMachine (k + 1) Symbol State Oracle Choose where
+  initial := machine.initial
+  tr state symbol work answer :=
+    OutputToTape.instruction <$> machine.tr state symbol (fun i => work i.castSucc) answer
+
+/-- Unfold a single redirected transition without unfolding its machine in continuations. -/
+theorem outputToTape_tr [Functor Choose] (machine : MultiTapeMachine k Symbol State Oracle Choose)
+    (state : State) (symbol : Option Symbol) (work : Fin (k + 1) → Option Symbol)
+    (answer : Oracle → Option Symbol) :
+    machine.outputToTape.tr state symbol work answer =
+      OutputToTape.instruction <$> machine.tr state symbol (fun i => work i.castSucc) answer := rfl
+
+variable [Functor Choose] [DecidableEq Oracle]
+  (machine : MultiTapeMachine k Symbol State Oracle Choose)
+  (choose : {α : Type} → Choose α → OracleComp spec α)
+  (hchoose : ∀ {α β : Type} (f : α → β) (choices : Choose α),
+    choose (f <$> choices) = f <$> choose choices)
+  (query : Oracle → List Symbol → OracleComp spec (List Symbol))
+
+include hchoose
+
+/-- Output buffering preserves the complete program, including the source's communication state. -/
+theorem runConfigFrom_outputToTape (fuel : ℕ) (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) :
+    machine.outputToTape.runConfigFrom choose query fuel (OutputToTape.config cfg) =
+      OutputToTape.config <$> machine.runConfigFrom choose query fuel cfg := by
+  apply runConfigFrom_map machine machine.outputToTape choose choose query query OutputToTape.config
+  intro cfg
+  cases hs : cfg.tapes.state with
+  | none => simp [runConfigFrom, hs]
+  | some state =>
+    simp only [runConfigFrom, OutputToTape.config_state, hs, OutputToTape.config_inputSymbol,
+      OutputToTape.config_workTapeSymbols, OutputToTape.config_answerSymbols, outputToTape_tr,
+      hchoose, bind_map_left, map_bind]
+    congr 1
+    funext a
+    cases a <;> simp [OutputToTape.instruction, OutputToTape.step_config,
+      OutputToTape.receive_config]
+
+omit hchoose [DecidableEq Oracle] in
+/-- Output buffering starts with a blank work tape, without a precomputed output word. -/
+theorem initialConfig_outputToTape (input : List Symbol) :
+    machine.outputToTape.initialConfig input =
+      OutputToTape.config (machine.initialConfig input) := by
+  refine Config.ext ?_ rfl
+  refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ ?_ rfl <;> funext i <;> induction i using Fin.lastCases <;>
+    simp [initialConfig, OutputToTape.config, MultiTapeTM.outCfg, Cfg.init]
+
+omit hchoose in
+/-- Effect-free deterministic output redirection is exactly upstream's compiler. -/
+theorem toTM_outputToTape (machine : MultiTapeMachine k Symbol State Empty Id) :
+    machine.outputToTape.toTM = machine.toTM.outputToTape := by
+  simp only [toTM, MultiTapeTM.outputToTape, MultiTapeTM.tr_ofTr, outputToTape]
+  congr 1
+  funext state symbol work
+  cases machine.tr state symbol (fun i => work i.castSucc) Empty.elim with
+  | step a symbol move => rfl
+  | query oracle next => exact oracle.elim
+
+end Turing.MultiTapeMachine

+/-- A one-instruction program simulation preserves every clocked run. The hypothesis includes
+halted configurations, and the embedding may change the tape alphabet and input word. -/
+theorem runConfigFrom_map
+    (embed : Config k Symbol State Oracle input → Config k' Symbol' State' Oracle' input')
+    (hstep : ∀ cfg, target.runConfigFrom choose' query' 1 (embed cfg) =
+      embed <$> source.runConfigFrom choose query 1 cfg)
+    (fuel : ℕ) (cfg : Config k Symbol State Oracle input) :
+    target.runConfigFrom choose' query' fuel (embed cfg) =
+      embed <$> source.runConfigFrom choose query fuel cfg := by
+  induction fuel generalizing cfg with
+  | zero => simp
+  | succ fuel ih =>
+    rw [show fuel + 1 = 1 + fuel by lia, target.runConfigFrom_add, source.runConfigFrom_add,
+      hstep, bind_map_left, map_bind]
+    congr 1
+    funext next
+    exact ih next
+

 All private interpreter state is retained, including state shared by coin and oracle programs. -/

+/-- Placing a configuration before a block of extra tapes gives an appended family. -/
+theorem embed_castAdd (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input)
+    (tapes : Fin (k + k') → ℤ → Option Symbol) (heads : Fin (k + k') → ℤ) :
+    embed (Fin.castAddEmb k') cfg tapes heads =
+      ⟨cfg.state, cfg.inputPos, Fin.append cfg.workTapes (fun i => tapes (Fin.natAdd k i)),
+        Fin.append cfg.workTapePos (fun i => heads (Fin.natAdd k i)), cfg.output⟩ := by
+  refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ ?_ rfl <;> funext i <;> induction i using Fin.addCases with
+  | left i =>
+    have h : partialInv (Fin.castAddEmb k') (i.castAdd k') = some i :=
+      partialInv_embed (Fin.castAddEmb k') i
+    simp [embed, h]
+  | right i =>
+    have h : Fin.natAdd k i ∉ Set.range (Fin.castAddEmb k') := by
+      rintro ⟨j, hj⟩
+      exact Fin.castAdd_ne_natAdd j i hj
+    simp [embed, partialInv_eq_none _ h]
+
+/-- Placing a configuration after a block of extra tapes gives an appended family. -/
+theorem embed_natAdd (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input)
+    (tapes : Fin (k' + k) → ℤ → Option Symbol) (heads : Fin (k' + k) → ℤ) :
+    embed (Fin.natAddEmb k') cfg tapes heads =
+      ⟨cfg.state, cfg.inputPos, Fin.append (fun i => tapes (i.castAdd k)) cfg.workTapes,
+        Fin.append (fun i => heads (i.castAdd k)) cfg.workTapePos, cfg.output⟩ := by
+  refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ ?_ rfl <;> funext i <;> induction i using Fin.addCases with
+  | left i =>
+    have h : i.castAdd k ∉ Set.range (Fin.natAddEmb k') := by
+      rintro ⟨j, hj⟩
+      exact Fin.castAdd_ne_natAdd i j hj.symm
+    simp [embed, partialInv_eq_none _ h]
+  | right i =>
+    have h : partialInv (Fin.natAddEmb k') (Fin.natAdd k' i) = some i :=
+      partialInv_embed (Fin.natAddEmb k') i
+    simp [embed, h]
+
+/-- Reserving one last tape is the corresponding `Fin.lastCases` family. -/
+theorem embed_castSucc (cfg : Cfg k Symbol State input)
+    (tapes : Fin (k + 1) → ℤ → Option Symbol) (heads : Fin (k + 1) → ℤ) :
+    embed Fin.castSuccEmb cfg tapes heads =
+      ⟨cfg.state, cfg.inputPos, Fin.lastCases (tapes (Fin.last k)) cfg.workTapes,
+        Fin.lastCases (heads (Fin.last k)) cfg.workTapePos, cfg.output⟩ := by
+  change embed (Fin.castAddEmb 1) cfg tapes heads = _
+  rw [embed_castAdd]
+  refine Cfg.ext rfl rfl ?_ ?_ rfl <;> funext i <;> induction i using Fin.lastCases <;>
+    simp [Fin.append, Fin.addCases]
+
 end Turing.MultiTapeTM

+/-!
+# Preparing a buffered word for use as input
+
+A completed output buffer has its head just past the word. `prepareInput` marks the cell left of
+the flag head and rewinds the word, using the existing `markWork` and `rewindWork` machines.
+Every other tape and head, the real input head, and the output are preserved.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.prepareInput`: prepare the last two work tapes as a virtual input.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_prepareInput`: the handoff costs `word.length + 4` transitions,
+  including when the word is empty.
+
+## References
+
+Adapted from `MultiTape/Plumbing/PrepareInput.lean` on the cslib `crypto` branch at
+`5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`, reusing Christian Reitwiessner's tape routines.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapeTM
+
+variable {k : ℕ} {Symbol State : Type*} {input : List Symbol}
+
+/-- Mark the left boundary and rewind the buffered word on the last two work tapes. -/
+noncomputable def prepareInput (k : ℕ) (mark : Symbol) :
+    MultiTapeTM (k + 2) Symbol (MarkWorkState ⊕ RewindWorkState) :=
+  ((markWork Symbol (some mark)).extendTapes (tapeEmb (Fin.natAdd k 1))).seq
+    ((rewindWork Symbol).extendTapes (tapeEmb (Fin.natAdd k 0)))
+
+/-- Preparation rewinds the buffered word and marks its left boundary, preserving all other data.
+The flag head must start at zero; the caller ensures its tape is otherwise blank. -/
+theorem runFrom_prepareInput (mark : Symbol) (cfg : Cfg (k + 2) Symbol State input)
+    (word : List Symbol) (hword : cfg.workTapes (Fin.natAdd k 0) = tapeOfList word)
+    (hhead : cfg.workTapePos (Fin.natAdd k 0) = word.length)
+    (hflag : cfg.workTapePos (Fin.natAdd k 1) = 0) :
+    (prepareInput k mark).runFrom (cfg.withState (some (prepareInput k mark).q₀))
+        (word.length + 4) =
+      { cfg.withState (none : Option (MarkWorkState ⊕ RewindWorkState)) with
+        workTapes := Function.update cfg.workTapes (Fin.natAdd k 1)
+          (Function.update (cfg.workTapes (Fin.natAdd k 1)) (-1) (some mark))
+        workTapePos := Function.update cfg.workTapePos (Fin.natAdd k 0) 0 } := by
+  let marker := (markWork Symbol (some mark)).extendTapes (tapeEmb (Fin.natAdd k (1 : Fin 2)))
+  let rewind := (rewindWork Symbol).extendTapes (tapeEmb (Fin.natAdd k (0 : Fin 2)))
+  let mid : Cfg (k + 2) Symbol MarkWorkState input :=
+    { cfg.withState none with
+      workTapes := Function.update cfg.workTapes (Fin.natAdd k 1)
+        (Function.update (cfg.workTapes (Fin.natAdd k 1)) (-1) (some mark)) }
+  have hmark : marker.runFrom (cfg.withState (some marker.q₀)) 2 = mid := by
+    simp only [marker, runFrom_tapeEmb, oneTapeCfg, Cfg.withState, extendTapes_q₀,
+      runFrom_markWork, embed_tapeEmb]
+    simp [mid, Cfg.withState, hflag]
+  have hrewind : rewind.runFrom (mid.withState (some rewind.q₀)) (word.length + 2) =
+      { mid.withState (none : Option RewindWorkState) with
+        workTapePos := Function.update cfg.workTapePos (Fin.natAdd k 0) 0 } := by
+    simp only [rewind, runFrom_tapeEmb, oneTapeCfg, Cfg.withState, extendTapes_q₀]
+    have hmid : mid.workTapes (Fin.natAdd k 0) = cfg.workTapes (Fin.natAdd k 0) := by
+      simp [mid]
+    rw [hmid, show mid.workTapePos (Fin.natAdd k 0) = word.length from hhead,
+      runFrom_rewindWork_none _ _ _ hword le_rfl, embed_tapeEmb]
+    simp [mid, Cfg.withState]
+  have hseq := runFrom_seq hmark rfl hrewind rfl
+  simp only [prepareInput, marker, rewind, mid, Sequential.leftCfg, Sequential.rightCfg,
+    Cfg.withState, Cfg.mapState, Option.map_none,
+    show 2 + (word.length + 2) = word.length + 4 by lia] at hseq ⊢
+  exact hseq
+
+end Turing.MultiTapeTM

+/-!
+# Configuration laws for closed fair-coin programs
+
+Closed machines have no oracle channels and draw fresh fair bits through `ProbComp.uniform Bool`.
+These specializations of the common machine laws let probabilistic realizations work directly
+with configuration distributions. Actual halting is required when padding or sequencing clocks.
+
+## Main definitions
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.runClosedConfigFrom`: retain the configuration of a closed fair-coin run.
+
+## Main results
+
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.eval_runClosedConfigFrom_seq`: add two halting bounds.
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.eval_runClosedConfigFrom_add_of_halted`: padding preserves halted runs.
+* `Turing.MultiTapePTM.eval_runClosedConfigFrom_ofDeterministic`: deterministic run distributions.
+
+## References
+
+Specializations of the common halting, sequencing and deterministic embedding rules, adapted
+from the cslib `crypto` branch at `5ff69ca93402e7c947208dc56396d6d86203ccd8`.
+-/
+
+@[expose] public section
+
+namespace Turing.MultiTapePTM
+
+open Cslib MultiTapeMachine MultiTapeMachine.Sequential
+
+variable {k : ℕ} {Symbol State State₀ State₁ : Type} {input : List Symbol}
+
+/-- Retain the complete configuration of a closed run with fresh fair coins. -/
+noncomputable def runClosedConfigFrom (machine : MultiTapePTM k Symbol State) (fuel : ℕ)
+    (cfg : Config k Symbol State Empty input) : ProbComp (Config k Symbol State Empty input) :=
+  machine.runConfigFrom (ProbComp.uniform Bool) Empty.elim fuel cfg
+
+/-- The closed output is the projection of the final configuration program. -/
+theorem runClosed_eq_map (machine : MultiTapePTM k Symbol State) (fuel : ℕ)
+    (input : List Symbol) :
+    machine.runClosed fuel input =
+      (fun final => final.tapes.output) <$>
+        machine.runClosedConfigFrom fuel (machine.initialConfig input) := rfl
+
+/-- Padding a halting run preserves the complete configuration distribution. -/
+theorem eval_runClosedConfigFrom_add_of_halted (machine : MultiTapePTM k Symbol State)
+    (cfg : Config k Symbol State Empty input) (fuel padding : ℕ)
+    (hhalt : ∀ final ∈ (ProbComp.eval (machine.runClosedConfigFrom fuel cfg)).support,
+      final.tapes.state = none) :
+    ProbComp.eval (machine.runClosedConfigFrom (fuel + padding) cfg) =
+      ProbComp.eval (machine.runClosedConfigFrom fuel cfg) := by
+  conv_rhs => rw [← PMF.bind_pure
+    (ProbComp.eval (machine.runClosedConfigFrom fuel cfg))]
+  unfold runClosedConfigFrom runConfigFrom
+  rw [MultiTapeMachine.runConfigFrom_add, ProbComp.eval_bind]
+  apply Probability.PMF.bind_congr_on_support
+  intro final hfinal
+  rw [MultiTapeMachine.runConfigFrom_halted _ _ _ _ _ (hhalt final hfinal)]
+  rfl
+
+/-- Any larger clock gives the same configuration distribution after a halting bound. -/
+theorem eval_runClosedConfigFrom_eq_of_halted (machine : MultiTapePTM k Symbol State)
+    (cfg : Config k Symbol State Empty input) {fuel larger : ℕ} (hle : fuel ≤ larger)
+    (hhalt : ∀ final ∈ (ProbComp.eval (machine.runClosedConfigFrom fuel cfg)).support,
+      final.tapes.state = none) :
+    ProbComp.eval (machine.runClosedConfigFrom larger cfg) =
+      ProbComp.eval (machine.runClosedConfigFrom fuel cfg) := by
+  simpa only [Nat.add_sub_of_le hle] using
+    eval_runClosedConfigFrom_add_of_halted machine cfg fuel (larger - fuel) hhalt
+
+/-- Padding a halting bound preserves the closed output distribution. -/
+theorem eval_runClosed_eq_of_halted (machine : MultiTapePTM k Symbol State) (input : List Symbol)
+    {fuel larger : ℕ} (hle : fuel ≤ larger)
+    (hhalt : ∀ final ∈ (ProbComp.eval
+      (machine.runClosedConfigFrom fuel (machine.initialConfig input))).support,
+      final.tapes.state = none) :
+    ProbComp.eval (machine.runClosed larger input) =
+      ProbComp.eval (machine.runClosed fuel input) := by
+  simp only [runClosed_eq_map, ProbComp.eval_map,
+    eval_runClosedConfigFrom_eq_of_halted machine _ hle hhalt]
+
+/-- Shared-tape sequencing preserves distributions once both phases have actually halted. -/
+theorem eval_runClosedConfigFrom_seq (first : MultiTapePTM k Symbol State₀)
+    (second : MultiTapePTM k Symbol State₁) (cfg : Config k Symbol State₀ Empty input)
+    (firstTime secondTime : ℕ)
+    (hfirst : ∀ result ∈ (ProbComp.eval (first.runClosedConfigFrom firstTime cfg)).support,
+      result.tapes.state = none)
+    (hsecond : ∀ result ∈ (ProbComp.eval (first.runClosedConfigFrom firstTime cfg)).support,
+      ∀ final ∈ (ProbComp.eval
+        (second.runClosedConfigFrom secondTime (start second result))).support,
+        final.tapes.state = none) :
+    ProbComp.eval ((first.seq second).runClosedConfigFrom
+      (firstTime + secondTime) (left second cfg)) =
+      (ProbComp.eval (first.runClosedConfigFrom firstTime cfg)).bind
+        (fun result => (ProbComp.eval
+          (second.runClosedConfigFrom secondTime (start second result))).map right) := by
+  have h := run_interpret_runConfigFrom_seq first second (ProbComp.uniform Bool) Empty.elim
+    (fun q (s : Unit) => (fun a => (a, s)) <$> ProbComp.unifOracle q)
+    cfg firstTime secondTime () (by
+      intro result hresult
+      rw [OracleComp.run_interpret_stateless, PMF.monad_map_eq_map] at hresult
+      obtain ⟨final, hfinal, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp hresult
+      exact hfirst final hfinal) (by
+      intro result hresult final hfinal
+      rw [OracleComp.run_interpret_stateless, PMF.monad_map_eq_map] at hresult hfinal
+      obtain ⟨source, hsource, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp hresult
+      obtain ⟨target, htarget, rfl⟩ := (PMF.mem_support_map_iff _ _ _).mp hfinal
+      exact hsecond source hsource target htarget)
+  simp only [OracleComp.run_interpret_stateless] at h
+  have hout := congrArg (PMF.map Prod.fst) h
+  simp only [PMF.monad_map_eq_map, PMF.map_bind,
+    PMF.bind_map, PMF.map_comp, Function.comp_def] at hout
+  change PMF.map id _ = _ at hout
+  rw [PMF.map_id] at hout
+  exact hout
+
+/-- A deterministic embedding has a point-mass configuration distribution. -/
+theorem eval_runClosedConfigFrom_ofDeterministic (machine : MultiTapeTM k Symbol State)
+    (fuel : ℕ) (cfg : Config k Symbol State Empty input) :
+    ProbComp.eval ((ofDeterministic machine).runClosedConfigFrom fuel cfg) =
+      PMF.pure { cfg with tapes := machine.runFrom cfg.tapes fuel } := by
+  have h := run_interpret_runConfigFrom_ofDeterministic machine (ProbComp.uniform Bool) Empty.elim
+    (fun q (s : Unit) => (fun a => (a, s)) <$> ProbComp.unifOracle q)
+    (Probability.PMF.uniformOfFintype Bool)
+    (fun s => by
+      rw [OracleComp.run_interpret_stateless]
+      exact congrArg (PMF.map (fun bit => (bit, s))) (ProbComp.eval_uniform Bool)) fuel cfg ()
+  rw [OracleComp.run_interpret_stateless] at h
+  have hout := congrArg (PMF.map Prod.fst) h
+  simp only [PMF.monad_map_eq_map, PMF.map_comp,
+    PMF.pure_map] at hout
+  change PMF.map id _ = _ at hout
+  rw [PMF.map_id] at hout
+  exact hout
+
+end Turing.MultiTapePTM
